HAIER PLUMBING REQUESTED A JULIE ONE-CALL JOINT MEET TICKET COVERING A LARGE SEWER AND WATERLINE PROJECT IN THE HILLSBORO AREA.  DURING THE JOINT MEET, HAIER PLUMBING EXPLAINED TO LOCATORS IN ATTENDANCE WHAT THE PROJECT ENTAILED AND SHOWED THEM A MAP OF THE AREAS THAT NEEDED TO BE LOCATED FOR THE START OF THE PROJECT.  WHEN HAIER NEEDED ADDITIONAL AREAS LOCATED, THEY STATED THEY WOULD CONTACT THE LOCATORS AND EXPLAIN WHAT AREAS SHOULD BE LOCATED NEXT.    ON 6/14/2010 HAIER CONTACTED THE CONSOLIDATED UTILITY SERVICE (CUS) LOCATOR WORKING FOR AMEREN AND REQUESTED AN AREA OF RAILROAD STREET SOUTH OF IL RTE. 16 (SCHOOL STREET) TO BE LOCATED FOR A BORE ACROSS SCHOOL ST.  WHEN THE CUS LOCATOR FOR AMEREN SHOWED UP TO THE LOCATION SPECIFIED, HE LOCATED THE 8" STEEL HIGH PRESSURE GAS MAIN AND BOTH HE AND THE EXCAVATOR FOR HAIER WALKED AROUND 1624 SCHOOL ST. TOGETHER LOOKING FOR A POSSIBLE GAS METER.  NEITHER THE LOCATOR NOR HAIER NOTICED THE GAS METER OR FARM TAP FOR 1624 SCHOOL ST.  ON 6/18/2010, HAIER WAS EXCAVATING IN RAILROAD STREET AND STRUCK THE UNMARKED 3/4" STEEL GAS SERVICE BETWEEN THE 8" HIGH PRESSURE STEEL MAIN ON THE EAST SIDE OF RAILROAD STREET AND THE FARM TAP SERVING 1624 SCHOOL ST.  THE FARM TAP WAS OBSCURED BY VEGETATION AND LANDSCAPING TO THE EXTENT THAT HAIER CREW MEMBERS WERE STANDING NEXT TO IT WHEN THE DAMAGE OCCURRED AND DID NOT REALIZE IT WAS THERE UNTIL THEY HEARD THE GAS BLOWING FROM THE DAMAGE NEAR THE TAP.    AMEREN RECEIVED A CALL FROM THE EXCAVATOR AT 0843 ON 6/18/2010 AND AN AMEREN FIRST RESPONDER WAS ON SITE AT 0850.  EMERGENCY RESPONDERS INSURED THE AREA WAS SAFE INCLUDING THE STRUCTURE AT 1624 SCHOOL ST.  IL RTE. 16 WAS SHUT DOWN AT 0925 AND ORDER WAS MADE TO CUT THE ELECTRIC SERVICE TO 1624 SCHOOL ST. DUE TO GAS IN AIR DUE TO EXCESSIVE WINDS.  NO GAS WAS EVER DETECTED INSIDE THE STRUCTURE AT 1624 SCHOOL ST.  CREWS WERE MOBILIZED TO SHUT OFF THE FLOW OF GAS AND REPAIR THE DAMAGED FACILITIES.  SINCE THE SERVICE WAS HIT BETWEEN THE MAIN AND THE FARM TAP, THE 8" MAIN HAD TO BE EXCAVATED IN TWO LOCATIONS AT A SAFE DISTANCE FROM THE HIT WHERE TWO 8" LINE STOPPERS AND A BYPASS COULD BE WELDED ON THE MAIN ALLOWING STOPPERS TO BE SET TO STOP OFF THE FLOW OF GAS TO THE DAMAGED GAS FACILITIES.  AT 1600, IL RTE. 16 WAS RE-OPENED.  DUE TO THE EXTENT OF LARGE DIAMETER STEEL WORK THAT HAD TO BE COMPLETED COUPLED WITH A SEVERE ROUND OF THUNDERSTORMS THAT EVENING, GAS WAS SHUT DOWN AT 1016 ON 6/19/2010.  THE SERVICE HAD BEEN SEVERED BY THE EXCAVATOR NEAR A 3/4" WELD ELBOW.  CREWS MADE REPAIRS TO THE STEEL SERVICE LINE AND GAS WAS RESTORED TO THE CUSTOMER AT 1624 SCHOOL ST. AT 1630 ON 6/19/2010.

WASHINGTON GAS RESPONDED TO THE SCENE OF A HOUSE FIRE AT 8738 OXWELL LANE IN LAUREL, MD ON 4/29/10 AT THE REQUEST OF THE PRINCE GEORGE'S FIRE BOARD. UPON ARRIVAL, THE METER VALVE WAS FOUND TO HAVE BEEN TURNED OFF BY THE FIRE DEPARTMENT.  THE METER  BUILD-UP WAS CONSUMED BY THE FIRE. THE RISER WAS CAPPED OFF. A GAS MIGRATION SURVEY WAS CONDUCTED AROUND THE PERIMETER OF THE HOUSE AND OVER THE SERVICE LINE TO THE MAIN. NO INDICATIONS WERE FOUND.  ON 4/30/10, WASHINGTON GAS RETURNED TO THE SITE TO EXCAVATE THE SERVICE LINE IN THE YARD, CAP IT OFF, AND PERFORM A PRESSURE TEST ON IT. APPROXIMATELY 40 FEET OF SERVICE LINE WAS TESTED WITH NO LEAKS FOUND. THIS PORTION OF THE SERVICE LINE WAS ABANDONED IN PLACE AFTER THE PRESSURE TEST. WASHINGTON GAS BELIEVES THE FIRE STARTED ELSEWHERE IN THE HOUSE AND CONSEQUENTLY CONSUMED ITS FACILITIES.

RLA INVESTMENTS, INC. IS PERFORMING MAINTENANCE ACTIVITIES IN VARIOUS LOCATIONS OF DUKE ENERGY OHIO'S SERVICE TERRITORY PURSUANT TO A CONTRACT WITH DUKE ENERGY OHIO. THE MAINTENANCE ACTIVITIES INVOLVE THE REPLACEMENT OF NATURAL GAS SERVICE RISERS IN CONNECTION WITH DUKE ENERGY OHIO'S RISER REPLACEMENT PROGRAM.     ON MONDAY, APRIL 5, 2010, AT APPROXIMATELY 4:08PM, CODY FAUL, AN EMPLOYEE OF RLA INVESTMENTS,   WAS PERFORMING MAINTENANCE ACTIVITIES AT 4044 ASHWOOD CT., WITHAMSVILLE, OH IN CLERMONT COUNTY.  MR. FAUL, A MEMBER OF A TWO-MAN RISER CREW, WAS WORKING ALONE AT THE TIME OF THE ACCIDENT.  IT IS BELIEVED THAT MR. FAUL WAS PERFORMING A FULL GAS SERVICE RISER REPLACEMENT BY CONNECTING THE EXISTING GAS SERVICE PIPE TO THE NEW RISER USING A STAB CONNECTION FITTING PRIOR TO BEING DISCOVERED UNRESPONSIVE.  MR. FAUL WAS TRANSPORTED TO A LOCAL HOSPITAL AND PRONOUNCED DEAD ON ARRIVAL.  THIS INCIDENT IS CURRENTLY UNDER INVESTIGATION.    NOTE: IT IS OUR UNDERSTANDING THAT ONLY A DRUG TEST WAS ADMINISTERED ON THE CREW LEADER (DAVID SMITH), NOT AN ALCOHOL TEST.    AS OF 6-2-10, INCIDENT IS STILL UNDER INVESTIGATION, WAITING ON ACTUAL CAUSE OF DEATH REPORT FROM CORONER AND TOXICOLOGY REPORT.    AS OF 6-30-10, THE DEATH OF CODY FAUL WAS RULED ACCIDENTAL AND THAT THE CAUSE OF DEATH WAS ASPHYXIATION (DUE TO METHANE GAS EXPOSURE).              ALSO, ACCORDING TO THE TOXICOLOGY REPORT, NO DRUGS WERE FOUND IN HIS SYSTEM.

MR. PHILLIP VALDEZ, GAS, WATER, AND SEWER SUPERINTENDENT WAS NOTIFIED BY TELEPHONE AT 15:38 THAT THERE WAS A FIRE AT THE QUEMAZON SUBDIVISION MONTESSORI SCHOOL LOCATED AT 4600 ESPERANZA ST. IN LOS ALAMOS NEW MEXICO. AFTER ARRIVING ON THE SCENE AT 4600 ESPERANZA ST. MR. VALDEZ FOUND THAT A VEHICLE HAD LEFT THE ROADWAY, STRUCK A GAS METER AND BROKE OFF THE RISER, AND CONTINUED INTO THE SIDE OF THE BUILDING. THE BUILDING AND THE VEHICLE WERE ON FIRE. THE DRIVER OF THE VEHICLE AND ITS OTHER OCCUPANTS AND THE OCCUPANTS OF THE BUILDING WERE EVACUATED WITH NO INJURIES BEING REPORTED. THE LOS ALAMOS COUNTY FIRE DEPARTMENT RESPONDED TO THE FIRE AND AND PUT OUT THE BLAZING VEHICLE AND BUILDING BUT FLAMES CONTINUED TO COME FROM THE RISER WHICH HAD THE VEHICLE ATOP OF IT. THE FIRE DEPARTMENT CALLED IN A TOW TRUCK WHICH REMOVED THE VEHICLE FROM THE BUILDING AND FROM ATOP OF THE RISER, AT WHICH TIME THEY EXTINGUISHED THE FLAMES COMING FROM THE RISER. A LOS ALAMOS COUNTY GAS TECHNICIAN PLACED A CLIMAX PLUG INTO THE RISER AND SHUT OF THE FLOW OF GAS. THE AREA WAS BAR TESTED WITH A CGI TESTER AND A FLAME IONIZATION UNIT TO TEST FOR ANY POSSIBLE GAS LEAKAGE. NO LEAKS WERE DETECTED AND THE SERVICE LINE WAS THEN SQUEEZED OFF AND CAPPED TEN (10) FEET FROM THE RISER. GAS TECHNICIANS CHECKED THE AREA THE FOLLOWING DAY FOR LEAKS AND NONE WERE DETECTED.

CONTRACTOR FOR THE COMPANY WAS PERFORMING DIRECTIONAL BORING WORK ASSOCIATED WITH A SERVICE RENEWAL. THE EXISTING SERVICE WAS CONTACTED BY THE BORE HEAD CAUSING A MALLEABLE ELBOW TO BREAK. GAS MIGRATED INTO AN UNDERGROUND CELLAR RESULTING IN AN EXPLOSION AND FIRE.

A FIRE AT AN UNOCCUPIED HOME OCCURRED AT APPROXIMATELY 2335 HOURS ON 2/13/10.   THE FIRE DEPARTMENT CALLED AT PG&E AT APPROXIMATELY 0005 HOURS. THE PG&E GAS SERVICE REPRESENTATIVE (GSR) ARRIVED AT 0020 HOURS.  THE FIRE DEPARTMENT AND GSR WERE UNABLE TO SHUT OFF THE SERVICE VALVE AT THE METER DUE TO DAMAGE TO THE VALVE BY THE FIRE.  A GAS CREW WAS CALLED AND THEY CUT OFF THE GAS SERVICE AT THE MAIN AT APPROXIMATELY 02:30.  ACCORDING TO THE FIRE DEPARTMENT THE THE FIRE APPEARS TO HAVE STARTED IN ONE OF THE CLOSETS IN THE HOME.  THE HOUSE FIRE DAMAGED THE GAS METER WHICH RELEASED NATURAL GAS RESULTING IN A SECONDARY IGNITION.  THE FIRE DAMAGE TO THE HOME RESULTED IN PROPERTY DAMAGES EXCEEDING $50,000.  THERE WERE NO INJURIES AND NO FATALITIES.  NO MAJOR MEDIA WAS PRESENT.

ATMOS ENERGY DISCOVERED A LEAKING COMPRESSION COUPLING IN THE AREA WHERE THIS FIRE OCCURRED.  THE LEAKING COMPONENT WAS PRESERVED IN ITS NATIVE STATE AND SENT TO A LABORATORY FOR TESTING TO DETERMINE THE CAUSE OF FAILURE.  A FLOW RATE TEST WAS PERFORMED AND THE TEST REVEALED THAT THE LEAK RATE FROM THE LEAKING COMPONENT WAS NOT LARGE ENOUGH TO CAUSE AN ACCUMULATION OF A FLAMMABLE MIXTURE TO HAVE CONTRIBUTED TO THIS HOUSE FIRE.  ATMOS ENERGY'S EXHAUSTIVE INVESTIGATION DID NOT IDENTIFY ANY OTHER SOURCES THAT COULD HAVE CONTRIBUTED TO THIS EVENT, THEREFORE THE CAUSE OF THIS FIRE IS UNDETERMINED.

ON MONDAY, JANUARY 25, 2010 AT APPROXIMATELY 2:30PM A SINGLE-FAMILY HOME AT 2022 WEST 63RD STREET, CLEVELAND, OH (CUYAHOGA COUNTY) WAS INVOLVED IN AN EXPLOSION/FIRE. THE GAS SERVICE LINE WAS SHUT-OFF AT APPROXIMATELY 4:30PM. A LEAK SURVEY OF THE MAIN LINES AND SERVICE LINES ON W. 83RD BETWEEN MADISON AND LORAIN REVEALED NO INDICATIONS OF GAS NEAR THE STRUCTURE. A SERVICE LEAK AT 2131 WEST 83RD STREET WAS DETECTED DURING THE LEAK SURVEY. THIS SERVICE LINE WAS REPLACED UPON DISCOVERY.     ON TUESDAY, JANUARY 26TH, 2010 THE SERVICE LINE AT 2022 W. 83RD WAS AIR TESTED AT OPERATING PRESSURE WITH NO PRESSURE LOSS. AN ODOR TEST WAS CONDUCTED AT 2028 WAST 83RD STREET. THE RESULTS OF THIS ODOR TEST REVEALED ODOR LEVELS WELL WITHIN DOT COMPLIANCE LEVELS. OUR INVESTIGATION REVEALED AN ODOR COMPLAINT AT THIS RESIDENCE ON JANUARY 18TH. DOMINION PERSONNEL RESPONDED TO THE CALL AND MET WITH THE CLEVELAND FIRE DEPARTMENT. DOMINION FOUND THE METER DISCONNECTED AND THE METER SHUT-OFF VALVE IN THE HALF OPEN POSITION. THE SHUT-OFF VALVE WAS CLOSED BY THE DOMINION TECHNICIAN AND SECURED WITH A LOCKING DEVICE. THE TECHNICIAN PLACED A 3/4 INCH PLUG IN THE OPEN END OF THE VALVE. THE TECHNICIAN ALSO ATTEMPTED TO CLOSE THE CURB-SLOP VALVE, BUT COULD NOT. THE SERVICE LINE WAS THEN BAR HOLE TESTED UTILIZING A COMBUSTIBLE GAS INDICATOR FROM THE STREET TO THE STRUCTURE.  AS A RESULT.  NO LEAKAGE WAS DISCOVERED. A SECOND ATTEMPT TO CTOSE THE CURB BOX  VALVE ON JANUARY 19TH ENDED WHEN BLOCKAGE WAS DISCOVERED IN THE VALVE BOX. THE VALVE BOX WAS IN THE PROCESS OF BEING SCHEDULED FOR EXCEVATLON AND SHUT OFF BY A CONSTRUCTION CREW AT THE TIME OF THE INCIDENT.  AN INVESTIGATION OF THE INCIDENT SITE DETERMINED THE CAUSE TO BE ARSON AS APPROXIMATELY 6 INCHES OF SERVICE LINE AND THE METER SHUT-OFF VALVE (WITH LOCKING DEVICE STILL INTACT), DETACHED FROM THE SERVICE LINE, WERE RECOVERED INSIDE THE STRUCTURE.

ON JUNE 20, 2026, DURING A LINE SERVICE SWAP INITIATED BY GAS CONTROL, MAINLINE VALVE (MLV) 3-1A WAS INADVERTENTLY OPENED. AT THE TIME, MLV 3-1A WAS LOCKED AND TAGGED OUT; HOWEVER, RESIDUAL GAS REMAINED IN THE POWER GAS TUBING. THE PRESENCE OF THIS TRAPPED GAS CAUSED THE MAINLINE VALVE TO CRACK OPEN, RESULTING IN A NATURAL GAS RELEASE THROUGH THE BLOWOFF VALVE. UPON RECOGNIZING THE ISSUE, GAS CONTROL ATTEMPTED TO REVERSE THE LINE SERVICE SWAP, BUT THOSE EFFORTS WERE UNSUCCESSFUL. AS A RESULT, APPROXIMATELY 12,906 MCF OF NATURAL GAS WAS UNINTENTIONALLY RELEASED INTO THE ATMOSPHERE.
RELEASE CAUSED BY THIRD PARTY DRILLING OPERATIONS.  DRILL HEAD BORED INTO THE PIPELINE CAUSING A RELEASE OF NATURAL GAS BACK INTO THE BORE PIT. VOLUME OF 1,000 MCF OF NATURAL GAS WAS RELEASED.

PART H – NARRATIVE DESCRIPTION OF THE INCIDENT ON JUNE 14, 2026, AT 15:30 HOURS (CST), SYLVESTER SILLER, REGULATORY MANAGER FOR GOLDEN TRIANGLE STORAGE, LLC (“GTS”), WAS NOTIFIED OF AN UNINTENTIONAL AIR EMISSIONS RELEASE. FROM GTS INVESTIGATIONS, A FOUR (4)-INCH BLOWDOWN VALVE ON DEHY TRAIN B, KNOWN AS VALVE BDV5403B, WAS OFF SET AND VENTING GAS TO THE BLOWDOWN HEADER.   GTS INCIDENT RESPONSE  UPON DISCOVERY BY ONSITE GTS OPERATIONS STAFF, THE UPSTREAM MANUAL VALVE WAS IMMEDIATELY CLOSED, THE FLOW SUBSIDED, AND THE SYSTEM CAME INTO BALANCE.  INITIAL NOTIFICATIONS WERE MADE WITHIN THE HOUR OF REPORT TO THE NATIONAL RESPONSE CENTER WITH PRELIMINARY ESTIMATES OF LOST GAS.  AFTER FURTHER ASSESSMENT OF THE OPERATIONAL TRENDS, IT WAS CONFIRMED THAT A 26-HOUR PERIOD OF VENTING STARTED ON JUNE 13, 2026, FROM ONE (1) INDIVIDUAL BLOWDOWN POINT, RESULTING IN A CUMULATIVE VENTING OF 12.3 MMSCF OF NATURAL GAS TO ATMOSPHERE.    REASONS FOR REPORTING UNDER 49 CFR §191.3(1)(III), AN INCIDENT IS DEFINED AS UNINTENTIONAL ESTIMATED GAS LOSS OF THREE (3) MILLION CUBIC FEET (SCF) OR MORE. THE REPORTED EVENT CAUSED THE VENTING OF STORED NATURAL GAS FROM THE SYSTEM THROUGH AN ENGINEERED BLOWDOWN SYSTEM THROUGH A NORMAL ELEVATED POINT OF DISCHARGE.  THERE WERE NO INCREASED SAFETY RISKS OR EXPOSURE TO THE PUBLIC, NO ONSITE INJURIES, OR EQUIPMENT DAMAGE. HOWEVER, THE RELEASE OF THE GAS THROUGH THE VENT (BLOWDOWN) SYSTEM WAS STILL UNINTENTIONAL AND THEREFORE CONSIDERED A GAS LOSS MEETING THE CRITERIA ABOVE FOR REQUIRED REPORTING.  INVESTIGATION INTO THE ROOT CAUSE INVESTIGATIONS ELUCIDATED THAT THE VALVE INITIALLY FAULTED WEEKS PRIOR TO INCIDENT BUT REMAINED CLOSED UNTIL THE AFTERNOON OF JUNE 13, 2026. THERE WAS NO UNINTENTIONAL RELEASE FROM VALVE BDV5403B PRIOR TO JUNE 13, 2026, AS CONFIRMED BY OPERATIONAL TREND DATA. TROUBLESHOOTING OF THE ACTUAL VALVE AND NATURAL GAS SYSTEM REVEALED NO DAMAGE OR REQUIRED REPAIRS TO THE LINE. VALVE BDV5403B AND ITS ASSOCIATED ACTUATOR ARE PART OF THE STATIONS BLOWDOWN SYSTEM AS REQUIRED BY CFR 192.167(A)(2), WHERE A FAIL-OPEN CONFIGURATION IS THE STANDARD DESIGN CHOICE TO PROVIDE A SAFE AND ROBUST SYSTEM.    GTS CORRECTIVE ACTIONS LOGIC ON CONTROLLERS IS BEING MODIFIED TO BETTER IDENTIFY AND CAPTURE THIS TYPE OF FAILURE.  BALANCE NOTIFICATIONS WILL BE BUILT INTO THE SYSTEM FOR THE OPERATORS, ALONG WITH FURTHER TRAINING TO ENSURE UNDERSTANDING OF THE LINE PACK ADJUSTMENTS.  ADDITIONAL TOOLS ARE BEING ADDED FOR TRACKING EVENTS FOR IMBALANCE VISIBILITY, AS WELL AS ADJUSTMENTS TO SYSTEM OPERATING CONDITIONS IN ORDER TO TIGHTEN THE IDENTIFICATION AND CAPTURE OF THESE TYPES OF VENTING EVENTS GOING FORWARD.  CLOSING IN THE EVENT PHMSA REQUIRES ADDITIONAL INFORMATION TO THIS 30-DAY FOLLOW UP REPORT, PLEASE DO NOT HESITATE TO REACH OUT TO SYLVESTER SILLER AT SSILLER@CALICHESTORAGE.COM, OR AFTON STERLING, VP OF REHS, AT ASTERLING@CALICHESTORAGE.COM.

ON 4/2/26 DUE TO HEAVY RAINS AND FLOODING IN THE AREA, A LAND SLIP OCCURRED AND CAUSED A RELEASE ON A SECTION OF PIPE AT A GIRTH WELD. THE RELEASE WAS 712.2 MCF OF NATURAL GAS. THE PIPELINE WAS SHUT IN PROMPTLY AND REPAIRS WERE MADE BY CUTTING OUT AND REPLACING A 27.2' SECTION OF PIPE. LINE WAS RESTARTED ON 4/4/26 AT 11:00 AM EST.  PROBABLE CAUSE IS NATURAL FORCE DAMAGE FROM HEAVY RAINS AND FLOODING CAUSING A LAND SLIP.  THE FAILED PIPE HAS BEEN SENT FOR METALLURGICAL ANALYSIS, AND A SUPPLEMENTAL REPORT WILL BE FILED ONCE THE DATA IS RECEIVED AND ANALYZED.  ***UPDATE*** CAUSE CHANGED TO MECHANICAL FAILURE/WELD - METALLURGICAL ANALYSIS WAS PERFORMED AND DID NOT INDICATE ANY DEFECTS IN THE WELD. ROOT CAUSE ANALYSIS PERFORMED AND DETERMINED SINCE PIPE MOVED WHEN CUTTING OUT THE WELD IT INDICATED RESIDUAL STRESS FROM SUSPECTED MISALIGNMENT.  CONSTRUCTION MANUAL GUIDANCE FOR WELDING WAS POSSIBLY NOT ADHERED TO.  ORGANIZATIONAL MATURITY OVER TIME HAS CORRECTED THIS POTENTIAL WITH INSPECTIONS, CONTRACTOR VETTING AND SELECTION PROCESSES, AND DOCUMENTATION OF WELD ACTIVITIES.
cause: MATERIAL FAILURE OF PIPE OR WELD

text: AT 9:15 A.M. ON JANUARY 25, 2026, THE CANE HILL COMPRESSOR STATION EXPERIENCED A COMPLETE LOSS OF POWER, INCLUDING BOTH UTILITY POWER AND THE BACKUP GENERATOR.    THE ONSITE ET EMPLOYEE-INITIATED ACTIONS TO MITIGATE THE RISK OF THE STATION ACTIVATING THE ESD BLOWDOWN SYSTEM. AT APPROXIMATELY 9:30AM THE STATION BEGAN TO BLOW DOWN DUE TO THE LOSS OF POWER AND AIR. THE ONSITE EMPLOYEE ATTEMPTED TO CLOSE THE CANE HILL COMPRESSOR STATION SUCTION AND DISCHARGE VALVES TO STOP THE ESD BLOWDOWN; HOWEVER, THE VALVES WERE INOPERABLE DUE TO FROZEN VALVE CONDITIONS. THE ET EMPLOYEE GATHERED PORTABLE STATION HEATERS TO TRY TO THAW THE FROZEN VALVE AND CONTROLS.     AT 1:45PM ON JANUARY 25, 2026 IT WAS CONFIRMED THE INCIDENT HAD MET THE REPORTING CRITERIA. THE NRC WAS NOTIFIED ON JANUARY 25, 2026, AT 2:38PM (INCIDENT # 1453392) AND THE 48HR UPDATE WAS MADE ON JANUARY 27,2026 AT 10:08AM (INCIDENT # 1453504).       AT APPROXIMATELY 2:30 P.M., A BACKUP EMPLOYEE ARRIVED ONSITE AND WAS ABLE TO CLOSE THE SUCTION AND DISCHARGE VALVES. BECAUSE THE DISCHARGE VALVE DID NOT FULLY SEAT, IT ALLOWED GAS TO BYPASS AND CONTINUE TO ESD THE STATION. THE ET EMPLOYEES THEN SUCCESSFULLY STARTED THE BACKUP AIR COMPRESSOR, WHICH ENABLED THE ESD BLOWDOWN VALVE TO CLOSE AND ULTIMATELY STOPPED THE GAS RELEASE AT 4:22PM

ON NOVEMBER 14, 2025, PCC RECEIVED A REPORT OF A POTENTIAL LINE STRIKE AND DISPATCHED FIELD OPERATIONS. UPON ARRIVAL, OPERATIONS ENCOUNTERED EMERGENCY SERVICES BLOCKING SITE ACCESS DUE TO A RUNNING THIRD-PARTY EXCAVATOR POSING AN IGNITION RISK. OPERATIONS ISOLATED TWO LINES SEGMENTS IN THE IMMEDIATE AREA OF THE EVENT (THE 440-000 AND 441-000) AND MONITORED PRESSURES. THE 12" 440-000 LINE SHOWED INDICATIONS OF BEING IMPACTED WHILE THE 20" 441-000 LINE SHOWED NO ISSUES. THE 440-000 LINE WAS THEN ISOLATED AND DE-PRESSURED, ALLOWING EMERGENCY RESPONDERS TO ENTER AND SHUT DOWN THE EXCAVATOR. ONCE EXCAVATOR WAS IN A SAFE STATE, OPERATIONS VERIFIED DAMAGE WAS LIMITED TO THE 440-000 LINE.      A ONE-CALL TICKET WAS IN PLACE AT THE TIME OF THE EVENT, FLAGGED AS “IN CONFLICT,” NOTING SHALLOW DEPTH AND REQUIRING “WATCH AND PROTECT”. DESPITE POSITIVE RESPONSE INSTRUCTIONS FROM ONEOK, THE EXCAVATOR COMPANY FAILED TO NOTIFY ONEOK BEFORE DIGGING. THE DAMAGED 41 FEET OF PIPE WAS REPLACED, INSPECTED, X-RAYED, RECOATED, AND THE LINE BROUGHT BACK INTO SERVICE ON 11/15/2025.

THE PROGRAMMING LOGIC HAS BEEN UPDATED TO PREVENT REOCCURRENCE OF THIS ISSUE.

ON OCTOBER 22, 2025, AT 6:30 A.M. WHILE INVESTIGATING LINE SHUT-INS AND COMPRESSOR SHUTDOWNS DUE TO HIGH O2 ISSUES AN OPERATIONS (OPS) TECH OBSERVED THAT THE HEADLEE DISCHARGE LINE HAD 40 PSIG WHEN THE NORMAL OPERATING PRESSURE IS 1250 PISIG. THE EMPLOYEE NOTIFIED THE OPS SUPERVISOR WHO THEN VERIFIED THE LINE PRESSURE WITH ANOTHER OPS TECH LOCATED AT THE LUPIN STATION. AT 6:40 A.M. THE OPS TEAM BEGAN A LEAK INVESTIGATION ON THE 7406642 - LUPIN TO HEADLEE. AT 09:37 A.M. FIELD PERSONNEL PINPOINT THE LOCATION THE LEAK. THE LINE WAS SHUT IN, AND FIELD PERSONNEL BEGAN TO INVESTIGATE THE SEVERITY OF THE LEAK. AT 11:15 A.M. OPERATIONS MADE AN INITIAL DETERMINATION THAT THE LEAK MAY EXCEED THE REPORTABLE THRESHOLD AND NOTIFIED DOT COMPLIANCE. THE NRC NOTIFICATION WAS MADE AT 12:06 P.M. TXRRC NOTIFICATION WAS MADE AT 12:15 P.M. CONFIRMED DISCOVERY WAS AT 9:39 P.M. WHEN OPERATIONS DETERMINED THE VOLUME LOST TO BE 7.784 MMCF.     ON NOVEMBER 25, 2025, ACUREN INSPECTION INC. COMPLETED THE METALLURGICAL TESTING. THE TESTS CONCLUDED:    1. THE FAILURE COINCIDED WITH A REGION OF INTERNAL CORROSION PRESENT ALONG THE TOP OF THE PIPE. THE INTERNAL CORROSION OCCURRED IN A MESA-LIKE PATTERN WITH SMALL, CIRCULAR PITS.   2. THE OBSERVED INTERNAL CORROSION OCCURRED IN AN ENVIRONMENT CONTAINING CARBON DIOXIDE AND WATER, COMBINING TO FORM CARBONIC ACID RESULTING IN SIDERITE.   3. THE PIPE WAS CONSISTENT WITH NOMINAL 12-INCH OD X 0.250-INCH WT, API 5L GRADE X52 MATERIAL MANUFACTURED VIA THE HF-ERW PROCESS WITH A POST WELD HEAT TREATMENT.     ENERGY TRANSFER'S INTERNAL INVESTIGATION CONCLUDED THAT THE ROOT CAUSE OF THE INCIDENT WAS LIQUID/WATER CONTENT FROM PRODUCERS ENTERING THE PIPELINE.     PLAN TO PREVENT RECURRENCE:  IMPLEMENT A CLEANING PIG SCHEDULE TO SWEEP ANY LIQUID BUILD UP IN THE PIPELINE AND A CORROSION TREATMENT/MONITORING PROGRAM.

text: ON 9-19-2025, A THIRD-PARTY CONTRACTOR WAS TESTING A RELIEF VALVE ON A TYPE C PIPELINE AT AN ENTERPRISE COMPRESSOR STATION. DURING THE TEST, THERE WAS A FAILURE, NATURAL GAS WAS RELEASED AND SOME LIQUID PRODUCT SPRAYED OUT ACROSS HIGHWAY 285.  AT 11:59 CST, AN ENTERPRISE TECHNICIAN MADE INTERNAL NOTIFICATION AND CALLED 911 TO REPORT THE GAS RELEASE TO LOCAL EMERGENCY RESPONDERS. AT 12:12, ENTERPRISE SHUT OFF GAS FLOW TO THE PIPELINE. AT 12:40 PM, ENTERPRISE ISOLATED THE RELIEF VALVE. AT 12:45, ENTERPRISE DETERMINED THAT THIS EVENT WAS AN INCIDENT DUE TO GAS LOSS. ON 9-19-2026 AT 13:09 AND 13:10, THE TRRC AND NRC WERE NOTIFIED BY ENTERPRISE OF THE INCIDENT, RESPECTIVELY.      AT 15:50, AN ENTERPRISE CONTRACTOR STARTED THE CLEANING OF HIGHWAY 285. AT 20:30, THE CONTRACTOR COMPLETED THE CLEANUP AND HIGHWAY 285 WAS OPENED BY TXDOT IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. ON 9-19-2025 AT 20:11, THE PIPELINE WAS PLACED BACK INTO SERVICE. A DIFFERENT CONTRACTOR TESTED THE RELIEF VALVE AND FOUND IT TO OPERATE WITHIN ACCEPTABLE PARAMETERS.    THE INVESTIGATION OF THE INCIDENT DETERMINED THAT THE CONTRACTOR DID NOT HAVE A WRITTEN PROCEDURE TO TEST THE RELIEF VALVE, AND THE CONTRACTOR WAS NOT FAMILIAR WITH THE RELIEF VALVE CONFIGURATION.

SATURDAY MAY 17TH @3:16PM: PIPELINE CONTROL (PLC) RECEIVED A CALL FROM THE SOUR LAKE, TX FIRE DEPARTMENT INDICATING THEY HAD RESPONDED TO THE VENTING CALL AND WAS CURRENTLY ONSITE OUTSIDE OUR COMPRESSOR STATION AND VERIFIED IT WAS VENTING GAS.     PLC NOTIFIED THE OPERATIONS ON-CALL TECHNICIAN AT 3:18PM AND PASSED ON INFORMATION. PLC ALSO NOTIFIED THE OPERATIONS ON-CALL OPS TECH THAT THEY WOULD BEGIN DROPPING UNITS TO TRY AND ISOLATE THE ISSUE AND STOP THE VENTING.     @~3:26PM THE FIRE CHIEF INDICATED THAT THE VENTING HAD STOPPED, HE HAD NO FURTHER CONCERNS, AND LEFT THE LOCATION.    @3:41PM: THE ON-CALL ARRIVED AT THE LOCATION AND MADE HIS ROUNDS, REVIEWED THE FACILITY DATA, AND DETERMINED THAT UNIT #5 WAS THE ISSUE, SO HE MADE THE UNIT UNAVAILABLE AND LOCKED IT OUT FOR FURTHER INVESTIGATION.    MONDAY, MAY 19TH @~8:30AM: THE FACILITY OPERATOR AND ENGINEER WENT TO INVESTIGATE THE PSV AND FOUND THAT THE TUBING LEADING TO THE PSV PILOT HAD A BLOWN-OUT CONNECTION. BENCH-TESTED THE PSV TO ENSURE THE PROPER SET POINT. (NO ISSUES FOUND)    TUESDAY, MAY 20TH @~9:00AM: MU5 WAS PLACED BACK IN SERVICE AT STATION 40 WITH NO ISSUES.

ON MAY 9, 2025, AN INCIDENT OCCURRED ON THE 210000 - PERKINS 10" HP TO FT CHADBOURNE, 6.14 MILES SOUTHWEST OF SILVER, TEXAS IN COKE COUNTY.    AT APPROXIMATELY 1930 THE LINE HAD A RELEASE. IT WAS DETERMINED TO BE A RUPTURE THAT OCCURRED DURING ROUTINE MAINTENANCE PIGGING OPERATIONS.    ON MAY 16, 2025, AT 1230, IT WAS DETERMINED THE REPAIRS WOULD EXCEED THE $145,400.00 REPORTABLE DOLLAR CRITERIA AND THE NRC AND THE TXRRC WERE NOTIFIED.    THE LINE SEPARATION IS STILL UNDER INVESTIGATION AND THE AFFECTED SECTION OF THE PIPE HAS BEEN SENT TO THE LAB FOR ANALYSIS.  A SUPPLEMENTAL REPORT WILL BE SUBMITTED WHEN THE LAB ANALYSIS AND INVESTIGATION IS COMPLETE.     **THE LAB RESULTS CONCLUDED THAT THE FAILURE COINCIDES WITH A REGION OF INTERNAL CORROSION PRESENT ALONG THE BOTTOM OF THE PIPE.  THE INTERNAL CORROSION OCCURRED DUE TO HYDROGEN SULFIDE AND CARBON DIOXIDE COMBINING WITH WATER TO FORM AN ACIDIC ENVIRONMENT.    TO PREVENT THIS FROM OCCURRING IN THE FUTURE, OPERATIONS WILL IMPLEMENT A PIGGING SCHEDULE AND CORROSION INHIBITOR PROGRAM SPECIFIC FOR THE PIPELINE.  COUPONS WILL BE ADDED BEFORE THE LINE IS PUT BACK INTO SERVICE.     A SUPPLEMENTAL REPORT WILL BE SUBMITTED ONCE THE PIPELINE HAS BEEN PUT BACK INTO SERVICE.    **ON SEPTEMBER 19, 2025, AT APPROXIMATELY 1000 THE LINE WAS PUT BACK INTO SERVICE.

THE INITIAL INDICATION OF THE EVENT OCCURRED WHEN THE CONTROL ROOM SAW A LOSS OF SCADA COMMUNICATIONS AT METER STATION PIN #3000. THERE WAS NO INDICATION THAT A RELEASE WAS OCCURRING AT THAT TIME. THEN, NGPL RECEIVED A PHONE CALL FROM THE WOODWARD FIRE DEPARTMENT INDICATING THAT THE FIRE DEPARTMENT WAS RESPONDING TO A FIRE 1.5 MILES AWAY FROM THE METER STATION. NGPL  PERSONNEL WERE DISPATCHED TO METER STATION PIN #3000 AND CONFIRMED THERE WAS FIRE AT THE METER STATION. THE NGPL METER STATION WAS ISOLATED AND WAS NO LONGER FEEDING THE FIRE AT 12:50. NGPL'S CUSTOMER DID NOT IMMEDIATELY ISOLATE THEIR LINE BECAUSE THEY DID NOT WANT TO INTERRUPT SERVICE TO ONE OR MORE TOWNS IN OKLAHOMA SO THE FIRE CONTINUED TO BURN UNTIL EXTINGUISHED AT 22:10 ON APRIL 20, 2025. NO REPAIRS WERE NECESSARY ON THE MAIN LINE. SERVICE WAS RESTORED TO THE MAINLINE ON 4/24/25 AT 16:50. THE METER STATION WAS LEFT OUT OF SERVICE. THE CAUSE OF THE EVENT/LEAK WAS DETERMINED TO BE A LIGHTNING STRIKE.

ON 04/09/25 AT APPROXIMATELY 1309 PM, A VALVE CAP O-RING FAILED CAUSING THE ENGINE ROOM GAS DETECTION SYSTEM TO TRIGGER THE ESD SYSTEM.  A 26'' PLUG VALVE WAS FOUND TO BE LEAKING BY AND ADDITIONAL VALVES WERE MANUALLY OPERATED TO ISOLATE THE STATION.  UPON INVESTIGATION, IT WAS DETERMINED THE 26'' PLUG VALVE WAS FOUND IN THE CLOSED POSITION HOWEVER, THE VALVE DID NOT CLOSE ENTIRELY.    THE VALVE WAS INSPECTED, GREASED, FUNCTION TESTED AND WAS STILL FOUND TO BE NOT FULLY ISOLATING.    THE SECTION WAS ISOLATED AND TAKEN OUT OF SERVICE. VALVE WAS LOCKED OUT AND TAGGED OUT FOR FURTHER INVESTIGATION AND REPAIRS.  THE REST OF THE STATION WAS PUT BACK IN SERVICE.    NOTIFICATION WAS MADE TO THE NRC (#1428154) AT 1406 PM ON 04/09/25 AND THE 48 HOUR UPDATE (1428308) WAS MADE ON 04/11/25 AT 0908 AM.

DURING ROUTINE SHUTDOWN OF A UNIT AT THE AMARILLO COMPRESSOR STATION, GAS CONTROL RECEIVED A CALL FROM THE PUBLIC INDICATING THAT GAS WAS VENTING. AN EMPLOYEE WAS DISPATCHED TO INVESTIGATE AND UPON ARRIVAL DISCOVERED THAT THE UNIT SUCTION VALVE DID NOT CLOSE. THE VENT VALVE WAS THEREFORE VENTING NATURAL GAS. THE EMPLOYEE SHUT THE VENT VALVE AND THE SYSTEM WAS RETURNED BACK TO NORMAL OPERATION. THE RELEASE WAS ESTIMATED TO HAVE LASTED FOR ONE HOUR. UPON INVESTIGATION, IT WAS DISCOVERED THAT THE VALVE MALFUNCTION WAS DUE TO A FAULTY PLC INPUT CARD. THE FAULTY PLC INPUT CARD WAS REPLACED.

OPERATIONS PERSONNEL CONFIRMED THE LEAK AND BEGAN TO ISOLATE THE PIPELINE SECTION. ON MARCH 8TH AT ROUGHLY 1924 AN INCREASE IN BUILDING LEL WAS OBSERVED BY PIPELINE CONTROL. AS A RESPONSE TO THE RISING LEL PERCENTAGE, PIPELINE CONTROL SHUTDOWN STATION REMOTELY AND SHORTLY AFTER REMOTELY EMERGENCY SHUTDOWN THE STATION TO COMBAT THE RISING LEL PERCENTAGE IN THE COMPRESSOR BUILDING. FOLLOWING THE COMMAND FROM PIPELINE CONTROL THE DISCHARGE ESD BLOCK VALVE FAILED TO CLOSE. OPERATIONS RESPONDED TO INCIDENT AND FOUND AIR PRESSURE HAD NOT ALLEVIATED FROM DISCHARGE ESD BLOCK VALVE AS DESIGNED, WHICH HELD THE VALVE IN THE OPEN POSITION. OPERATIONS COMPLETED TROUBLESHOOTING ON DISCHARGE ESD BLOCK VALVE AND BELIEVED TO HAVE BLOCK VALVE CLOSED WHICH OPENED ESD VENT VALVES. IT WAS THEN DETERMINED THAT DISCHARGE ESD BLOCK VALVE HAD NOT CLOSED ENTIRELY SO PRESSURE CONTINUED TO BE ALLEVIATED BY ESD VENT VALVES UNTIL OPERATORS WERE ABLE TO MANIPULATE VALVES IN THE FIELD COMPLETELY ISOLATING THE SYSTEM. THIS ALLOWED FOR STATION TO DEPRESSURIZE AS PLANNED AND COMPRESSOR BUILDING LEL ISSUE TO BE LOOKED INTO FURTHER. FINDING WAS A BROKEN SITE GLASS PIPE NIPPLE ON UNIT 4 SCRUBBER BOTTLE.    WILLIAMS OPERATIONS AND I&E PERSONNEL COMPLETED TROUBLESHOOTING ON DISCHARGE ESD BLOCK VALVE AND FOUND THAT VERSA VALVE ON INSTRUMENT AIR SYSTEM WAS OPERATING SPORADICALLY. VERSA VALVE ASSOCIATED WITH DISCHARGE ESD BLOCK VALVE WAS REPLACED WITH NEW BEFORE BRING STATION BACK INTO NORMAL OPERATIONS. FULL SYSTEM TEST WAS COMPLETED ON THURSDAY MARCH 13TH TO ENSURE THINGS WERE FUNCTIONING AS INTENDED.     FURTHER INVESTIGATION IS ONGOING.

ENERGY TRANSFER (ET) PERSONNEL RECEIVED A CALL FROM THE LANDOWNER AT 9:40 AM ON MARCH 7TH, 2025, OF A POTENTIAL LEAK IN AN ET ROW. ET PERSONNEL ARRIVED ON SITE AT 10:00AM AND STARTED TAKING PRECAUTIONARY MEASURES AND ISOLATING THE LINE. THE LINE WAS ISOLATED AT 11:44 AM. IT WAS NOT CONFIRMED THAT THE LEAK WAS ON THE GALVAN G13 LTS UNTIL 14:05 ON MARCH 11TH, 2025, AND IT WAS PREDICTED TO EXCEED THE COST REPORTING THRESHOLD. THE INCIDENT INVESTIGATION IS STILL UNDERWAY, AND THE LINE IS CURRENTLY OUT OF SERVICE. REMEDIATION IS PENDING RESULTS OF THE INVESTIGATION.    ON MAY 19TH 2025 ET COMPLETED THE PIPELINE REPAIRS ON THE AFFECTED AREAS IDENTIFIED. THE LINE WAS PLACED BACK INTO SERVICE ON JULY 17TH, 2025.    THE SAMPLES FROM THE PIPE SECTIONS THAT WERE REPLACED WERE SENT OFF FOR METALLURGICAL ANALYSIS WHERE THE CAUSE WAS DETERMINED TO BE INTERNAL MICROBIOLOGICAL INDUCED CORROSION (MIC). A CHEMICAL TREATMENT PLAN WILL BE IMPLEMENTED TO PREVENT REOCCURRENCE.

OPERATIONS DISCOVERED GAS LEAK AT MP 97.15 ON SVL-T-T-T WITH HANDHELD LEAK SURVEY EQUIPMENT.  AFTER CONFIRMATION, LINE PRESSURE WAS REGULATED TO 80% OF OPERATING PRESSURE AND EXISTING PRESSURE WAS DRAWN DOWN BY A DOWNSTREAM CUSTOMER.  AFTER EXCAVATION, A TRANSVERSE CRACK WAS VISUALLY IDENTIFIED ON THE PIPE BODY.  THE LINE WAS SUBSEQUENTLY ISOLATED, FURTHER DRAWN DOWN BY CUSTOMERS WITH REMAINING PRESSURE BLOWN DOWN.  THE PIPE SEGMENT WAS THEN CUT OUT AND REPLACED WITH PRETESTED PIPING.  THE CUTOUT PIPE WAS SENT TO A METALLURGICAL LAB FOR ANALYSIS.  LAB ANALYSIS CONCLUDED THE FOLLOWING:  THE PRIMARY FAILURE MECHANISM WAS STRESS CORROSION CRACKING (SCC), DRIVEN BY RESIDUAL TENSILE STRESSES FROM PREEXISTING BENDING DURING CONSTRUCTION IN COMBINATION WITH A MILDLY CORROSIVE, OXYGEN-DEPLETED ENVIRONMENT.  SCC MAY NOT HAVE OCCURRED IN THE ABSENCE OF PIPE BENDING DURING CONSTRUCTION, HIGHLIGHTING THE CRITICAL ROLE OF MECHANICAL LOADING IN THIS FAILURE.  UNINTENTIONAL LOSS VOLUME WAS UPDATED AND REDUCED AFTER FURTHER ANALYSIS.
cause: MATERIAL FAILURE OF PIPE OR WELD

text: MONTANA DAKOTA UTILITIES (MDU) EMPLOYEE RESPONDED TO A NO-HEAT/GAS ODOR CALL AT THE FARMHOUSE NEAR THE LEAK AT 3:49 AM MT/ 4:49 AM CT AM MONDAY 2/17/25.  CUSTOMER'S FURNACE WOULD RUN FOR A SHORT PERIOD OF TIME AND THEN SHUT DOWN. MDU EMPLOYEE SAID THE PRESSURE AT THE CUSTOMER'S HOUSE WAS ZERO. CUSTOMER ALSO SAID SHE HEARD A LOUD HISSING, FIRST HEARING THE HISSING ABOUT 3:00 PM MT/4:00 PM CT SUNDAY 2/16/25. MDU EMPLOYEE WENT TO THE FARM TAP TAKE-OFF AND PRESSURE WAS ZERO ON THE MDU SIDE THERE AS WELL.  THE SOUND OF HISSING WAS LOUD, AND MDU EMPLOYEE CALLED WBI GAS CONTROL AND REQUESTED WBI EMPLOYEES TO ASSIST, WBI EMPLOYEES RESPONDED TO THE SCENE.     MDU EMPLOYEE ALSO SAID THAT HE WAS RESPONDING TO GAS ODOR CALLS IN SIDNEY ON 2-16-25, HIS FIRST CALL WAS 2:00 AM MT/3:00 AM CT. THE GAS ODOR/LEL AND CALLS VARIED IN NUMBER WITH WIND DIRECTION; WHEN THE WIND WAS BLOWING TOWARD TOWN CALLS INCREASED.  WBI EMPLOYEES RESPONDED TO THE LOCATION AND CONFIRMED SUSPECTED AREA OF THE LEAK TO WBI GAS CONTROL AT 7:30AM MST ON 2/17/25. PIPELINE WAS CONTINUALLY MONITORED UNTIL IT WAS SHUT IN AND BLOWN DOWN AT 2:00PM MST ON 2/17/25. LINE WAS REPAIRED AND RETURNED TO SERVICE BY 12:30AM MST ON 2/18/25.    SUPPLEMENTAL INFORMATION 6/13/2025:  THE FAILED SECTION WAS SENT INTO A LAB FOR METALLURGICAL ANALYSIS. THE RESULTS FROM THIS ANALYSIS CONFIRMED THAT THE CAUSE OF THE FAILURE WAS LACK OF PENETRATION AND MISALIGNMENT OF THE WELD WHEN THE WELD WAS MADE DURING THE INITIAL CONSTRUCTION OF THE PIPELINE IN 1947.
cause: MATERIAL FAILURE OF PIPE OR WELD

text: ON 02/10/2025, A LANDOWNER CONTACTED A CNX REPRESENTATIVE TO INQUIRE ABOUT AN AUDIBLE POTENTIAL GAS RELEASE AT THE MOR40 VALVE SETTING. IT WAS INITIALLY ASSUMED THE OBSERVED NOISE WAS FROM CONTEMPORANEOUS CNX PIGGING OPERATIONS BLOWING DOWN THE BARREL AT BAILEY VALVE SET TO LAUNCH A PIG.  THE CNX REPRESENTATIVE CONTACTED THE LANDOWNER BACK TO RELAY THAT INFORMATION AND THE LANDOWNER THANKED THE CNX REPRESENTATIVE FOR THE RESPONSE.  DURING THIS PIGGING OPERATION THAT WAS CONDUCTED PURSUANT TO CNX PIGGING PROCEDURES AND OPERATIONAL PARAMETERS,  THE PRESSURE INCREASED IN THE 1260 MOR40 U2 PIPELINE (UPSTREAM OF THE PIPELINE BEING PIGGED). BASED ON A TREND OF THE DATA, THE PRESSURE APPEARS TO HAVE REMAINED BELOW THE MAOP OF THE PIPELINE AND THE SET-POINT FOR THE PRV LOCATED UPSTREAM AT THE MOR40 WELL PAD.  HOWEVER, THE PRV OPENED AT THIS TIME. THE PRV REMAINED OPEN AND RELEASED GAS UNTIL A PRODUCTION OPERATOR ARRIVED ONSITE APPROXIMATELY TWO HOURS LATER AND FOUND THE PRV RELIEVING. THE PRODUCTION OPERATOR SECURED THE RELEASE WITHIN APPROXIMATELY 9 MINUTES OF HIS FINDING.  THE PRV WAS SET TO RELIEVE AT 1300 PSIG; BASED ON THE PRESSURE DATA TREND IT APPEARS TO HAVE RELIEVED AT APPROXIMATELY 1126 PSIG. THE PRV WAS TESTED ON 02/11/2025 AND FOUND TO RELIEVE AT 1148 PSIG; IT WAS THEN RESET TO 1300 PSIG. THE PRV WAS LATER THOROUGHLY INSPECTED BY THE MANUFACTURER (MERCER) WHO FOUND EVIDENCE OF NORMAL WEAR ON VALVE INTERNAL COMPONENTS. THE MANUFACTURER STATED THAT THIS WEAR COULD CAUSE A POTENTIAL LEAK, WHICH IN TURN COULD CAUSE A VALVE TO ACTIVATE BELOW ITS SET PRESSURE; IN ADDITION, THE MANUFACTURER TESTED THE SPRING FOR PROPER FUNCTION AND FOUND IT TO BE WITHIN TOLERANCE. AFTER COMPLETING THEIR INSPECTION, NO DEFINITIVE CAUSE FOR THE SUB-SET PRESSURE ACTIVATION WAS IDENTIFIED BY THE MANUFACTURER.  CNX HAS TAKEN THIS VALVE OUT OF SERVICE AND REPLACED IT WITH A NEW VALVE TO AVOID A RECURRENCE.

ON JANUARY 19, 2025, TC ENERGY CONFIRMED AN UNINTENTIONAL GAS RELEASE AT THE LOST RIVER COMPRESSOR STATION IN MATHIAS, WEST VIRGINIA, AFTER A LANDOWNER REPORTED A POTENTIAL ISSUE. UPON ARRIVAL, OPERATIONS PERSONNEL OBSERVED NATURAL GAS BEING RELEASED TO THE ATMOSPHERE AND CONFIRMED THE FAILURE AT 1801 EST. GAS CONTROL REPORTED A PRESSURE DROP FROM APPROXIMATELY 700 PSI TO 550 PSIG. THE FAILURE WAS TRACED TO ESD BLOW-OFF VALVE C10-90, WHICH OPENED OUT OF SEQUENCE DUE TO BELOW FREEZING AMBIENT ATMOSPHERIC TEMPERATURES, CAUSING A PRESSURE DROP IN THE COMPRESSED AIR SYSTEM. OPERATIONS MANUALLY ISOLATED THE VALVE BY CLOSING UPSTREAM FIRE VALVE C10-314, STOPPING THE GAS RELEASE AT 1804 EST. GAS CONTROL CONFIRMED PIPELINE WB5 WAS AT 502 PSIG AT THE TIME. THE FAILED VALVE WAS REMOVED, TESTED, AND SUCCESSFULLY CYCLED BEFORE BEING REINSTALLED. TC ENERGY WILL ASSESS MITIGATION MEASURES TO PREVENT RECURRENCE.

NRC WAS CALLED REPORTING THE SECOND SET OF BUBBLES. (NRC#1421007, 48HR UPDATE#1421083).     THE PIPELINE WAS ISOLATED ON 01/13/25 AT 1330. DUE TO POOR WEATHER CONDITIONS, SEA STATES AND DSV AVAILABILITY, THE REPAIR CONTRACTOR WAS NOT ABLE TO DEPLOY UNTIL 5/11/25.  THE LEAK WAS LOCATED AND A CLAMP WAS INSTALLED ON 5/12/25 AT 1100.  THE PIPELINE WAS RETURNED TO SERVICE AT APPROXIMATELY 1415 ON 05/14/25.    THE 48HR NRC NOTIFICATION WAS UPDATED ON 05/11/25 AT 1955 TO REFLECT THE CHANGE FROM UNKNOWN OWNER TO SEA ROBIN PIPELINE. (#1430839)    THE UNINTENTIONAL VOLUME WAS SPLIT BETWEEN TWO INCIDENTS FOR SEA ROBIN, BOTH OCCURRED 01/13/25 ON THE SAME PIPELINE.  TOTAL VOLUME FOR BOTH INCIDENTS WAS 1,587,069 MCF.

ON DECEMBER 29, 2024, BATESVILLE COMPRESSOR STATION 63 ON THE TENNESSEE GAS PIPELINE (TGP) SYSTEM EXPERIENCED AN ESD EVENT. GAS CONTROL IMMEDIATELY CONTACTED TGP OPERATIONS AT 01:45 CST. THE OPERATIONS TEAM ARRIVED ON SITE AT 2:05 CST AND CONFIRMED THAT GAS WAS VENTING. THE KM TECHNICIAN IDENTIFIED VALVE 63-1S TO BE UNEXPECTEDLY OPEN AND CLOSED THE VALVE AND SECURED THE GAS RELEASE. THE NRC WAS CALLED AT 3:04 CST BY KM PERSONNEL AND THE INITIAL REPORT WAS CAPTURED AS RECEIVED BY 3:07 CST. A 48-HOUR NRC REPORT WAS MADE TO UPDATE THE GAS RELEASE VOLUME TO 49,399 MCF. INITIAL INVESTIGATION DETERMINED THAT LIGHTNING HAD STRUCK THE BUILDING PROTECTION SYSTEM IN COMPRESSOR BUILDING "B" CAUSING A LOSS OF COMMUNICATION WITH THE STATION CONTROLS. THIS LOSS OF COMMUNICATION ACTIVATED THE TGP ESD FAIL SAFE SYSTEM.     FOLLOWING AN INVESTIGATION REGARDING THE VALVE OPERATION, IT WAS DETERMINED THAT THE ROOT CAUSE OF THE ISSUE WAS THE FAILURE OF AN OBSOLETE ACTUATOR WHICH RESULTED IN THE VALVE ACTUATING TO THE OPEN POSITION RATHER THAN THE INTENDED CLOSED POSITION. THE FAILURE MAY HAVE BEEN ATTRIBUTED TO INTERNAL DEBRIS OR WORN COMPONENTS WITHIN THE ACTUATOR. UPON FURTHER REVIEW OF THE ESD SYSTEM, IT WAS CONCLUDED THAT SIX VALVES, INCLUDING VALVE 63-1S, WERE EQUIPPED WITH ESD ACTIVATION THAT WAS NOT FUNCTIONALLY REQUIRED. AS A RESULT, AN INITIATIVE WAS IMPLEMENTED TO RECONFIGURE THESE VALVES WITHIN THE SYSTEM TO REDUCE THE LIKELIHOOD OF MECHANICAL FAILURES.

ON DECEMBER 13, 2024, AT THE NGPL PARIS COMPRESSION STATION 802 IN LAMAR COUNTY, TEXAS, A REPORTABLE RELEASE OF 11,792 MCF OCCURRED. STATION 802 UNIT 2 EXPERIENCED A FUSE BLOWOUT ON ITS HMI, CAUSING THE UNIT TO GO OFFLINE WHILE THE MANIFOLD VALVE REMAINED OPEN, VENTING GAS FOR APPROXIMATELY 24 MINUTES.    NO INJURIES OR ILLNESSES WERE REPORTED, AND STATION 802 WAS PLACED BACK IN SERVICE SHORTLY THEREAFTER. THE INCIDENT WAS REPORTED TO THE NRC (1418839) ON THE SAME DAY, DECEMBER 13, 2024.

PERSONNEL LANDED AT HIA 582 PLATFORM FOR A ROUTINE VISIT AND NOTICED GAS BUBBLES IN THE WATER ABOUT 1/2 MILE FROM THE PLATFORM. THE LEAK WAS SUSPECTED TO BE COMING FROM THE HIOS 30" PIPELINE SEGMENT 7869. THE PIPELINE WAS ISOLATED AND THE PRESSURE ON THE PIPELINE STARTED TO DROP, VERIFYING THE LEAK WAS FROM THAT SEGMENT. THE NRC WAS NOTIFIED (REPORT #  1416543) NO SHEEN OR IMPACT TO PERSONNEL. THE SEGMENT REMAINS ISOLATED UNTIL REPAIRS CAN BE MADE.  AT THE TIME OF THIS SUBMITTAL, A DIVE BARGE HAS NOT BEEN ABLE TO VISIT THE SUB-SEA SITE OF THE PIPELINE.  THE PIPELINE SEGMENT REMAINS DEPRESSURIZED AND SHUT IN.  A DIVE BARGE IS SCHEDULED TO VISIT ON DEC. 20, 2024 IF WEATHER PERMITS.

ON 11/05/2024 AT APPROXIMATELY 04:45, DUE TO AN INCREASING FLOW RATE THAT COULD NOT BE CONTROLLED WITH A SET POINT CHANGE, GAS CONTROL CALLED A TECHNICIAN TO INVESTIGATE THE REGULATORS AT THE EFM 4 TO NET MEXICO METER STATION. UPON ARRIVAL, THE TECHNICIAN FOUND THE STATION BLOWING GAS TO THE ATMOSPHERE AND DISCOVERED A BROKEN 1" NIPPLE ON THE #2 REGULATOR RUN. AT APPROXIMATELY 06:00, THE TECHNICIAN SHUT THE UPSTREAM MANUAL VALVE AND VERIFIED THAT THE DOWNSTREAM PNEUMATIC VALVE WAS CLOSED. THE TECHNICIAN THEN THROTTLED THE #1 REGULATOR TO ACHIEVE THE DESIRED SET POINT GIVEN BY GAS CONTROL. AT 06:30, THE TECHNICIAN REPLACED THE NIPPLE WITH AN XXH NIPPLE, INSTALLED A NEW 1" VALVE, RECONNECTED THE TUBING, AND RETURNED THE STATION TO NORMAL SERVICE.

SNG LOUISVILLE COMPRESSOR STATION 4132 IMPROPER VALVE SEQUENCE CONFIGURATION ON JD MODE OF OPERATION. VALVE 137 WAS NOT CONFIGURED PROPERLY FOR JD MODE SEQUENCE. LINE PRESSURE EXCEEDED MAOP OF 500 PSIG INITIATING OVER PRESSURE DEVICE ACTIVATION ON LOW SIDE DISCHARGE HEADER AT LOUISVILLE COMPRESSOR STATION. THE HIGHEST PRESSURE REACHED WAS 524.84 PSIG. RELIEF VALVE BLEW FOR 21 MINUTES AN 7 SECONDS. CALCULATED GAS LOSS IS 4,610.47 MCF AND IS RECORDABLE TO PHMSA.   NO INJURIES, NO CONTRACTOR INVOLVEMENT, NOT PART OF A PROJECT.

ON FRIDAY AFTERNOON 9/20/24 AT 13:21 CT, A TECHNICIAN AT THE MONROE GAS STORAGE COMPRESSOR STATION OBSERVED SMALL BUBBLES RISING WITHIN A PUDDLE OF WATER WHILE DOING REGULAR INSPECTION ROUNDS WITHIN THE FENCED FACILITY. AFTER CONFIRMING THE PRESENCE OF NATURAL GAS AT THE LOCATION AND SUSPECTING A PINHOLE LEAK, THE 18" EASTSIDE GAS TRANSMISSION LINE WAS ISOLATED BY MANUALLY CLOSING THE DOWNSTREAM VALVES. BECAUSE THE LINE WAS NOT FLOWING AT THE TIME, THE UPSTREAM VALVES WERE ALREADY CLOSED. THE EFFECTED LINE SEGMENT WAS ISOLATED BY 14:13 CT.  AFTER INITIAL COORDINATION REGARDING POSSIBLE COST OF REPAIR, IT WAS DETERMINED TO CLASSIFY THE EVENT AS AN INCIDENT AND NOTIFY THE NATIONAL RESPONSE CENTER (NRC). THE NRC WAS NOTIFIED BY THE WILLIAMS SECURITY OPERATIONS CENTER AT 15:27 CT. THE PIPELINE WAS SAFELY BLOWN DOWN WITH LOCK OUT / TAG OUT COMPLETED BY 19:20 CT THAT EVENING.    DUE TO THE PIPELINE'S 10' DEPTH IN THE AREA, IT TOOK MULTIPLE DAYS FOR CONTRACTORS TO CLEAN THE LINE THROUGH CLEANING PIGS, PURGE WITH NITROGEN AND POTHOLE THROUGH HYDROVACING TO PINPOINT THE LEAK LOCATION. ONCE IDENTIFIED (THROUGH DETECTING THE PRESENCE OF NITROGEN), THE LEAK LOCATION WAS FULLY AND SAFELY EXCAVATED (CONSIDERING THE SIGNIFICANT DEPTH) ON 10/14/24.  AS OF 10/15/24, INTERNAL CORROSION WAS FOUND AT THE PINHOLE LEAK LOCATION. THE EFFECTED PIPE IMMEDIATELY NEAR THE LEAK LOCATION WAS CUT-OUT ON 10/17/24 AND SENT TO A LAB FOR ANALYSIS.     WILLIAMS OPERATIONS, PIPELINE INTEGRITY AND CONSTRUCTION TEAMS ESTABLISHED A CONSERVATIVE PLAN TO REPLACE NECESSARY PIPE AND RETURN THE LINE TO SERVICE. APPROXIMATELY 350 FEET OF 18-INCH PIPE IN THE LOW AREA OF THE PIPELINE (WITHIN THE FACILITY) WAS REPLACED AND HYDROTESTED. THE LINE WAS RETURNED TO SERVICE ON 11/9/2024.    THE CAUSE IS SUSPECTED TO BE SULFATE REDUCING BACTERIA MICROBIOLOGICALLY INFLUENCED CORROSION (SRB-MIC) BASED ON LAB RESULTS. REPRESENTATIVES FROM OPERATIONS, MANAGEMENT AND PIPELINE INTEGRITY HAVE ESTABLISHED AN INTERNAL CORROSION MITIGATION PLAN TO PREVENT REOCCURRENCE. COUPONS HAVE BEEN INSTALLED AT EACH WELL HEAD LOCATION AND OTHER LOCATIONS, BASED ON INTERNAL CORROSION DATA GATHERED, OPERATIONS, MANAGEMENT, COMPLIANCE AND CORROSION DEPARTMENT WILL DEEM IF MORE LOCATIONS ARE NEEDED. A PIGGING PROGRAM THAT INCLUDES ALL 13 LATERALS IS FORTHCOMING, WITH ADDITIONAL FOCUS ON THE 18" LATERAL.

DURING ROUTINE PIGGING OPERATION TO REMOVE HYDROCARBON LIQUIDS AND WATER FROM A 60-PSIG GAS GATHERING PIPELINE, THE FLUIDS WERE DECANTED IN A CONTROLLED MANNER INTO A TEMPORARY ATMOSPHERIC STORAGE (FRAC) TANK. OPERATING PROCEDURES DID NOT ADDRESS THE NEED TO ESTABLISH A SAFETY ZONE (VISUAL WARNINGS AND WINDSOCKS) AROUND THE PIPELINE PIGGING OPERATION AREA TO HELP TO ELIMINATE RANDOM IGNITION SOURCES IN AN AREA EXPECTED TO HAVE TEMPORARY EXPOSURE TO HYDROCARBON VAPORS. ULTIMATELY, IT WAS A VEHICLE WHICH WAS PARKED TOO CLOSE TO THE WORK AREA WHICH PROVIDED THE IGNITION SOURCE WHEN AN EMPLOYEE ENTERED THE VEHICLE AND TURNED THE IGNITION KEY. THE RELEASE OF HYDROCARBON VAPORS WAS THE EXPECTED RESULT OF THE CONTROLLED DEPRESSURIZING OF A STREAM OF HYDROCARBON LIQUIDS INTO AN ATMOSPHERIC STORAGE VESSEL, WHICH HAD NO MEANS OF VAPOR CONTAINMENT. ADDITIONALLY, A VAPOR CONTROL AND DISCHARGE PLAN WAS NOT UTILIZED DURING THE PROCESS. THE ROOT CAUSE OF THE FIRE WAS A FAILURE OF OPERATING PROCEDURES IN ALLOWING A POTENTIAL SOURCE OF IGNITION (A VEHICLE) TO BE LOCATED WITHIN AN AREA EXPECTED TO BE TEMPORARILY EXPOSED TO EVOLVED HYDROCARBON VAPORS. THIS INCIDENT WAS NOT THE RESULT OF ANY PIPELINE MATERIAL FAILURE, ABNORMAL OPERATING CONDITIONS (I.E., OVERPRESSURE CONDITION), OR INCIDENTAL THIRD-PARTY DAMAGE TO THE PIPELINE FACILITIES.

DURING A ROUTINE OFFSHORE FLIGHT PATROL, A PIPELINE TECHNICIAN SPOTTED AN AREA OF BUBBLES IN THE GOM NEAR THE HIA 582 PLATFORM. THE BUBBLES WERE SUSPECTED TO BE COMING FROM THE 30" NATURAL GAS PIPELINE SEGMENT 7869. THE PIPELINE WAS ISOLATED AND MONITORED. NO SHEEN WAS OBSERVED. THE LEAK WAS REPORTED TO THE NRC AND PHMSA.    THE VISION BARGE, CONTRACTED FROM CHET MORRISSON, ARRIVED ON LOCATION. THE PIPELINE LIES AT A SEA DEPTH OF 356 FEET IN CONDITIONS OF VERY POOR VISIBILITY. SATURATION DIVERS FOUND THE PINHOLE NATURAL GAS LEAK ON THE 30" PIPELINE. THE CONCRETE AND SOMASTIC COATING ON THE PIPE WERE REMOVED AND A 30" X 24" PLIDCO CLAMP WAS BOLTED IN PLACE OVER THE LEAK. ALL UT READINGS AROUND THE CLAMP AND LEAK AREA WERE GOOD.    AN ANODE SLED WAS INSTALLED ON THE PIPE TO SUPPORT CURRENT CORROSION MITIGATION PROGRAMS. THE PIPELINE WAS TESTED UP TO 900 PSI, NORMAL OPERATING PRESSURE, AND NO LEAKS WERE OBSERVED BY THE DIVERS. THE PIPELINE WAS PLACED BACK IN SERVICE. ON 8/8/2024, AN OPERATIONS DECISION WAS MADE TO CHANGE OPERATIONAL FLOW WITHIN THE FACILITY. THIS WAS A NEW VALVE CONFIGURATION TO MEET CUSTOMER DEMAND. DURING THE OPERATIONAL VALVE REALIGNMENTS, PSV 114 WAS NOT IDENTIFIED THUS NO ADJUSTMENTS WERE MADE TO THE PSV.  ON 8/9/2024, UPON CHANGING THE OPERATIONAL ALIGNMENT EDMOND STORAGE PIPELINE A1129 TO A4002 PRESSURE RELIEF VALVE (PSV114) ACTIVATED AS DESIGNED.   WITH THE ACTIVATION OF THE PSV, THERE WAS A RELEASE OF 26.1 MMCF.  OPERATIONS HAS CONDUCTED A CAUSE MAP OF THE INCIDENT. THIS REVIEW INCLUDED A HAZARD ANALYSIS OF EACH FLOW PATH THROUGH THE FACILITY TO ENSURE APPROPRIATE PROTECTION IS IN PLACE. ADDITIONALLY, ALL OPERATIONAL FLOW CHANGES WILL GO THROUGH A REVIEW PROCESS PRIOR TO MAKING FUTURE CHANGES TO MINIMIZE THE OPPORTUNITY FOR REOCCURRENCE.

ON JULY 2, 2024, A FIRE OCCURRED AT THE OASIS WAHA COMPRESSOR STATION, 2.26 MILES NORTH OF COYANOSA, TEXAS IN PECOS COUNTY.    AT APPROXIMATELY 0500 SCADA NOTIFIED OPERATIONS ABOUT A UNIT DOWN ON FIRE DETECTION.    0520, IT WAS DISCOVERED THAT COMPRESSOR UNITS 3 & 4 WERE ON FIRE, ESDD THE STATION AND CALLED THE LOCAL FIRE DEPARTMENT TO THE STATION.    AT 0543, IT WAS DETERMINED THE REPAIRS AND DAMAGES WOULD EXCEED THE $145,400.00 REPORTABLE DOLLAR CRITERIA AND THE NRC AND THE TXRRC WAS NOTIFIED.    LOCAL FIRE DEPARTMENT EXTINGUISHED THE FIRE.    THE DAMAGED COMPRESSORS WERE BYPASSED, AND THE STATION WAS BACK ONLINE ON JULY 5.    FUEL GAS AND LINE OIL FUELED THE FIRE.  THE CAUSE OF THE FIRE IS STILL UNDER INVESTIGATION. A SUPPLEMENTAL REPORT WILL BE SUBMITTED ONCE INVESTIGATION IS COMPLETE.      **DURING THE PHYSICAL INSPECTION THERE WERE ALSO FOUND TO BE BROKEN BOLTS GATHERED FOR ANALYSIS.  THE COUPLING COVER BOLT, AS WELL AS A MISSING BOLT FROM THE TURBINE DRAIN FLANGE WERE FOUND ON THE SKID FLOOR.  THESE BOLTS WERE ALSO SENT TO METALLURGIST ALSO AND WERE DETERMINED TO HAVE FAILED DUE TO FATIGUE.      THE SHEARED BOLT AND STAINING ON THE DRAIN FLANGE SUGGEST A POSSIBLE ROOT CAUSE OF THE FIRE.  THE FAILURE OF THE FLANGE AS AN OIL SEALING MECHANISM WOULD LEAD TO OIL DRAINING DIRECTLY ONTO THE EXHAUST BLANKET LEADING TO VAPORIZATION AND IGNITION OF THE OIL.    THIS WAS AN ISOLATED INCIDENT.     THE MITIGATION STEPS TO PREVENT THIS FROM OCCURRING IN THE FUTURE ARE AS FOLLOWED:  -EVALUATE FIRE EYES/GAS DETECTOR PLACEMENT ON THESE PACKAGES.    -CHANGE FASTENERS ON ENGINE SWINGS.     -COORDINATE AN EVALUATION OF ALL UNITS TO CONFIRM NO MISSING/BROKEN FASTENERS, THIS IS NOW INCLUDED IN OUR 4000-HOUR PREVENTATIVE MAINTENANCE PLAN.

ON 6/17/2024 BUBBLING WAS SEEN FROM A THIRD-PARTY HELICOPTER PILOT.  THE PILOT REPORTED THE SITUATION TO BBT WHICH THEY INVESTIGATED AND CONFIRMED ON 6/18/2024 TO BE THE 16" BBT PIPELINE.  BBT INITIALLY TREATED IT AS A SRC DUE TO THE NATURE OF THE EVENT (SLOW LEAK) AND THE VICINITY (IN THE MARSH, 1.5 MILES FROM THE NEAREST BUILDING), BUT WAS ELEVATED TO AN INCIDENT WITHIN AN HOUR WHEN IT WAS DETERMINED IT WAS GOING TO EXCEED THE REGULATORY REQUIREMENT IN BECOMING AN INCIDENT ON 6/28/2024 (DUE TO THE MOBILIZATION COST AND EQUIPMENT NEEDED IN THE MARSH) .  THE LEAK WAS ISOLATED IMMEDIATELY, AND DISCUSSIONS WERE MADE TO MINIMIZE FUGITIVE EMISSIONS. AS A RESULT, CUSTOMERS BURNED DOWN THE GAS TO THE REGULATOR SET POINT (200PSI).  THE REMAINING GAS WAS BLOWN DOWN TO INITIATE REPAIRS.  REPAIRS STARTED ON 6/24/2024 (WELD-ON SLEEVE) AND THE PIPELINE WAS RETURNED TO SERVICE ON 7/1/2024.  LOCALIZED PITTING WAS DETERMINED TO BE THE CAUSE IN-BETWEEN THE CONCRETE COATINGS NEAR THE SEAMS WHERE COAL TAR IS THE COATING.

ON MAY 30, 2024, A BODY VENT FITTING ON AN ABOVE-GROUND 12-INCH VALVE BEGAN LEAKING TO ATMOSPHERE AFTER IT WAS OPERATED AS PART OF AN IN-LINE INSPECTION OF A NATURAL GAS TRANSMISSION PIPELINE.  THE 12-INCH VALVE WAS ASSOCIATED WITH THE ISOLATION OF A PIG RECEIVER LOCATION INVOLVED IN THE IN-LINE INSPECTION PROJECT. THE LEAK WAS CONTINUOUSLY MONITORED BY UGI PERSONNEL UNTIL THE VALVE WAS REPLACED ON JUNE 18, 2024.    ON JULY 7, 2025, A SUPPLEMENTAL AND FINAL REPORT IS BEING FILED TO PROVIDE UPDATED INCIDENT INFORMATION.     UGI CONSULTED WITH THE VALVE MANUFACTURER WHO EXAMINED AND INVESTIGATED THE VALVE. UGI SUBSEQUENTLY PERFORMED A ROOT CAUSE ANALYSIS OF THE EVENT. UGI CONCLUDED THAT THE ROOT CAUSE OF THIS EVENT WAS ATTRIBUTABLE TO THE VALVE SEALS THAT WERE EXPOSED TO DEBRIS SUCH AS WELD SLAG. WELD SLAG WAS FOUND EMBEDDED INTO THE SEALS AND DID NOT ALLOW THE VALVE TO SEAL COMPLETELY. THE BODY BLEED VALVE ALSO DID NOT SEAL AND WAS STRIPPED WHILE BEING OPERATED AND LEAKED CONTINUOUSLY TO ATMOSPHERE FOR A SHORT DURATION. UGI WAS ABLE TO STOP THE LEAK UNTIL THE FINAL REPAIR COULD BE MADE. BASED ON THE SMALL OPENING OF THE BODY BLEED VALVE, THE ESCAPING GAS WAS NEGLIGIBLE.

A PLANNED ESD WAS CONDUCTED TO DEPRESSURIZE THE STATION FOR MAINTENANCE AND VALVE REPAIRS. DURING THE ESD, THE DISCHARGE SIDE GATE VALVES OPERATED AS INTENDED, BUT SUCTION SIDE GATE VALVE #43 DID NOT FULLY CLOSE, ONLY PARTIALLY CLOSING. AN INVESTIGATION WILL BE CONDUCTED TO DETERMINE WHY VALVE #43 DID NOT FUNCTION PROPERLY.

ET PERSONNEL PROCEEDED WITH ISOLATING THE LINE AND AT 14:03 THE VALVES WERE LOCKED OUT. AT APPROXIMATELY 14:45, ENERGY TRANSFER PERSONNEL CONFIRMED A LEAK ON THE SME L11 12-INCH PIPELINE   (28.122918, -99.967259) AND PROCEEDED WITH BLOWING DOWN THE LINE. THIS IS A 12-INCH TYPE C GAS GATHERING LINE IN A RURAL AREA LOCATED IN WEBB COUNTY NEAR LAREDO, TX    AN ESTIMATED 22 MCF OF UNINTENTIONAL GAS WAS RELEASED. IT WAS DETERMINED UPON CONFIRMED DISCOVERY THAT THIS INCIDENT WOULD BE REPORTABLE DUE TO THE ESTIMATE OF PROPERTY DAMAGE AND REPAIR COST. THIS INCIDENT WAS REPORTED TO THE NRC ON APRIL 17TH 2024, AT 2:57PM    THE LINE WAS EXCAVATED AND A COUPON (36-INCHES LONG: 0.250-INCH WT) WAS SENT INTO ADV INTEGRITY FOR 3RD PARTY ANALYSIS.  FAILURE WAS FOUND TO BE AT THE 6 OCLOCK POSITION; PIT WAS MEASURED TO BE 0.5 INCHES IN DIAMETER.  SEDIMENT WAS FOUND, REMOVED, AND ANALYZED AT THE 6 OCLOCK POSITION OF THE PIPE. OUR EFFORTS TO MITIGATE THIS ISSUE IS TO MODIFY OUR MAINTENANCE PLAN BY INCORPORATING CHEMICAL TREATMENT FOR IRON SULFIDE AND SOLID DEPOSITS ALONG WITH OUR ROUTINE MAINTENANCE AND PIGGING

THE INCIDENT TOOK PLACE AT FARMER BROTHERS METERING AND REGULATING STATION BEGINNING AT 20:41 ON MARCH 25, 2024. AT THE FACILITY, NATURAL GAS NORMALLY FLOWS THROUGH A FILTER SEPARATOR WHERE ANY LIQUIDS FLOWING THROUGH THE SEPARATOR GO TO A SUMP. WHEN THE SUMP LEVEL EXCEEDS A CERTAIN THRESHOLD, THE CONTROLLER ACTUATES THE CONTROL VALVE TO THE OPEN POSITION TO RELEASE LIQUIDS TO A WASTE TANK. THE CONTROL VALVE'S MECHANICAL LEVEL CONTROLLER FAILED TO REVERT POSITION ONCE THE LIQUID LEVEL IN THE SUMP HAD DROPPED BELOW THE DESIGN THRESHOLD. GAS FLOWED FROM THE SEPARATOR THROUGH A 2" NPS PIPE INTO A WASTE TANK AND THEN ENTERED THE ATMOSPHERE THROUGH THE TANK BLOWOFF VALVES UNTIL THE AFTERNOON OF MARCH 26, 2024 AT 14:45 WHEN THE INCIDENT WAS DISCOVERED.    UPON ARRIVAL AT THE FACILITY, PERSONNEL IMMEDIATELY SHUT THE MANUAL VALVE TO THE LIQUIDS TANK WHICH CEASED EMISSIONS OF NATURAL GAS TO THE ATMOSPHERE AT 15:07 ON MARCH 26, 2024. THE CONTROLLER ON THE CONTROL VALVE WAS FOUND TO BE MISALIGNED BECAUSE THE SPRING TENSION WAS TOO HIGH, NOT ALLOWING THE VALVE TO CLOSE. THE VALVE'S CONTROLLER WAS IMMEDIATELY RECALIBRATED, RESET, AND TESTED TO ENSURE FUNCTIONALITY.

text: ON JANUARY 17, 2024, AT APPROXIMATELY 06:20 HRS. CST, TC ENERGY WAS NOTIFIED BY THE PUBLIC OF A POTENTIAL GAS RELEASE AT THE CORINTH COMPRESSOR STATION. TC ENERGY OPERATIONS PERSONNEL ARRIVED AT THE CORINTH COMPRESSOR STATION, LOCATED IN ALCORN COUNTY, MISSISSIPPI, AND DISCOVERED NATURAL GAS BEING RELEASED TO ATMOSPHERE. THE UNINTENTIONAL GAS RELEASE WAS CONFIRMED BY TC ENERGY OPERATIONS AT APPROXIMATELY 07:16 HRS. CST. IT WAS LATER CONFIRMED THAT THE BLOWDOWN VALVE'S (5SH-2D BD) STRATIX SWITCH, WHICH COMMUNICATES THE VALVE STATUS TO THE PROGRAMMABLE LOGIC CONTROLLER (PLC), HAD MALFUNCTIONED. THIS LOSS OF COMMUNICATION CAUSED THE BLOWDOWN VALVE TO LOSE ITS HOLD CLOSED COMMAND FROM THE PLC. THE VALVE TRAVELED OPEN DUE TO THE LOSS OF SIGNAL WHEN THE SWITCH FAILED. THE MALFUNCTIONING SWITCH ALSO CAUSED NO ALARM TO BE CONVEYED TO THE EMERGENCY SHUTDOWN DEVICE (ESD) PLC AND THEREFORE, IS THE REASON GAS CONTROLLER DID NOT RECEIVE A "CALL OUT" ALARM FROM THE SCADA SYSTEM. TC ENERGY OPERATIONS MANUALLY CLOSED THE BLOWDOWN VALVE AT 08:05 HRS. CST. THE STRATIX SWITCH WAS REPLACED AND THE ESD SYSTEM WAS PLACED BACK INTO NORMAL SERVICE AT APPROXIMATELY 12:30 HRS. CST. THE CORINTH COMPRESSOR STATION WAS NOT SHUT DOWN DUE TO THIS INCIDENT.

ON JANUARY 12, 2024, SEVERE WEATHER INCLUDING HEAVY WINDS AND SNOW PASSED THROUGH THE GAYLORD, MICHIGAN AREA. WHEN THE POWER FAILURE ALARM WAS DETECTED AT 7:23 PM. EST, THE MONITORING CENTER CALLED THE TECHNICIAN ON SITE TO INVESTIGATE THE ALARM. THE TECHNICIAN COULD AUDIBLY HEAR BLOWING GAS AT 7:47 P.M. EST AND DISCOVERED NATURAL GAS WAS BEING RELEASED THROUGH THE UNIT 1101 BLOWDOWN STACK. IMMEDIATE ACTION WAS TAKEN BY VERIFYING NO FIRE EXISTED, A SECOND TECHNICIAN WAS DISPATCHED AND ASSISTED IN SAFELY ISOLATING THE GAS SOURCE BY CLOSING THE UNIT VALVE WHICH ENDED THE RELEASE AT 8:15 P.M. EST. UNINTENTIONAL GAS LOSS WAS CALCULATED TO 3.61 MILLION CUBIC FEET (MMCF).     NO PROPERTY DAMAGE, INJURIES OR MANDATORY EVACUATIONS WERE NEEDED. THE CAUSE OF THE UNINTENTIONAL RELEASE WAS ATTRIBUTED TO LOSS OF COMMERCIAL POWER AT THE STATION. THE BACKUP GENERATOR DID NOT START, AND THE VENT VALVE OPENED DUE TO THE LOSS OF CONTROL AIR PRESSURE.  THE VENT VALVE IS DESIGNED TO FAIL OPEN IN THE CASE OF LOW CONTROL AIR AND THE SUCTION AND DISCHARGE VALVES REMAINED IN THEIR CURRENT OPEN OPERATING STATE. NO OVERPRESSURE OCCURRED.     AFTER FURTHER INVESTIGATION OF THE AUXILIARY POWER UNIT (APU), IT WAS FOUND TWO LOOSE PRIMARY IGNITION WIRES CAUSED THE ENGINE TO BACKFIRE WHICH RESULTED IN A SMALL TEAR IN THE LEFT BANK SECONDARY FUEL REGULATOR DIAPHRAGM. A LOW HORSEPOWER CONDITION ENSUED. APU WAS REPAIRED AND PLACED BACK IN SERVICE ON JANUARY 19, 2024.    MODIFIED SECTIONS A5, G2 AND G6 PER PHMSA'S REQUEST.

ON NOVEMBER 27, 2023 AT 11:07 (CST), STATION 527 IN PORT SULPHUR, LA EXPERIENCED AN EMERGENCY SHUT DOWN (ESD) EVENT. THE INITIAL NOTIFICATION WAS COMPLETED BY LOCAL TGP OPERATIONS PERSONNEL WHO WERE ONSITE AT THE TIME OF THE EVENT. UPON STATION WALKTHROUGH, IT WAS DISCOVERED THAT THE STATION BLOCK VALVE WAS NOT FULLY CLOSED, ALLOWING FOR VENTING OF GAS THROUGH THE BLOW-DOWN VALVE. AT 11:20 (CST), TGP OPERATIONS PERSONNEL CLOSED THE BLOW-DOWN VALVE TO STOP VENTING OF THE GAS. AT THE TIME OF THE EVENT, BOTH STATION 527 AND THE ASSOCIATED SCADA SYSTEM WERE OFFLINE. THE SCADA SYSTEM WAS UNDERGOING MAINTENANCE DUE TO A FLOW-REVERSAL PROJECT OCCURRING AT THE STATION. SINCE THIS EVENT, STATION 527 HAS REMAINED IDLE.     THE INTERNAL INVESTIGATION DETERMINED THAT WHILE DOWNLOADING THE RTU, THE ESD TEST STAND WAS NOT REMOVED FROM SERVICE. UPON DOWNLOADING THE RTU, THE STATION ESD ACTIVATED. IT WAS DETERMINED THAT ONCE THE ESD ACTIVATED, THE STATION BLOCK VALVE WAS NOT ABLE TO FULLY CLOSE DUE TO A ROCK FILTER BECOMING CLOGGED ON THE PILOT GAS. THE GAS LOSS DUE TO THIS INCIDENT 16,319 MCF.     IN ORDER TO PREVENT REOCCURRENCE, WRITTEN PROCEDURES ARE BEING DEVELOPED FOR TAKING THE ESD TEST STAND OUT OF SERVICE AND FOR DOWNLOADING THE RTU SAFETY. ADDITIONALLY, THE VALVE OPERATOR IS BEING ADJUSTED SO THAT THE POWER GAS DOES NOT HAVE REDUNDANT FILTRATION.

ON NOVEMBER 13, 2023, ONEOK TECHNICIANS WERE TROUBLESHOOTING A COMPRESSOR AT THE HERSCHER COMPRESSOR STATION. DURING TROUBLESHOOTING AN INCORRECT FUSE WAS REMOVED, CAUSING THE STATION TO EMERGENCY SHUTDOWN (ESD). DURING THE ESD SEQUENCE, THE OPERATORS NOTICED THE SHUTDOWN WAS TAKING LONGER THAN TYPICAL, THEREFORE THEY PROCEEDED TO MANUALLY ISOLATE THE STATION BLOW DOWN VALVE TO STOP THE BLOW DOWN. UPON FURTHER STATION WALKDOWN INSPECTIONS, THE OPERATORS DISCOVERED THAT THE STATION LOADING VALVE WAS LEFT IN THE INCORRECT OPEN POSITION. THE STATION WAS RETURNED TO SERVICE AFTER THE OPERATORS CLOSED THE VALVE AND LEFT IT IN THE CORRECT POSITION.

ON NOVEMBER 8, 2023, AT APPROXIMATELY 12:11 HOURS CONSUMERS ENERGY GAS CONTROL RECEIVED AN ALARM NOTIFICATION WHICH INDICATED A POSSIBLE FIRE AT THE ST. CLAIR COMPRESSOR STATION (PLANT 4 DEHYDRATION SYSTEM BUILDING). THE CONSUMERS ENERGY ST. CLAIR COMPRESSOR STATION IS IN IRA, MICHIGAN (ST. CLAIR COUNTY).    A STATION MECHANIC AT THE SITE WAS NOTIFIED AND CONFIRMED ACTIVATION OF THE PLANT FIRE-GATE SYSTEM OCCURRED DUE TO THE FIRE DETECTION ALARM. FOLLOWING THE EVENT, THE PLANT WAS REMOVED FROM SERVICE AND THE SCENE WAS MADE SAFE. ADDITIONAL PERSONNEL WERE DISPATCHED TO THE STATION TO DETERMINE THE POTENTIAL CAUSE OF THE ACTIVATION.     DURING THE INCIDENT INVESTIGATION, NO NOTABLE INDICATIONS OF FAILURES WERE PRESENT IN THE FACILITY, BUT UPON ARRIVAL, IT WAS NOTED THAT A GAP IN THE INSULATION ON THE REBOILER EXHAUST STACK WAS CLEARLY VISIBLE AND WAS PRESUMED TO BE THE SOURCE OF A FALSE TRIP INDICATION TO THE FIRE-EYE (IN DIRECT LINE OF SIGHT) DUE TO THE INFRARED IRRADIATION FROM THE PIPE (OPERATING AS NORMAL UP TO 1500 DEGREE F). THE INSULATION ON THE EXHAUST SYSTEM WAS INSPECTED WITH NO NOTABLE ISSUES OBSERVED, REPAIRED, AND RETURNED TO SERVICE ON NOVEMBER 9, 2023.    ON NOVEMBER 10, 2023, AT APPROXIMATELY 11:17 HOURS, LESS THAN 24 HOURS AFTER THE RETURN TO SERVICE CONSUMERS ENERGY GAS CONTROL RECEIVED AN ALARM NOTIFICATION WHICH INDICATED A POSSIBLE FIRE AT THE ST. CLAIR COMPRESSOR STATION (PLANT 4 DEHYDRATION SYSTEM BUILDING). THE EQUIPMENT WAS TAKEN OFF-LINE, AND ALL INSULATION WAS REMOVED TO PERMIT PHYSICAL INSPECTION. SEVERAL CRACKED WELDS WERE IDENTIFIED ON THE EXHAUST LINE OF THE THERMAL OXIDIZER, SUPER HEATER, AND CONDENSATE COLLECTION SYSTEM OF THE THERMAL OXIDIZER. LOOSE BOLTS WERE FOUND IN THE FLANGED CONNECTIONS OF THE SYSTEM, AND AN EXHAUST PIPE SLIP JOINT CONNECTION TO THE EXHAUST STACK WAS FOUND TO NO LONGER BE INSERTED INTO THE FITTING.    BOTH EVENTS WERE REPORTED TO MPSC AS REQUIRED WHEN AN EMERGENCY SHUTDOWN SYSTEM IS ACTIVATED, AND GAS RELEASED. HOWEVER, A MORE IN-DEPTH VISUAL INSPECTION CONFIRMED ADDITIONAL EQUIPMENT DAMAGE ANTICIPATED TO EXCEED PHMSA REPORTING CRITERIA OF $139,700.     ADDITIONAL INVESTIGATIONS AFTER THE EVENT HAVE IDENTIFIED A CONCERN RELATIVE TO INSUFFICIENT BOLT TORQUE SPECIFICATIONS USED DURING A 2020 REPAIR TO THE SYSTEM, PIPE FABRICATION FAILURE RESULTING IN PRE-STRESS BEING APPLIED TO THE FAILED SYSTEM CONNECTION POINTS, AND POTENTIAL PINNED PIPE IN A HIGH THERMAL GROWTH AREA OF THE SYSTEM EXACERBATING STRESSES IMPARTED TO THOSE SAME CONNECTION POINTS. FURTHER PROBLEM SOLVING IS REQUIRED TO DETERMINE THE ROOT CAUSE OF THE FAILURE. HOWEVER, WITH THE CONCERNS DEFINED, CONSUMERS ENERGY HAS TAKEN ACTION TO REMEDIATE EACH CONCERN THROUGH A REFABRICATION OF THE SUPER HEATER VESSEL FAILED COMPONENTS, PIPE ASSEMBLIES FOUND TO BE CREATING THE PRE-STRESS SCENARIO, SLIP JOINT INSERTION WAS INCREASED TO AVOID RISK OF THE JOINT FAILING, APPLICATION OF TORQUE SPECIFICATIONS FROM THE ORIGINAL EQUIPMENT MANUFACTURER, AND IMPLEMENTATION OF A PREVENTATIVE MAINTENANCE SCHEDULE FOR RE-VALIDATING TORQUE ON BOLTED CONNECTIONS FOLLOWING RETURN TO SERVICE.    FURTHER ANALYSIS IS REQUIRED TO SUPPORT CONFIRMATION OF THE PIPE FAILURE MODES IDENTIFIED IN THE FIELD AND IS PRESENTLY UNDERWAY. THE ORIGINAL EQUIPMENT MANUFACTURER HAS BEEN ENGAGED IN THE REVIEW AND REPAIR PLAN AND IS SUPPORTING REVIEW OF THE STRESS ANALYSIS. ENGINEERING SUPPORT HAS BEEN CONTRACTED TO SUPPORT MODEL DEVELOPMENT OF THE SYSTEM AND EXECUTE A PIPE STRESS ANALYSIS. FOLLOWING THE OUTCOME OF THE MODELING AND VALIDATION OF THE FAILURE MODES, ADDITIONAL STEPS MAY BE NECESSARY TO IMPROVE THE INTEGRITY OF THE SYSTEM AND WILL BE IMPLEMENTED ACCORDINGLY.    FURTHER ANALYSIS CONFIRMED THE FAILURE WAS A RESULT OF INSUFFICIENT BOLT TORQUE SPECIFICATIONS PROVIDED BY THE MANUFACTURER DURING A PREVIOUS REPAIR TO THE SYSTEM. THE FAILURE WAS A RESULT OF THE BOLTS YIELDING AND TORQUE WAS LOST THROUGH THE THERMAL CYCLE CAUSING BOLTS TO LOOSEN.

THE ROOT CAUSE INVESTIGATION REVEALED THE FOLLOWING:    THE INSTALLED REINFORCEMENT SADDLE (INSTALLATION DATE UNKNOWN) WAS NOT PROPERLY FITTED AND WAS ATTACHED WITH AN INSUFFICIENT SINGLE-PASS FILLET WELD TO BOTH THE PIPELINE AND TO THE CENTRAL BRANCH PIPE.  THESE WELDS ARE NOT SUFFICIENT TO PROPERLY ATTACH THIS REINFORCEMENT SADDLE.    MOVEMENT OF THE BRANCH WITH ALL ATTACHED FLANGES, VALVE, AND PIPING CAUSED A DUCTILE OVERLOAD FAILURE OF THE PIPE WALL THAT INITIATED AT THE TOE OF THE REINFORCING SADDLE TO PIPELINE WELD AND PROCEEDED THROUGH-WALL IN TWO OR MORE STEPS.    NO EVIDENCE OF FATIGUE WAS OBSERVED.
cause: MATERIAL FAILURE OF PIPE OR WELD

ON THE MORNING OF AUGUST 8, 2023, TEXAS EASTERN BEGAN AN ANOMALY DIG TO EXPOSE A GEOMETRY FEATURE (BUCKLE/DENT) AT THE 6 O-CLOCK POSITION.  THE LINE IN THIS AREA WAS VERY DEEP (>11-FEET).  THE UPSTREAM VALVE WAS CLOSED AT 09:39 E.T. TO LOWER THE LINE PRESSURE FOR THE EXCAVATION AND REPAIR.  DOWNSTREAM COMPRESSION WAS USED TO HELP PULL THE PRESSURE DOWN.  WHILE EXCAVATING THE ANOMALY, THE CREW IDENTIFIED INDICATIONS OF A LEAK AT APPROXIMATELY 17:00 ET.  AN OPERATIONS TEAM WAS THEN CALLED IN TO INVESTIGATE THE SUSPECTED LEAK. AT 19:28 ET THE DOWNSTREAM VALVE WAS CLOSED TO FULLY BLOWDOWN THE LINE. AT APPROXIMATELY 20:30 E.T. IT WAS DECIDED THAT REPAIRS COULD LIKELY EXCEED THE PHMSA REPORTING COST THRESHOLD.  AT 21:09 ET THE NATIONAL RESPONSE CENTER WAS NOTIFIED.      THE BLOWDOWN WAS COMPLETED ON AUGUST 9, 2023, AT APPROXIMATELY 12:30 ET.  THE LINE WAS THEN EXCAVATED AND THE PIPING IN AREA OF THE SUSPECTED LEAK WAS CUT OUT AND REMOVED.  AN AIR PRESSURE TEST WAS THEN PERFORMED ON THE CUT-OUT SEGMENT AND A SMALL THROUGH WALL FEATURE ON THE WELD (12 O-CLOCK) ADJACENT TO THE GEOMETRY FEATURE WAS IDENTIFIED.  THE PIPE WAS THEN TRANSPORTED TO A LAB FOR FURTHER ANALYSIS AS TO THE CAUSE.    04/24/2024 SUPPLEMENTAL  UPDATED PART G - APPARENT CAUSE AND PART J - INTEGRITY INSPECTIONS  THE CAUSE OF THE LEAK WAS TENSILE OVERLOADING OF THE PIPE RESULTING IN A 1.5-INCH DUCTILE FAILURE AT TOE OF THE GIRTH WELD. A BENDING MOMENT EXERTED HIGH TENSILE STRESS NEAR THE 12:00 O'CLOCK LOCATION AND HIGH COMPRESSIVE STRESS THE 6:00 O'CLOCK LOCATION, CAUSING THE LEAK AT THE 12:00 O'CLOCK LOCATION AND A BUCKLE AT THE 6:00 O'CLOCK LOCATION.
cause: MATERIAL FAILURE OF PIPE OR WELD

text: A GAS ODOR WAS REPORTED BY THE PUBLIC NEAR SERVICE LINE 281. DURING THE FIELD LEAK INVESTIGATION, A LEAK WAS DISCOVERED ON A 4" STEEL PIPE INDICATING THE PRESENCE OF CORROSION. THE LEAK LOCATION REQUIRED DAILY LANE CLOSURE FOR WORK ACTIVITIES RELATED TO THE REPAIR. TO ISOLATE THE LEAK, TWO STOPPLES WERE INSTALLED TO CONTINUE SERVING CUSTOMERS NATURAL GAS. A TOTAL OF 350 FEET OF NEW PIPELINE WAS INSTALLED TO REMOVE THE CORROSION. AFTER PIPE REPLACEMENT, A HYDROSTATIC TEST WAS PERFORMED TO ENSURE PIPELINE INTEGRITY. DURING ANALYSIS, THE STRAY CURRENT SOURCE CONFIRMED TO BE A TELEPHONE CABLE. UNABLE TO DETERMINE A GAS VOLUME DUE TO THE PINHOLE SIZE OF THE LEAK.

ON 6/1/2023 AT APPROXIMATELY 10:30 AM, GULF SOUTH PIPELINE COMPANY LLC'S OPERATIONS PERSONNEL WERE ALERTED BY ENTERPRISE PRODUCTS PERSONNEL THAT ENTERPRISE'S WELL 11, WHICH IS ADJACENT TO GULF SOUTH'S PETAL GAS STORAGE NATURAL GAS CAVERNS PGS 10 AND PGS 12A, WAS EXPERIENCING AN INCREASE IN PRESSURE RESULTING IN A SURFACE LEAK.  GULF SOUTH WAS NEITHER INJECTING NOR WITHDRAWING GAS FROM WELLS PGS 10 OR PGS 12A, AND DECIDED NOT TO DO SO UNTIL THE PRESSURE ON ENTERPRISE'S WELL 11 HAD STABILIZED.     ON 6/2/2023 AT APPROXIMATELY 7:10 AM, GULF SOUTH AND ENTERPRISE DETERMINED THAT THE SURFACE LEAK ON ENTERPRISE'S WELL CONTAINED METHANE AND THAT A POSSIBLE SOURCE OF THE METHANE WAS EITHER CAVERN PGS 10 OR PGS 12A COMMUNICATING WITH ENTERPRISE'S WELL 11 BELOW GROUND, IN THE SALT FORMATION.  BECAUSE OF THIS POSSIBILITY, GULF SOUTH CALLED THE NRC. DURING THE INVESTIGATION OF THIS EVENT, GULF SOUTH IDENTIFIED THAT THE MAOP OF CAVERN PGS 10, WHICH IS 1550 PSIG AT THE SURFACE, INCREASED TO 1564 PSIG WITHOUT INJECTION OF GAS, AROUND THE SAME TIME OF THIS INCIDENT. GULF SOUTH PULLED GAS OUT OF BOTH CAVERNS PGS 10 AND PGS 12A OVER THE NEXT SEVERAL DAYS WHILE STAYING IN CONTACT WITH ENTERPRISE AND ENTERPRISE'S PRESSURE STABILIZED AFTER DOING SO.      PER BOARDWALK'S (GULF SOUTH'S) WELL CONTROL ERP, GULF SOUTH DECLARED A LEVEL 2 WELL CONTROL INCIDENT ON 6/2/2023 AT APPROXIMATELY 7:00 AM, DOWNGRADED THE INCIDENT TO A LEVEL 1 ON 6/3/2023 AT 8:15 AM, AND CLOSED THE INCIDENT ON 6/7/2023 AT 9:15 AM.     ADDITIONALLY, OUT OF AN ABUNDANCE OF CAUTION, GULF SOUTH HAS PERFORMED A MECHANICAL INTEGRITY TEST ON CAVERN PGS 12A AS WELL AS MULTIPLE PRESSURE, TEMPERATURE, AND DENSITY LOGS ON BOTH CAVERNS.    THE RESPONSE TO QUESTION B10A OF THIS REPORT IS SHOWN AS, "ONE INCH DEPTH OF COVER." THE LIMITATIONS OF THE REPORTING SYSTEM PROHIBIT ENTRY OF AN ACCURATE RESPONSE. THE CAVERN ROOF OF PGS 10 IS 2,163 FEET (25,956 INCHES) AND PGS 12A IS 4,284 FEET (51,408 INCHES) BELOW THE SURFACE.    THE RESPONSE TO QUESTIONS C4 AND C5 REFLECTS THE COMPLETION DATE OF CAVERN PGS 10; IT IS THE EARLIER OF THE TWO CAVERN COMPLETION DATES. THE COMPLETION DATE OF PGS 12A IS 7/22/2008.    THE RESPONSE TO QUESTION D3 REPRESENTS THE PIR OF CAVERN PGS 12A (THE LARGER OF THE TWO MAOPS). ADDITIONALLY, THE MAOP OF PGS 10 IS 543 FEET.    THE RESPONSE TO QUESTION E2 REPRESENTS THE MAOP OF CAVERN PGS 10; ADDITIONALLY, THE MAOP OF CAVERN PGS 12A IS 3181 PSIG. THE RESPONSE TO QUESTION E2B SHOWS THE MAOP ESTABLISHED DATE FOR CAVERN PGS 10. ADDITIONALLY, THE MAOP ESTABLISHED DATE FOR PGS 12A IS 7/22/2013.    THE RESPONSE TO QUESTION E3 SHOWS THAT THE PRESSURE EXCEEDED THE APPLICABLE ALLOWANCE IN §192.201 BECAUSE THE MAOP WAS EXCEEDED AND THE SYSTEMS SELECTIONS ARE LIMITED; HOWEVER, THE MAOPS ARE NOT ESTABLISHED BY §192.201 BUT BY API RP 1170.

THE E&C TECHNICIAN IMMEDIATELY PERFORMED SITE SAFETY AWARENESS.    17:13; THE E&C TECHNICIAN MANUALLY ACTIVATED THE ESD SYSTEM AND THE FIRE SUBSIDED.    17:16; THE ESD ACTION WAS COMPLETE.  THE E&C TECHNICIAN ALLOWED THE LOCAL FIRE DEPARTMENT TO ENTER THE STATION AND STAGE ON THE BACKSIDE OF THE COMPRESSOR BUILDING.    17:17; THE E&C TECHNICIAN NOTICED THERE WAS A SMALL FLICKER OF FLAME COMING FROM THE GLYCOL DRAIN BARREL AND HEARD A NOISE HEARD COMING FROM THE PNEUMATIC DEVICES.     17:22; THE OPERATIONS SUPERVISOR, THE E&C TECHNICIAN, AND THE OPERATIONS TECHNICIAN DETERMINED THE NOISE WAS THE AIR SUPPLY TO THE VAPOR RECOVER UNIT (VRU) CONTROLS.  THE EMPLOYEES ENTERED THE DEHYDRATION AREA WITH HANDHELD FIRE EXTINGUISHERS TO EXTINGUISH ANY FLAME OR FIRE AT THE GLYCOL BARREL.      17:35; THE OPERATIONS SUPERVISOR REPORTED TO THE OPERATIONS MANAGER THAT SUBSTANTIAL DAMAGE HAD OCCURRED TO THE VRU UNIT AND DEHYDRATION SKID.    17:45; THE EMERGENCY RESPONSE LINE CALL, REQUIRED BY PROCEDURE OM 159, WAS CONDUCTED.  THE EVENT WAS DEEMED REPORTABLE TO THE NRC ON THE BASIS OF COSTS.  AT THIS TIME, THE SCENE WAS SECURED AND PRESERVED UNTIL A CORPORATE ROOT CAUSE ANALYSIS TEAM WAS DEPLOYED TO THE STATION.      INVESTIGATION CONFIRMED THE FOLLOWING:    NO PERSONNEL WERE ON SITE AT THE TIME OF THE EVENT AND THE DEHYDRATION UNIT WAS NOT IN GAS DRYING SERVICE BUT WAS IN STANDBY SERVICE AS THE STATION WAS INJECTING GAS INTO THE STORAGE FIELD.     WITH THE HIGH AMBIENT TEMPERATURE AND NO WITHDRAWAL FROM STORAGE OCCURRING, THE MAIN BURNER WOULD HAVE LITTLE NEED TO OPERATE.  WITHOUT THE MAIN BURNER OPERATING, ONLY PILOT FUEL GAS WOULD BE USED BY THE SYSTEM.  WITH NO OUTLET FOR FUEL GAS TO BE USED, THE CONTACTOR WOULD BE A SOURCE OF ADDITIONAL GAS PRESSURE TO THE SEPARATOR WHICH IN TURN FEEDS THE FUEL GAS TRAIN TO THE SECONDARY LIQUID KNOCKOUT VESSEL, THE LOCATION OF THE THERMAL RELIEF VALVE.  SAID THERMAL RELIEF VALVE, TYPICALLY SET AT 125 PSIG, ACTIVATED WITH THE VENT PIPING DIRECTING GAS TOWARDS THE GROUND WHICH CONTAINS GRAVEL AND OTHER MATERIAL WHICH MOST LIKELY CAUSED STATIC ELECTRICAL CHARGES CREATING THE IGNITION SOURCE.  OBSERVATION FOUND THE HISTORIC VENT PIPING FOR THE THERMAL RELIEF VALVE WAS TERMINATED APPROXIMATELY ONE (1) FOOT ABOVE GRADE SURFACE WHICH DOES NOT MEET CURRENT KINDER MORGAN DESIGN CRITERIA.      FLAME RETARDANT TARPS ARE USED FOR WINTER PROTECTION OF THE DEHYDRATION EQUIPMENT.  DUE TO WIND, THE TARP BY THE KNOCKOUT VESSEL CAUGHT ON FIRE.  16:17 DATA SCAN SUPPORTS A SMALL INCREASE IN GAS FLOW FROM THE THERMAL RELIEF VALVE AT THE KNOCKOUT VESSEL.  16:17, A DROP IN AIR PRESSURE WITHIN THE AIR SYSTEM INDICATED THE FIRE HAD SPREAD TO THE VRU UNIT.  FIRE SPREAD TO THE TARP BY THE SEPARATOR.  16:30 DATA SCAN IDENTIFIES A LARGER GAS FLOW INCREASE WHICH IS SUSPECTED TO BE THE FIRE DAMAGED 1-INCH RELIEF VALVE ON THE SEPARATOR.    STATION GAS FLOW CONTINUES TO BYPASS THE DEHYDRATION AREA UNTIL ALL REPAIRS AND MODIFICATIONS ARE COMPLETED.  ON OR BEFORE NOVEMBER 1, 2023, A REPLACEMENT DEHYDRATION EQUIPMENT SKID WILL BE INSTALLED, ANY RELATED VENTS WILL BE VERIFIED AS MEETING KINDER MORGAN DESIGN CRITERIA OR MODIFIED AS NEEDED, AND A DESIGN REVIEW WILL BE CONDUCTED OF POSSIBLE INSTALLATION OF PRESSURE LIMITING DEVICE SENSING PRESSURE TO THE DEHYDRATION SKID TO SHUT IN THE CONTACTOR AS NECESSARY.

THE COMMUNICATION WITH EMERGENCY RESPONDERS INDICATED ON QUESTION A17 WAS TO NOTIFY THE SHERIFF'S OFFICE THAT THE STATION PURGE WOULD BEGIN SOON; IT WAS NOT A NOTIFICATION DUE TO A FIRE OR ASSISTANCE NEEDED.    ON 5/21/23, THE REPAIR WAS COMPLETED BY REPLACING THE TUBING. THE AFFECTED UNIT WAS RESTARTED AT APPROXIMATELY 13:11.

ON APRIL 12, 2023, AT ABOUT 1420HRS OPERATIONS TECHNICIAN WAS CONTACTED BY A GUARD AT A NEIGHBORING ROAD CONCERNING A SOUND COMING FROM THE PEARSALL COMPRESSOR STATION.  THE TECHNICIAN NOTIFIED HCC OF THE REPORT AND HEADED TO THE STATION TO INVESTIGATE.    AT ABOUT 1517HRS, THE TECHNICIAN RECEIVED ADDITIONAL INFORMATION FROM THE GUARD AND NOTIFIED HCC WHO SHUT DOWN THE COMPRESSOR.      AT ABOUT 1630HRS, THE TECHNICIAN ARRIVED AT THE STATION AND CONFIRMED THE PSV ON UNIT 1 HAD RELIEVED. THE PSV WAS DISASSEMBLED, AND CONDENSATE WAS FOUND IN THE SENSING TUBE AND PILOT, CAUSING THE PSV TO LIFT PREMATURELY. THE PILOT WAS REBUILT USING NEW PARTS, AND A DRAIN LINE WITH A LIQUIDS TRAP WAS FITTED TO THE PILOT.    ON APRIL 13, AT 1623HRS, AFTER REVIEWING SCADA INFORMATION, ENTERPRISE DETERMINED THE RELIEF VALVE DISCHARGED 4.7 MMSCF OF NATURAL GAS, THUS, MEETING THE DEFINITION OF AN INCIDENT PER 49 CFR 191.3.      THE TRRC WAS NOTIFIED ON AT 1638HRS, INCIDENT NUMBER 2822.

THE FINAL LABORATORY ANALYSIS REPORT FROM DNV INDICATES THAT THE LEAK OCCURRED ON THE UPSTREAM GIRTH WELD ON THE ELBOW SIDE DUE TO INTERNAL CORROSION.  THE CORROSION WAS CONCENTRATED AT THE ELBOW FITTING AT THE HEAT AFFECTED ZONE OF THE GIRTH WELD.  EVIDENCE INDICATES THERE WAS A CONDUCTIVE ENVIRONMENT AT THE ELBOW FITTING GIRTH WELD DUE TO THE POTENTIAL FOR WATER TO ACCUMULATE, LOW PH, AND HIGH CHLORIDES.

ON 3/8/2023 WILLIAMS PIPELINE CONTROL WAS NOTIFIED BY A LANDOWNER OF A GAS SMELL NEAR HIS PROPERTY IN THE AREA OF A WILLIAMS PIPELINE. TECHNICIANS RESPONDED TO THE AREA AND BEGAN INVESTIGATING TO DETERMINE THE SOURCE OF THE SMELL. TECHNICIANS UTILIZED AN INFRARED LEAK DETECTION TOOL AND CONFIRMED A LEAK FROM THE PIPELINE. ONCE CONFIRMED THE PIPELINE WAS ISOLATED USING BLOCK VALVES AND THE GAS WAS EVACUATED FROM THE PIPE. AFTER GAS WAS REMOVED FROM THE SYSTEM AND THE LEAK WAS STOPPED, THE PIPELINE WAS EXCAVATED AND THE SOURCE OF THE LEAK WAS DETERMINED TO BE A CRACK ON MAINLINE B.     IN-FIELD HARDNESS WAS PERFORMED AT THE CRACK LOCATION TO CONFIRM A HARD SPOT DEFECT WAS PRESENT AT THE LOCATION OF THE CRACK. THE HARD SPOT MEASURED 364 BHN X 6.5" LONG X 6" WIDE.     ON OCTOBER 7, 2021 WILLIAMS CONTRACTED ROSEN TO INSPECT MAINLINE B (MLV 180B10 TO MLV 185B5) WITH THEIR HARD SPOT ILI (DMG) TECHNOLOGY TO ASSESS FOR THE HARD SPOT THREAT. THERE WERE A TOTAL OF 6 HARD SPOT ANOMALIES REPORTED BY ROSEN AND 4 OF THOSE 6 HARD SPOT FEATURES WERE EXCAVATED/EVALUATED FOR VERIFICATION. THE HARDNESS VALUES CONFIRMED FROM THESE 4 FEATURES RANGED FROM 192-208 BHN, WHICH WAS SLIGHTLY HARDER THAN BASE HARDNESS (~170-180 BHN). ALL 4 FEATURES WERE RECOATED PER WILLIAMS REPAIR PROCEDURE. THE HARD SPOT DEFECT THAT CRACKED (AND LEAKED) AT MP 1558.66 WAS NOT REPORTED BY ROSEN FROM THEIR 2021 HARD SPOT ILI. RE-ANALYSIS IS ONGOING WITH ROSEN BASED ON THE HARD SPOT DEFECT FOUND. LAB TESTING ON HARD SPOT WITH CRACK NOT YET COMPLETED AS PIPE WAS SENT TO TDW FOR PULL TESTING WITH THEIR HARD SPOT ILI TOOL TO VERIFY CAPABILITIES. WE HAVE NOT CONFIRMED HYDROGEN STRESS CRACKING.
cause: MATERIAL FAILURE OF PIPE OR WELD

text: ON MARCH 3, 2023 AT APPROXIMATELY 14:52, A NATURAL GAS RELEASE OCCURRED AT THE 20150013 ATHLON DISCHARGE 12-INCH PIG LAUNCHER SITE LOCATED 23 MILES SOUTHEAST OF ODESSA, TX IN MIDLAND COUNTY.    WHILE PREPARING TO LAUNCH A CLEANING PIG, THE OPERATOR MOVED ALL VALVES INVOLVED TO THEIR PROPER POSITIONS AS PER SOP. THE OPERATOR VISUALLY AND AUDIBLY WITNESSED THE PIG TRAP BLOW DOWN. ONCE THE PIG TRAP WAS COMPLETELY BLOWN DOWN THE OPERATOR BEGAN TO OPEN THE PIG TRAP DOOR AS PER SOP. THE OPERATOR WALKED AWAY FROM THE PIG TRAP DOOR TO RETRIEVE THE CLEANING PIG FROM HIS TRUCK AND HEARD A HISSING SOUND COMING FROM THE PIG TRAP. THE HISSING SOUND WAS GROWING LOUDER AND THE OPERATOR REMOVED HIMSELF FROM THE AREA TO BE SAFE. THAT IS WHEN THE GAS PRESSURE CAUSED THE PIG TRAP DOOR TO OPEN CAUSING THE RELEASE OF GAS FROM THE 16-INCH PIG TRAP DOOR.     AT APPROXIMATELY 16:35, IT WAS CALCULATED AND CONFIRMED THAT THE UNINTENTIONAL GAS LOSS WAS AT 3.69 MMCF, WHICH EXCEEDED THE 3 MMCF REPORTING CRITERIA AND THE NRC WAS NOTIFIED AT 16:49.    THE BETTIS ACTUATOR AND VERSE VALVE WERE REMOVED AND SENT FOR INSPECTION AND REPAIRS.      A NEW MANUAL GEAR OPERATOR WAS INSTALLED AND AT 14:00 ON 04MAR THE PIPELINE WAS PUT BACK INTO SERVICE.    **JUNE 1, 2023, IT WAS DETERMINED THAT THE 1-INCH MAIN LINE SUPPLY GAS BALL VALVE WAS LEAKING BY AND LIKELY RE-SUPPLIED THE ACTUATOR ASSEMBLY WITH ENOUGH PRESSURE TO ACTUATE THE VALVE OPEN ALLOWING GAS TO RE-ENTER THE PIG LAUNCHING BARREL THUS CAUSING THE UNINTENTIONAL GAS RELEASE.    THE LEAKING 1-INCH BALL VALVE WAS REPLACED WITH A NEW ONE.      THIS WAS AN ISOLATED INCIDENT AND TO PREVENT THIS FROM OCCURRING IN THE FUTURE AND THIS SITE, THE ACTUATORS WERE REMOVED AND REPLACED WITH MANUAL GEAR OPERATORS.     THE SITE SPECIFIC PIGGING PROCEDURES HAVE BEEN UPDATED TO INCLUDE AREAS WITH ACTUATORS TO LOCK OUT THE SUPPLY SOURCE BLOWDOWN VALVE IN THE OPEN POSITION IN CASE THERE IS A LEAKING VALVE AND TO PREVENT GAS FROM RE-ENTERING THE PIG LAUNCHER BARREL.

AT 10:09AM MST ON FEBRUARY 5, 2023, A FAULTY HAZARDOUS GAS DETECTOR IN THE CONTROL ROOM OF EL PASO NATURAL GAS (EPNG) EUNICE B COMPRESSOR STATION CAUSED THE COMPRESSOR STATION TO UNDERGO AN EMERGENCY SHUTDOWN (ESD). DURING THE SHUTDOWN, SUCTION VALVE VB1 DID NOT CLOSE FULLY CAUSING GAS TO CONTINUE TO VENT. THIS LED TO A RELEASE OF 5,459 MCF GAS RELEASE. AT 11:03AM, AN EPNG EMPLOYEE ARRIVED AT SITE, CLOSED THE VALVE, STOPPING THE GAS RELEASE, AND RETURNED THE STATION TO NORMAL OPERATION. THERE WERE NO INJURIES OR FATALITIES. THE INVESTIGATION INTO THIS VALVE MALFUNCTION DETERMINED THAT THERE WAS FLAWED PROGRAMMING IN THE PLC LOGIC WHICH HAS BEEN RESOLVED.

ON FEBRUARY 4, 2023, AN UNINTENTIONAL RELEASE OF 6.7 MILLION CUBIC FEET OF NATURAL GAS OCCURRED WHEN A 2-INCH 2-PIECE, THREADED VALVE PULLED APART, ON THE HIGH-PRESSURE DUMP LINE ON THE WELL HEAD SEPARATOR. A TECHNICIAN WAS NEARBY AT THE TIME OF THE RELEASE. NO INJURIES, NO FATALITIES AND NO DAMAGES WERE REPORTED.      THE ISOLATION PLAN GENERATED FOR THE SECTION REQUIRED LATERAL VALVES TO BE CLOSED AND THE RELEASE WAS ISOLATED WITHIN 78 MINUTES. AFTER THE NATURAL GAS RELEASE, THERE WAS A SMALL RELEASE OF CRUDE OIL THAT IS A BYPRODUCT OF THE STORAGE WELL SYSTEM. A PRIMARY CAUSE OF THE EQUIPMENT FAILURE HAS YET TO BE DETERMINED AS THE INCIDENT IS CURRENTLY UNDER INVESTIGATION.  A SUPPLEMENT REPORT WILL BE FILED UPON THE COMPLETION OF THE INVESTIGATION.       UPDATE 7/3/2023 FAILURE INVESTIGATION FINAL SUMMARY REPORT     THE RESULTS OF THE ANALYSIS INDICATE THAT THE BALL VALVE AND THREADED CONNECTION FAILED DUE TO EXPANSION OF THE FEMALE THREADED SECTION ON THE BALL VALVE, MOST LIKELY AS A RESULT OF WATER FREEZING INSIDE THE VALVE. THE EXPANSION LED TO PARTIAL DISENGAGEMENT OF THE MALE THREADS ON THE THREADED CONNECTION AND THE FEMALE THREADS ON THE VALVE BODY. AN AXIL TENSILE STRESS, LIKELY FROM THE FREEZING WATER ACTING ON THE VALVE AND THREADED CONNECTION RESULTED IN DEFORMATION OF THE OF MALE THREADS FROM THE THREADED CONNECTIONS. WHICH SEPARATED THE VALVE BODY FROM THE MALE THREADED CONNECTION.

ON JANUARY 16, 2023, AT APPROXIMATELY 07:00, A FLORIDA GAS TRANSMISSION TECHNICIAN DISCOVERED A COMPRESSOR UNIT VENT VALVE WAS VENTING NATURAL GAS TO ATMOSPHERE AT THE COMPRESSOR STATION 24, NEAR TRENTON, FL. THE TECHNICIAN ISOLATED THE COMPRESSOR AT APPROXIMATELY 0730 HRS. ACCORDING TO COMPANY SCADA, THE VENT VALVE HAD BEGUN VENTING AT APPROXIMATELY 13:00 ON JANUARY 15, 2023, BUT NO OTHER SCADA ALARMS WERE TRIGGERED. THE UNIT WAS SHUT DOWN REMOTELY BY GAS CONTROL AT 11:00 ON JANUARY 15, 2023. THE COMPRESSOR UNIT AUTOMATICALLY VENTS AFTER TWO (2) HOURS OF SHUTDOWN. THE SHUTDOWN AND ALL VALVE POSITIONS INDICATED CLOSURE; THEREFORE, NO ALARMS WERE TRIGGERED.    THE VOLUME RELEASED WAS CALCULATED TO BE APPROXIMATELY 102.6 MMSCF NATURAL GAS. THE DETERMINATION TIME FOR THIS ESTIMATE WAS APPROXIMATELY 14:52 ON JANUARY 16, 2023, WHICH WAS FOLLOWED BY THE NRC NOTIFICATION THAT OCCURRED AT APPROXIMATELY 15:44.    THE CAUSE OF THE INCIDENT WAS LATER CONFIRMED TO BE A SUCTION SIDE ISOLATION VALVE NOT FULLY SEATING AFTER THE COMPRESSOR UNIT WAS SHUTDOWN. SPECIFICALLY, IT APPEARS THAT THE VALVE ACTUATOR MALFUNCTIONED RESULTING IN THE VALVE NOT FULLY SEATING, THEREBY ALLOWING PIPELINE PRESSURE TO BLEED BY INTO THE COMPRESSOR UNIT CAUSING THE NATURAL GAS TO BE VENTED TO ATMOSPHERE. THE SUCTION SIDE VALVE WAS FULLY CLOSED MANUALLY BY THE TECHNICIAN TO STOP FLOW OF GAS THROUGH THE COMPRESSOR. THE LOGIC TO ALLOW MORE TIME FOR VALVE CLOSURE WAS DEVELOPED AND INSTALLED THE DAY OF THE RCFA INVESTIGATION TO PREVENT RECURRENCE.
