THE REVISED REPORT COLLECTS DATA ABOUT THE PIPE ADJACENT TO THE GIRTH WELD. (2) ``FUNCTION OF PIPELINE SYSTEM'' IS NULL IN PART E5F OF THE REPORT. THE REVISED REPORT COLLECTS THE FUNCTION OF THE PIPELINE SYSTEM FOR ALL INCIDENTS.**    THIS SUPPLEMENTAL REPORT IS TO ACKNOWLEDGE THAT THE TWO RELEVANT SECTIONS IN PHMSA'S REQUEST HAVE BEEN REVIEWED AND NO FURTHER ACTIONS WERE NEEDED.

A MEMBER OF THE GENERAL PUBLIC NOTIFIED SOUTHERN NATURAL GAS (SNG) COMPANY'S GAS CONTROL OF A LOUD BLOWING SOUND IN THE VICINITY OF SNG'S LIVINSTON (AL) REGULATOR STATION.  UPON ARRIVAL AT THE SCENE, SNG OPERATIONS PERSONNEL FOUND THE REGULATOR STATION BUILDING AND PIPING ENGULFED IN FLAMES.  SURROUNDING GRASS WAS ALSO BURNING.  PERSONNEL CLOSED THE STATION'S TAP VALVES TO STOP FUEL FLOW TO THE FIRE.  LOCAL VOLUNTEER FIREMEN ASSISTED THE COMPANY PERSONNEL IN EXTINGUISHING THE FIRE.  TEMPORARY SERVICE WAS RESTORED TO THE TOWN OF LIVINGSTON. POST INCIDENT INVESTIGATION REVEALED THE MOST LIKELY CAUSE TO BE A CONCENTRATION OF NATURAL GAS, VENTED FROM CONTROL EQUIPMENT DESIGNED TO DO SO, INSIDE THE REGULATOR BUILDING DUE TO LACK OF VENTILATION.  THE GAS IGNITED FROM AN UNKNOWN SOURCE ALTHOUGH POSSIBLE SOURCES COULD HAVE BEEN AN ELECTRICAL SHORT OR LIGHTNING.

text: TUBING FITTING BECAME LOOSE ALLOWING COOLANT TO DRIP ONTO TURBO AND EXHAUST PIPING RESULTING IN A SMALL FIRE. THE FIRE WAS IMMEDIATELY EXTENGUISHED BY LOCAL EMPLOYEE AND SHUT DOWN ENGINE.  LEAKING FITTING WAS REPAIRED AND UNIT # 10 WAS RETURNED TO SERVICE WITHIN 3 HOURS OF SHUTTING DOWN UNIT.

THE PIPELINE CROSSES PROPERTY USED AS A LANDFILL.  THE NORMAL LANDFILL ACTIVITY WAS NOT ON THE PIPELINE RIGHTS-OF-WAY.  PIPELINE IS MARKED AND PROPERTY OWNERS ARE AWARE OF IT'S LOCATION.  PROPERTY OWNERS HAD STACKED TREE TRUNKS AND LIMBS ON THE ROW.  LANDOWNERS WERE MOVING THE DEBRIS OFF THE ROW USING BULLDOZERS.  PIPE COVER WAS REMOVED WHILE THE DEBRIS WAS BEING PUSHED INTO PILES.  BECAUSE OF THE REDUCED COVER, THE PIPE WAS FLATTENED BY THE DOZER TRACKS.  A NEIGHBOR HEARD THE RUPTURE AND CALLED A BWP EMPLOYEE, WHO DETERMINED THE RUPTURE WAS ON THE GULF SOUTH SYSTEM.

ETC EXPERIENCED A RUPTURE ON THE 36" OASIS PIPELINE IN A RURAL (CLASS I) AREA IN AUSTIN COUNTY, TX ON JULY 28, 2010.  THE LINE IS AN INTRASTATE NATURAL GAS TRANSMISSION PIPELINE UNDER THE JURISDICTION OF THE TEXAS RAILROAD COMMISSION.      THE INCIDENT WAS REPORTED TO THE TRRC UNDER INCIDENT ID: 551 AND ALSO TO THE NRC UNDER ID: 949134.  THROUGH A THOROUGH EXAMINATION, BY THIRD PARTY, KIEFNER & ASSOCIATES,  AND THROUGH MAG-PARTICLE TESTING,  STRESS CORROSION CRACKING (SCC) WAS DETERMINED TO HAVE BEEN INVOLVED. METALURGICAL  LAB ANALYSIS WILL BE PERFORMED ON THE FAILED SECTION OF PIPE AND WILL PROVIDE FURTHER DETAILED INFORMATION.    TO DATE, ETC HAS COMPLETED HYDROSTATIC TESTING OF APPROXIMATELY 30.5 MILES WITHIN THE AREA OF THE INITIAL IN SERVICE FAILURE.  THE TESTING CONSISTED OF FOUR TEST SECTIONS RUNNING EAST TO WEST FROM THE BRAZOS RIVER (STA. 2950+00) TO 4.5 MILES WEST OF MLV2 (STA. 4560+00). EACH TEST SECTION WAS TESTED TO A MINIMUM OF 100% SMYS FOR ONE HOUR AND THEN A SUBSEQUENT LEAK TEST AT 90% SMYS FOR A MINIMUM OF 8 HRS WITHOUT PRESSURE LOSS. SECTION 1 AND 4 SUCCESSFULLY PASSED THEIR INITIAL TESTS, SECTION 2 HAD TWO FAILURES AND SECTION 3 HAD 3 FAILURES BEFORE ACHIEVING A SUCCESSFUL TEST. IT SHOULD BE NOTED, THAT OF THE 5 FAILURES THAT OCCURRED DURING THE TESTING, THE MINIMUM FAILURE PRESSURE OCCURRED AT 84% OF SMYS INDICATING THERE WERE NO OTHER CRITICAL CRACKS THAT WOULD HAVE FAILED AT OPERATING PRESSURE.      BASED ON THE RESULTS OF THE HYDROSTATIC TESTING, AND INTEGRATION OF INFORMATION OBTAINED FROM THE RUPTURE SITE, SOIL RESISTIVITY SURVEYS AND SUBSEQUENT EXCAVATIONS, ETC FEELS THAT ALL OF THE SCC COLONIES OF A CRITICAL SIZE WERE LOCATED WITHIN THE SECTION OF LINE BETWEEN MLV1 TO MLV2. PLANS ARE TO REINSTORE SERVICE ON OR AROUND SEPTEMBER 1, 2010 AND SUBSEQUENTLY RUNNING THE EMAT CRACK DETECTION TOOL FROM OUR PRAIRIE LEE COMPRESSOR STATION TO KATY, APPROXIMATELY 113 MILES, TO FURTHER CONFIRM OUR FINDINGS AND FURTHER DEVELOP OUR OVERALL MITIGATION PLAN FOR THIS THREAT.     FINAL UPDATE 08/26/2013:  AFTER A THOROUGH METALLURGICAL EXAMINATION, PERFORMED BY KIEFNER AND ASSOCIATES, INC, THE FAILURE WAS MOST LIKELY DETERMINED TO BE CAUSED BY HIGH PH TYPE SCC IN THE BODY OF THE PIPE.   THIS DETERMINATION WAS BASED UPON PIPE-TO-SOIL POTENTIAL, SOIL RESISTIVITY, AND PH MEASUREMENTS AS WELL AS METALLOGRAPHIC SECTIONS THROUGH ADJACENT IN THE COLONY

A LANDOWNER CALLED ONEOK GAS TRANSPORTATION GAS CONTROL TO REPORT A NATURAL GAS LEAK ON THE 24 INCH A-1300 NATURAL GAS PIPELINE NEAR THE LITTLE RIVER IN CLEVELAND COUNTY OKLAHOMA AT APPROXIMATELY 2330 HOURS ON THURSDAY JULY 15, 2010.  ONEOK GAS TRANSPORTATION FIELD PERSONNEL WERE CONTACTED AND WERE ON THE SCENE BY 2355 HOURS.  THERE WAS NO EXPLOSION, NO FIRE, NO INJURIES, AND NO DEATHS.  THE LOCAL FIRE DEPARTMENT DID COME OUT TO THE SITE BUT DID NOT REMAIN ON SCENE.  THE OKLAHOMA CORPORATION COMMISSION WAS NOTIFIED VIA TELEPHONE AT 0155 HOURS ON FRIDAY JULY 16, 2010.  THE NATIONAL RESPONSE CENTER WAS CONTACTED AT 0257 HOURS ON FRIDAY JULY 16, 2010.  THE NRC INCIDENT NUMBER IS 947893.  THE A-1300 SEGMENT WHERE THE LEAK WAS LOCATED WAS ISOLATED BY CLOSING THE HIGHWAY 102 BLOCK VALVE AND THE LEXINGTON TAKE OFF VALVE.  THE 13.3 MILES OF PIPELINE AROUND THE LEAK WAS ISOLATED BY 0227 HOURS ON FRIDAY JULY 16, 2010.  THE LINE WAS ALLOWED TO BLOW DOWN AND THE SITE SECURED BY 0630 HOURS.  THREE TV STATION CREWS WERE IN THE AREA FOR A SHORT PERIOD OF TIME AND THEY WERE BRIEFED ON THE SITUATION.  APPROXIMATELY 10 FARM TAP CUSTOMERS WERE IMPACTED AND SERVICE TO THE TOWN OF LITTLE AXE, OKLAHOMA WAS PUT ON A CASCADE SYSTEM BY OKLAHOMA NATURAL GAS.  CLOSER EXAMINATION OF THE INCIDENT SITE REVEALED A 30 FOOT DIAMETER CRATER WHERE A DRIP WAS LOCATED.  REPAIR CONSISTED OF REPLACING 63 FEET OF A-1300 PIPELINE INCLUDING REMOVAL OF THE DRIP WITH 24 INCH 0.375 WALL THICKNESS X-60 GRADE PRETESTED PIPE.  THE PIPELINE WAS PUT BACK INTO NORMAL SERVICE AT 1530 HOURS ON SATURDAY JULY 17, 2010.  FIELD ASSESSMENT INDICATES A MATERIAL FAILURE OF THE 2 INCH BALON VALVE(S) LOCATED ON THE DRIP AS THE CAUSE OF THE INCIDENT.  THESE VALVES WERE IN SERVICE IN A DAMP AND / OR WET ENVIRONMENT.  IT APPEARS VALVE BODY AND / OR BOLT HAD CORROSION ISSUES WHICH LEAD TO VALVE FAILURE.  THERE WAS ADEQUATE CATHODIC PROTECTION ON THE PIPELINE AND DRIP.

A THIRD PARTY PLATFORM OPERATOR OBSERVED BUBBLES ON THE SURFACE IN THE GULF OF MEXICO IN WEST CAMERON BLOCK 513 ABOUT 100 MILES SOUTH OF CAMERON, LOUISIANA.  ON JUNE 20, 2010, SPECTRA ENERGY PERSONNEL CONFIRMED THE NATURAL GAS LEAK WAS ON THE TEXAS EASTERN TRANSMISSION, LP 20-INCH LINE 41-A-6.  THE WATER DEPTH AT THE LEAK SITE WAS APPROXIMATELY 165 FEET.  AFTER CONCRETE COATING WAS REMOVED, THE SOURCE OF THE LEAK WAS DETERMINED TO BE A PIN HOLE IN THE PIPE WALL.  ULTRASONIC TESTING RESULTS SHOWED NO WALL LOSS OUTSIDE THE IMMEDIATE AREA OF THE PIN HOLE.  THE MOST LIKELY CAUSE OF THE LEAK WAS DETERMINED TO BE INTERNAL CORROSION NEAR A GIRTH WELD.

ON THE MARCH 25, 2010 DAMAGE TO THE 12-INCH EAST TENNESSEE NATURAL GAS (OPID #04070) LINE 3307B-100 NEAR KINGSPORT, TENNESSEE (NATIONAL RESPONSE CENTER REPORT #935074) WAS DISCOVERED. text: A FIRE OCCURRED AT APPROXIMATELY 1230 HOURS ON 3/5/10 AT THE LINE 114 DEHYDRATOR STATION NEAR RIO VISTA.  DUE TO A DEHYDRATOR UPSET FROM AN UPSTREAM GAS SUPPLIER (VENOCO) LARGER THAN NORMAL QUANTITIES OF FLAMMABLE PIPELINE LIQUIDS WERE INTRODUCED INTO THE PG&E DEHYDRATOR.  THE EXTRA LIQUIDS TRAVELED THROUGH THE CONTACT TOWER, OVERWHELMING THE VAPOR RECOVERY SYSTEM AND EVENTUALLY REACHED THE REBOILER NATURAL GAS FIRED BURNER WHERE THE LIQUIDS IGNITED.  PROPERTY DAMAGES WERE APPROXIMATELY $50,000.  THERE WERE NO FATALITIES AND NO INJURIES. AT APPROXIMATELY 08:18 HRS ON FEBRUARY 22, A FIELD EMPLOYEE WAS PERFORMING ANNUAL VALVE MAINTENANCE ON AUXILIARY VALVE ON CEGT LINE AD-WEST. ON THURSDAY FEBRUARY 19TH WE DISCOVERED THAT THE ROOF DRAIN SYSTEM HAD FAILED TO KEEP CONTAINMENT OF PRODUCT LOCATED INSIDE TANK 223 WHICH LED TO A SUBSEQUENT RELEASE OF APPROXIMATELY 5,400 BARRELS INTO THE TANK 223 DIKE CONTAINMENT AREA.     OUR TEAM STARTED THE PROPER NOTIFICATION PROCESS IMMEDIATELY AND WORKED TO RECLAIM THE RELEASED PRODUCT. ONCE THE SPILL RESPONSE WAS COMPLETED, WE STRIPPED THE REMAINING PRODUCT OUT OF TANK 223 BACK TO THE CENOVUS REFINERY AND COMMENCED THE TANK CLEANING EFFORT SO THE INVESTIGATION TEAM COULD MAKE ENTRY TO THE TANK TO ASSESS WHAT MAY HAVE CAUSED THE FAILURE. THE INVESTIGATION TEAM PERFORMED THEIR INSPECTION AND FOUND A COUPLE OF FACTORS THAT PLAYED A ROLE IN THE ROOF DRAIN SYSTEM LOSING CONTAINMENT OF THE PRODUCT INSIDE OF TANK 223. THE INVESTIGATION TEAM FOUND THERE WAS AN INCOMPLETE WELD IN THE ROOF DRAIN PIPE THAT CONNECTS THE CHECK VALVE TO THE INTERNAL ROOF DRAIN SYSTEM.     ONCE THE ROOF DRAIN WAS CLOSED FOR THE WINTER SEASON, A BUILD UP OF ICE PUSHED THE CHECK VALVE UP AND OUT OF ITS NORMAL HORIZONTAL POSITION, LIKELY CAUSING STRESS ON THE WELD AND IN TURN ALLOWING WATER TO FLOW INTO THE CLOSED ROOF DRAIN SYSTEM. SUBSEQUENTLY, THE WATER FREEZING IN THE INTERNAL ROOF DRAIN PIPING CAUSED TWO OF THE FOUR PIVOT JOINTS IN THE ROOF DRAIN PIPING TO EXPAND AND LEAD TO A FAILURE IN THOSE TWO FLEXIBLE JOINTS ALLOWING PRODUCT FROM THE TANK TO EXIT OUT OF THE ROOF DRAIN SYSTEM INTO THE TANK 223 DIKE AREA.
cause: MATERIAL FAILURE OF PIPE OR WELD

THE SPOOL WHERE THE PINHOLE DEVELOPED WAS IDENTIFIED AS AN OPERATIONAL DEAD LEG, AND THE COMBINATION OF STAGNANT CONDITIONS AND PRODUCT CONTRIBUTED TO ACCELERATED CORROSION. INCIDENT/ ACCIDENT DESCRIPTION:    THIRD PARTY NOTIFIED OPERATIONS OF A POTENTIAL RELEASE AT THE BRAZOS METER STATION. UPON ARRIVAL, IT WAS DISCOVERED THAT THE FLAPPER PIN WAS NO LONGER PRESENT IN THE CHECK VALVE, RESULTING IN A RELEASE OF Y-GRADE. text: OPERATIONS PERSONNEL DISCOVERED A HAZARDOUS LIQUID RELEASE WHILE PERFORMING A ROUTINE INSPECTION WITHIN SUNOCO'S COLORADO SPRINGS TERMINAL TANK 30M-3 IMPOUNDMENT.  THE CONTENTS OF THE TANK, JET A TURBINE FUEL, WERE REMOVED, AND THE TANK APPURTENANCES WERE SEALED.  THE SOURCE OF THE RELEASE IS UNDER INVESTIGATION.  UPDATE: A THROUGH-WALL FEATURE WAS DISCOVERED WITHIN A FLOOR PLATE ON THE EAST SIDE OF TK-30M-3 DURING AN INTEGRITY TEST.  THE PLATE CONTAINING THE FEATURE WAS REMOVED AND SENT FOR ANALYSIS TO DETERMINE THE CAUSE OF FAILURE.  UPDATE – THE CAUSE OF THE LEAK WAS A LOCALIZED THICKNESS REDUCTION AND THROUGH-HOLE ON THE INNER WALL SURFACE OF 0.073 INCHES IN DIAMETER. THE LEAK WAS FOUND IN PLATE 24, 18.75 INCHES FROM THE NEAREST ADJACENT FLOOR PLATE WELD, AND 107 INCHES FROM THE SHELL. THE FEATURE WAS IDENTIFIED ONLY AFTER THE REMOVAL OF THE TANK LINER AND PERFORMANCE OF A HELIUM TEST. THE INNER SURFACE WALL LOSS MECHANISM COULD NOT BE DETERMINED. DEFINITIVE IDENTIFICATION WAS LIMITED BY THE ABRASIVE-BLASTED CONDITION OF THE SURFACE FOLLOWING THE LINING REMOVAL, WHICH WAS NECESSARY TO FIND THE ANOMALY. POTENTIAL FAILURE SCENARIOS WERE CONSIDERED. THESE INCLUDED A CORROSION DRIVEN MECHANISM ORIGINATING BENEATH THE INTERNAL LINING AND TANK SURFACE DUE TO A DEFECT IN THE LINING AS WELL AS MOISTURE ENTRAPMENT BETWEEN THE LINING AND TANK SURFACE INTERFACE. THE PRESENCE OF A PRE-EXISTING DEFECT THAT PROPAGATED OVER TIME WAS ALSO CONSIDERED. NO INHERENT MATERIAL DEFICIENCIES OR OUTER WALL CORROSION MECHANISMS WERE IDENTIFIED AS CONTRIBUTORS TO THE FAILURE.

ON 12/17/25 AT APPROXIMATELY MIDNIGHT, THE CONTROL ROOM OBSERVED AN OVERPRESSURE EVENT AND RECEIVED A LEAK WARNING ON THE 23034 – 10” PLAINS BASIN LINE. THE LINE WAS IMMEDIATELY SHUTDOWN AND FIELD OPERATIONS CONFIRMED A CRUDE OIL LEAK AT THE MIDLAND PLAINS BASIN MANIFOLD. THE LEAK WAS COMING FROM A FAILED FLANGE.     APPROXIMATELY 660 BARRELS OF CRUDE OIL WAS RELEASED INTO CONTAINMENT. CLEANUP CONTRACTORS REMOVED PRODUCT AND REMEDIATED IMPACTED SOIL.    THE LEAK WAS REPAIRED BY REPLACING GASKET AND BOLTS.     THE CAUSE OF THE ACCIDENT IS STILL UNDER INVESTIGATION. A SUPPLEMENTAL REPORT WILL BE SUBMITTED ONCE COMPLETE.    SUPPLEMENTAL & FINAL:  THE INVESTIGATION DETERMINED THE ACCIDENT WAS CAUSED BY INCORRECT OPERATIONS RESULTING IN AN OVERPRESSURE. FOLLOWING OUTBOUND COMMISSIONING CHECKS FIELD OPERATORS DID NOT RETURN VALVES TO THE CLOSED POSITION, LOCK OUT/TAG OUT WAS NOT PERFORMED, AND A MECHANICAL VALVE WAS NOT FULLY SEATED ALLOWING PRODUCT TO FLOW, OVERPRESSURE A FLANGE CONNECTION AND RELEASE CRUDE OIL.     TO PREVENT REOCCURRENCE, EXPAND COMMISSIONED AND NON-COMMISSIONED SYSTEM COMMUNICATION TO INCLUDE USING POSITIVE ISOLATION FOR NON-COMMISSIONED PARTS OF SYSTEMS AND VALVE MECHANICAL SEATING CHECKS DURING COMMISSIONING. ADDITIONALLY, OPERATIONAL STAFF TRAINING WILL INCLUDE DETAILS IN THE JOB PLAN FOR VALVE POSITION UPON COMPLETION OF A MECHANICAL SEAT CHECK OR POINT TO POINT CHECK.

ON DECEMBER 8, 2025, AT APPROXIMATELY 9:27 AM CST, TECHNICIANS DRIVING BY TANK 2521 AT GRANDSTAFF TERMINAL OBSERVED PRODUCT AROUND THE DISCHARGE LINE OF THE TANK. THE CUSHING CONTROL CENTER WAS NOTIFIED, AND THE TANK LINE WAS ISOLATED AND DRAINED TO INVESTIGATE THE SOURCE OF THE RELEASE. ADDITIONAL EQUIPMENT AND RESOURCES WERE MOBILIZED TO ASSIST WITH EXCAVATION AND CLEANUP OF THE AREA. AT APPROXIMATELY 12:50 PM CST, IT WAS DETERMINED THAT COSTS WOULD EXCEED THE NRC REPORTING THRESHOLD DUE TO THE EXTENT OF EXCAVATION NEEDED TO FIND THE SOURCE OF THE RELEASE. THE NRC WAS NOTIFIED AT 1:04 PM CST (NRC # 1449809). EXCAVATION AND CLEANUP CONTINUED UNTIL THE SOURCE OF THE RELEASE WAS IDENTIFIED AS A PINHOLE AT THE 6 O’CLOCK POSITION. A TEMPORARY REPAIR CLAMP WAS INSTALLED, AND CLEANUP EFFORTS WERE COMPLETED. THE 48-HOUR NRC UPDATE WAS MADE ON DECEMBER 10, 2025, AT 11:19 AM CST (NRC # 1449988).    THE FAILURE WAS ATTRIBUTED TO INTERNAL CORROSION ON A SECTION OF THE TANK LINE PIPING. THIS CORROSION RESULTED IN A 3/16-INCH HOLE, WHICH ALLOWED PRODUCT TO MIGRATE ALONG THE PIPE AND SURFACE NEAR THE 90-DEGREE BEND BEFORE FLOWING ABOVE GRADE ALONG THE TRUNK LINE PATH. THE INITIAL ESTIMATE WAS APPROXIMATELY 25 GALLONS, LATER REVISED TO 39 GALLONS FOLLOWING CLEANUP AND REMEDIATION EFFORTS.     PLANNING IS CURRENTLY UNDERWAY FOR THE EXECUTION OF A PERMANENT REPAIR IN FIRST QUARTER OF 2026.

DURING FACILITY INSPECTIONS ON 12/3/25 OPERATIONS DISCOVERED PRODUCT SEEPING FROM THE CHIME ON TANK 369. OPERATIONS BEGAN TRANSFERRING PRODUCT OUT OF THE TANK TO RELIEVE PRESSURE. ONCE THE LEAK STOPPED, TANK 369 WAS EMPTIED AND PREPPED FOR ENTRY. ONEOK'S TANK INTEGRITY GROUP IS CURRENTLY CONDUCTING AN INVESTIGATION INTO THE CAUSE OF THE RELEASE. ONCE THE CAUSE IS DETERMINED, A SUPPLEMENTAL REPORT WILL BE SUBMITTED.    SUPPLEMENTAL- THE RELEASE ON 12/3/25 WAS DUE TO SOIL SIDE CORROSION OF THE TANK BOTTOM STEEL.  A TANK FLOOR COUPON WAS CUT OUT NEAR WHERE THE TANK BOTTOM FAILURE AREA AND VISUALLY INSPECTED WITH CORROSION PIT MORPHOLOGY CONSISTENT WITH MIC (MICROBIAL INDUCED CORROSION).  SAND SAMPLES WERE TAKEN FROM UNDERNEATH THE TANK AND ANALYZED WHICH IDENTIFIED BACTERIAL COLONIES.  THE CP SYSTEM OPERATIONAL RECORDS WERE REVIEWED WITH NO CONCERNS NOTED.  ADDITIONAL CP READINGS WERE TAKEN WHERE THE TANK BOTTOM COUPONS WERE CUT OUT, AND RESULTS WERE ALL WITHIN THE EXPECTED RANGE. AT THIS TIME TANK 369 REMAINS OUT OF SERVICE. A NEW DOUBLE BOTTOM WILL BE INSTALLED.  THIS WILL SEPARATE THE NEW BOTTOM FROM THE EXISTING BOTTOM AND SAND/SOIL UNDERNEATH WITH AN HDPE LINER AND APPROXIMATELY 4” OF CONCRETE. REPAIRS ARE ANTICIPATED TO BE COMPLETED IN EARLY 2027. ONCE REPAIRS ARE COMPLETED A SUPPLEMENTAL FINAL WILL BE SUBMITTED.

ON OCTOBER 30, 2025, A FIRE OCCURRED AT THE CAPROCK METER STATION, 5.65 MILES NORTHWEST OF BARSTOW, TX IN WARD COUNTY.  AT APPROXIMATELY 1030, THE CONTROL CENTER LOSS COMMUNICATION WITH THE CAPROCK METER STATION.  WHEN OPERATIONS PERSONNEL ARRIVED THE MCC BUILDING HAD CAUGHT FIRE AND WAS ALMOST EXTINGUISHED.  BY THE TIME THE FIRE DEPARTMENT ARRIVED THE FIRE HAD EXTINGUISHED, AND THE FIRE FIGHTERS DELUGED THE BUILDING WITH WATER TO KEEP FROM RE-IGNITING.  THE STATION WAS SHUT IN.  AT 1430, IT WAS DETERMINED THAT THE THERMAL RELIEF VALVE RELEASED NGL THAT BLEW INTO THE MCC BUILDING'S HVAC, WHICH THEN WAS IGNITED AND CAUGHT THE MCC BUILDING ON FIRE.  NO DAMAGE OCCURRED ON THE PIPELINE.  THE STATION IS STILL SHUTDOWN.  A SUPPLEMENTAL REPORT WILL BE SUBMITTED ONCE BACK ONLINE.  ON NOVEMBER 28, 2025, AT APPROXIMATELY 14:07 THE PIPELINE WAS STARTED UP.  **THE RESULT CONCLUDED THE ROOT CAUSE WAS THAT THE THERMAL RELIEF VALVE WENT OFF AS INTENDED.  THE HALF INCH BY ONE-INCH THERMAL RELIEF HAD A NIPPLE AND A 90 ON THE EXHAUST PORT WHICH INITIALLY HAD THE LIQUID STREAM DISBURSING UPWARD. HOWEVER, THE EXHAUST NIPPLE HAD A 45-DEGREE CUT AT THE END OF THE NIPPLE AND CREATED ANOTHER EVENT. IT CREATED ENOUGH FORCE TO UNSCREW THE EXHAUST PIPING AND EVENTUALLY FELL OFF AND CHANGED THE STREAM DIRECTION FROM UPWARD TO HORIZONAL. THIS RESULTED IN THE HALF INCH NIPPLE CRACKING AT THE THREADS DUE TO THE FORCE AND DIRECTION CHANGE.  THE OPP AND THE THERMAL RELIEF VALVE WERE BOTH SET AT 1440.  THE 880 PRESSURE WAS THE LAST RECORDED PRESSURE PRIOR TO LOSING COMMUNICATIONS.  TO PREVENT THIS FROM REOCCURRING, OPERATIONS HAS RESET THE THERMAL RELIEF VALVE AND ROUTED THE THERMAL TO RELIEVE BACK TO THE DOWNSTREAM PIPELINE SYSTEM.

ON JUNE 24, 2025, MPLX OPERATIONS PERSONNEL ARRIVED AT CONAN STATION AND OBSERVED EVIDENCE OF A CRUDE OIL LEAK ORIGINATING FROM BELOW GROUND. THE LEAK WAS LOCATED IN THE VICINITY OF THE ENTERPRISE 20” OUTGOING LINE AND AN ADJACENT 10” RELIEF LINE.  IN RESPONSE, THE OPERATOR INITIATED AN EMERGENCY SHUTDOWN (ESD) OF THE STATION AND IMMEDIATELY NOTIFIED THE CONTROL ROOM AND THE OPERATIONS MANAGER. BOTH LINES WERE ISOLATED TO DETERMINE THE SOURCE OF THE LEAK. AFTER CONFIRMING THE LEAKING LINE, INLET FLOWS TO THE STATION WERE RETURNED TO SERVICE. THE ENTERPRISE 20” OUTGOING LINE WAS THEN DISCONNECTED AND BLINDED. THE STATION WAS SUBSEQUENTLY BROUGHT BACK ONLINE.  AN ESTIMATED VOLUME OF APPROXIMATELY 10 BARRELS (BBLS) OF CRUDE OIL WAS RELEASED. ALL RELEASED PRODUCT REMAINED CONTAINED ON MPLX PROPERTY WITH NO OFF-SITE IMPACT.  INVESTIGATION FINDINGS:  THE INVESTIGATION CONCLUDED THAT THE FAILURE WAS CAUSED BY INTERNAL CORROSION DUE TO MICROBIOLOGICAL ACTIVITY, LIKELY EXACERBATED BY THE LINE’S LOW FLOW RATES.  PATH FORWARD:  • ABANDON THE AFFECTED LINE.  • RETIE THE LINE TO ALTERNATE HEADERS TO INCREASE FLOW FREQUENCY.  • REPLACE THE LINE, AS NECESSARY, TO ENSURE CONTINUED SAFE OPERATION.

ON 06/06/25 AT APPROXIMATELY 17:35, AN OPERATOR EMPLOYEE DISCOVERED A SMALL FIRE ON PUMP C3 IN THE PUMP ROOM. THE FIRE WAS IMMEDIATELY EXTINGUISHED WITH A FIRE EXTINGUISHER. OPERATIONS DISCOVERED CRUDE OIL LEAKING FROM A SEAL ON THE 8INCH 100 LINE INSIDE ARROW CENTRAL DELIVERY POINT (CDP).     APPROXIMATELY 1 GALLON OF CRUDE OIL WAS RELEASED. A SMALL AMOUNT OF PRODUCT WAS CONSUMED BY THE FIRE. THE REMAINING PRODUCT WAS CLEANED-UP BY LOCAL PERSONNEL.      THE PUMP WAS REMOVED AND FLANGES BLINDED. THE PUMP HAS BEEN SENT TO A THIRD PARTY FOR ANALYSIS, INSPECTION AND REPAIR. THE LINE WAS RESTARTED ON 06/07/25 AT 07:50.    THE CAUSE OF THE ACCIDENT IS STILL UNDER INVESTIGATION BY A THIRD PARTY. A SUPPLEMENTAL REPORT WILL BE SUBMITTED ONCE THE INVESTIGATION IS COMPLETE.     SUPPLEMENTAL & FINAL:  THE INVESTIGATION DETERMINED THE CAUSE OF THE LEAK WAS DUE TO A PUMP-RELATED EQUIPMENT FAILURE. THE PUMP SHAFT NUT WAS BEING HELD ON BY THE SEAL COLLAR AND BEGAN TO BACK OFF AFTER THE FAILURE. THE SHAFT NUT BEGAN TO ROTATE AGAINST THE BEARING HOUSING CREATING ENOUGH HEAT TO IGNITE THE PRODUCT.    TO PREVENT RECURRENCE THE PUMP WAS REMOVED, FLANGES BLINDED AND OPERATIONS ROUTED TO OTHER PUMPS.

AT APPROXIMATELY 1515 ON MAY 21, 2025, A 2ND PARTY CONTRACTOR REPORTED PRODUCT COMING OUT OF THE ROOF DRAINS OF A NEARBY TANK. UPON INVESTIGATION, IT WAS FOUND THAT PRODUCT HAD COME FROM THE ROOF DRAIN OF TANK 150-53.    THE INVESTIGATION DETERMINED THAT THE RELEASE WAS DUE TO A DAMAGED ROOF SEAL FROM A THIRD-PARTY PIPELINE PIGGING OPERATION. DURING THE PIGGING PROCESS, NITROGEN UNINTENTIONALLY BYPASSED THE PIG AND ENTERED THE TANK. THE RAPID EXPANSION OF NITROGEN WITHIN THE TANK DAMAGED THE PRIMARY AND SECONDARY SEALS, ALLOWING PRODUCT TO ACCUMULATE ON THE EXTERNAL FLOATING ROOF AND FLOW THROUGH THE ROOF DRAIN.    ALL PRODUCT AND AFFECTED SOIL WERE RECOVERED. THE AREA WAS FOAMED TO SUPPRESS VAPORS, AND THE PRODUCT WAS REMOVED FROM THE TANK. THE TANK IS BACK IN SERVICE.

ON 05/05/2025 AT APPROXIMATELY 06:23, THE CONTROL CENTER RECEIVED SCADA INDICATIONS OF A RELEASE ON THE KELLER TO MIDLOTHIAN SEGMENT OF THE 16-INCH RINGGOLD TO CORSICANA SYSTEM. THE LINE WAS SHUTDOWN AND UPSTREAM AND DOWNSTREAM VALVES CLOSED TO ISOLATE THE SEGMENT. OPERATIONS PERSONNEL WERE DISPATCHED AND BEGAN FIELD INVESTIGATIONS TO LOCATE A POTENTIAL RELEASE.  ON 05/06/2025 AT APPROXIMATELY 14:10, FIELD PERSONNEL DISCOVERED CRUDE OIL ON THE GROUND NEAR MP 90.82 IN THE ARLINGTON/FT. WORTH AREA.  ONCE EXCAVATED, BOTH CRUDE OIL AND SEWER WATER WERE DISCOVERED IN THE EXCAVATION. THE LOCATION OF THE LEAK WAS WHERE A 48-INCH CITY OF FORT WORTH SEWER LINE CROSSED UNDER THE KELLER TO MIDLOTHIAN SEGMENT. INVESTIGATION IN THE DITCH FOUND THE CONCRETE SEWER LINE APPEARED TO HAVE FAILED AND WAS EXPELLING SEWAGE INTO THE THE IMMEDIATE AREA IN AND AROUND THE KELLER TO MIDLOTHIAN PIPELINE.    APPROXIMATELY 6,600 BARRELS OF CRUDE OIL WAS RELEASED. THE MAJORITY OF THE RELEASED CRUDE TRAVELED THROUGH THE FAILED SEWER PIPE TO A WATER TREATMENT FACILITY APPROXIMATELY 4 MILES TO THE NORTHEAST.   CLEANUP CONTRACTORS WERE MOBILIZED TO CLEANUP PRODUCT AND REMOVE IMPACTED SOIL AT THE FAILURE SITE. PEP COORDINATED CLEANUP EFFORTS AT THE WATER TREATMENT FACILITY WITH THE CITY.    THE LINE WAS RESTARTED ON 5/9/25 AT 22:00 BY AFFECTING A STOPPLE AND BYPASS AROUND THE FAILED SECTION.  AFTER THE PIPELINE WAS RESTARTED THE FAILED SECTION WAS COLD CUT AND REMOVED FROM THE GROUND, PREPPED AND SHIPPED TO A 3RD PARTY LABORATORY FOR ANALYSIS.    THE CAUSE OF THE ACCIDENT IS STILL UNDER INVESTIGATION. A SUPPLEMENTAL REPORT WILL BE SUBMITTED ONCE COMPLETE.     SUPPLEMENTAL & FINAL:  THE METALLURGICAL ANALYSIS DETERMINED THAT THE FAILURE WAS DUE TO EXTERNAL CORROSION. THE CAUSE OF THE EXTERNAL CORROSION WAS MICROBIOLOGICALLY INDUCED CORROSION (MIC) WITH HIGH LEVELS OF SULFUR OXIDIZING BACTERIA (SOB), WHICH WAS MORE LIKELY THAN NOT CAUSED BY SEWAGE CONTAMINATION OF SOIL AND WATER FROM THE FAILED CITY OF FORT WORTH SEWER LINE AT THE RUPTURE LOCATION.  THE AGGRESSIVE CORROSION THINNED THE WALL OF THE PIPE THAT SPANNED THE LENGTH OF AND LED TO THE RUPTURE.

ON APRIL 17, 2025, AT APPROXIMATELY 8:24 AM CDT, TECHNICIANS AT THE SUPERIOR TERMINAL WERE COMPLETING MAINTENANCE AND OBSERVING THE STARTUP OF THE LINE 6, UNIT 3 PUMP AFTER A SEAL REPLACEMENT. DURING STARTUP, A RELEASE OF PRODUCT WAS FOUND TO BE COMING FROM THE OUTBOARD SEAL ON UNIT 3, AND AN ENBRIDGE TECHNICIAN INITIATED THE PUMP EMERGENCY SHUTDOWN BUTTON. SUPERVISION WAS NOTIFIED, AND AFTER ISOLATING AND LOCKING OUT THE UNIT, THE SPILL WAS CLEANED UP PROMPTLY. THE VOLUME RELEASED WAS APPROXIMATELY 100 GALLONS, ALL OF WHICH WAS CONTAINED ON THE CONCRETE FLOOR WITHIN THE PUMP BUILDING. CLEANUP WAS COMPLETED WITH APPROXIMATELY 95 GALLONS OF CRUDE OIL RETURNED TO THE SYSTEM, AND CLEAN-UP MATERIALS WERE PROPERLY DISPOSED OF. THE SEAL WAS REPLACED, AND UNIT 3 WAS RETURNED TO SERVICE.      FOLLOWING THE RELEASE, THE FAILED SEAL WAS SUBMITTED TO THE MANUFACTURER FOR FURTHER ANALYSIS. THE FINDINGS INDICATED THAT THE SEAL ENCOUNTERED AN UNEXPECTED LOAD FORCE ON THE SEAL FACES DURING STARTUP, WHICH CONTRIBUTED TO ITS FAILURE. THIS LOAD FORCE WAS DETERMINED TO BE A RESULT OF THE SEAL INSTALLATION. BASED ON THESE FINDINGS, ADDITIONAL STEPS FOR THE WORK EXECUTION PLAN WERE IDENTIFIED TO MINIMIZE THE POSSIBILITY OF A RECURRENCE.

APPROXIMATELY 12 BARRELS OF CRUDE OIL WAS RELEASED. CLEANUP CONTRACTORS REMOVED PRODUCT AND REMEDIATED IMPACTED SOIL.    THE LEAK WAS REPAIRED BY REPLACING THE VALVE. THE LINE WAS PUT BACK IN SERVICE ON 04/11/2025.    THE CAUSE OF THE ACCIDENT IS STILL UNDER INVESTIGATION. A SUPPLEMENTAL REPORT WILL BE SUBMITTED ONCE THE INVESTIGATION IS COMPLETE.    SUPPLEMENTAL & FINAL:  THE INVESTIGATION DETERMINED THE CAUSE OF THE ACCIDENT WAS DUE TO INTERNAL CORROSION. THE LEAK COINCIDED WITHIN A REGION OF INTERNAL CORROSION LOCATED ALONG THE BOTTOM OF THE VALVE BODY. A PIT IN THE FLANGE MATERIAL ADJACENT TO THE LEAK LOCATION WAS ALSO OBSERVED, WHICH ALIGNED WITH PRE-EXISTING MANUFACTURING VOIDS. ADDITIONALLY, A SECOND PIT WAS IDENTIFIED WITHIN THE ADJACENT FLANGE MATERIAL OF THE VALVE, FURTHER CONTRIBUTING TO THE LOCALIZED CORROSION AND EVENTUAL LEAK.    TO PREVENT REOCCURRENCE, NDE EXAMINE ONE OTHER VALVE BY SAME MANUFACTURER WITH SAME APPROXIMATE MANUFACTURED DATE TO ENSURE NO THINNING OF THE BODY WAS OCCURRING.

OCTOBER 15, THE RELEASE WAS DUE TO A SUDDEN RUPTURE EVENT, AND THE AXIS OF THE RUPTURE ALIGNS WITH THE PIPE’S LONGITUDINAL SEAM WELD. THE FAILED PIPE IS 30-INCH DIAMETER, 0.386-INCH WALL THICKNESS WITH API 5L X70 DOUBLE-SUBMERGED ARC WELDED (DSAW) LONGITUDINAL SEAM MANUFACTURED BY THE BERG STEEL PIPE CORPORATION. A CORRECTIVE ACTION ORDER WAS ISSUED FOR THIS ACCIDENT (CPF NO. 3-2025-018-CAO) AND THE CORRECTIVE ACTIONS OF MECHANICAL AND METALLURGICAL TESTING AND ROOT CAUSE FAILURE ANALYSIS WERE COMPLETED.    JANUARY 8, 2026, THE ESTIMATED COSTS WERE UPDATED OTHERWISE THERE ARE NO FURTHER UPDATES; THIS IS THE FINAL REPORT.
cause: MATERIAL FAILURE OF PIPE OR WELD

AFTER INVESTIGATING THE CAUSE OF THE FAILURE, IT APPEARS LIKELY THAT THE O-RING FAILED DUE TO A COMBINATION OF VERY LOW TEMPERATURES (AS LOW AS 10F) AND A LACK OF ADEQUATE LUBRICATION. A NEW VALVE HAS BEEN PURCHASED AND WILL BE INSTALLED AND THE O-RING WILL BECOME PART OF A PREVENTATIVE MAINTENANCE SCHEDULE IN THE FUTURE.

EAST SPARTA UNIT 6 SHUT DOWN UPON GENERATION OF A PUMP SEAL FAILURE ALARM. UNIT WAS ISOLATED AND DRAINED. MPL AND THE MANUFACTURER ARE INVESTIGATING THE CAUSE OF THE FAILURE.     SEAL MATERIALS  STATIONARY FACE: SILICON CARBIDE  ROTATING FACE: CARBON    SUPPLEMENTAL FINAL UPDATE:  THE SEAL FAILURE WAS CAUSED BY A FAILURE IN THE PIN MECHANISM DESIGNED TO HOLD THE PRIMARY STATIONARY FACE IN PLACE, ALLOWING IT TO SHIFT AND BECOME MISALIGNED WITHIN THE LOCK RING. THIS MISALIGNMENT LED TO LOSS OF FLUID FILM, EXCESSIVE WEAR/HEAT, AND EVENTUAL LEAKAGE. TO PREVENT RECURRENCE, THE LOCKING MECHANISM WILL BE REDESIGNED TO SECURE THE STATIONARY FACE, AND ALL MECHANICAL SEALS FROM THIS MANUFACTURER ARE BEING REVIEWED FOR SIMILAR DESIGN FLAWS, TRACKED FOR PERFORMANCE, AND MONITORED FOR MEAN TIME BETWEEN FAILURES.

AT SOME POINT, FATIGUE CRACK GROWTH, DRIVEN BY PRESSURE CYCLING AT THE SITE OF THE DENT, IN COMBINATION WITH CONTINUED NNSCC, PROPAGATED THE CRACK UNTIL IT BECAME THROUGH-WALL.

AT 11:40 CST ON NOVEMBER 19, 2024, A PIPELINE TECHNICIAN WITH HOLLY ENERGY WAS NOTIFIED BY A LINE LOCATOR WITH ANOTHER PIPELINE OPERATOR OF A SUSPECTED LEAK NEAR SWEETWATER, TEXAS. THE PIPELINE TECHNICIAN ARRIVED ON SITE AT 12:00 CST, AND SEVEN MINUTES LATER THE ARTESIA CONTROL CENTER INITIATED A PIPELINE SHUTDOWN. FIELD TEAMS WERE DEPLOYED TO SECURE THE AREA. AS PART OF THE INITIAL RESPONSE, SCADA DATA WAS REVIEWED FOR PRESSURE DROPS AND FLOW ANOMALIES, AND A WALKDOWN OF ADJACENT RIGHT-OF-WAYS WAS CONDUCTED TO RULE OUT OTHER POSSIBLE SOURCES. NO WORK ACTIVITIES WERE UNDERWAY IN THE AREA, AND THERE WERE NO SIGNS OF RECENT GROUND DISTURBANCE NEAR THE RELEASE SITE.    UPON CONFIRMATION OF THE LEAK AT 14:15 CST, REGULATORY NOTIFICATIONS WERE MADE. THE NATIONAL RESPONSE CENTER (NRC, REPORT #1416839) WAS CONTACTED AT 15:01, FOLLOWED BY THE TEXAS RAILROAD COMMISSION (RRC) AT 15:10, BOTH WITHIN THE REQUIRED TIMEFRAMES. THE TEXAS COMMISSION ON ENVIRONMENTAL QUALITY (TCEQ) WAS NOTIFIED LATER THE SAME DAY AT 16:44. HOLLY ENERGY ACTIVATED ITS OIL SPILL REMOVAL ORGANIZATION (OSRO) AT 14:30 CST. LOCAL EMERGENCY RESPONSE AGENCIES WERE NOTIFIED, THOUGH NO ASSISTANCE WAS ULTIMATELY REQUIRED FROM LOCAL RESPONDERS.    BLACKLAND SERVICES, OUR PRIMARY LOCAL CONTRACTOR, MOBILIZED VACUUM TRUCKS, AN EXCAVATOR, AND A LIGHT PLANT FOR NIGHT OPERATIONS. HF SINCLAIR’S EMERGENCY RESPONSE TRAILER WAS ALSO DEPLOYED FROM THEIR TYE TERMINAL IN ABILENE, STOCKED WITH TOOLS, WATER BOOM, GENERATORS, ABSORBENT PADS, FIRE EXTINGUISHERS, FENCING, STOPS, AND STRAW WATTLE. ONCE THE OSRO ARRIVED, ADDITIONAL SUPPORT WAS PROVIDED BY VACUUM CONTRACTORS, A THIRD-PARTY EMERGENCY RESPONSE PROVIDER SPECIALIZING IN HAZARDOUS MATERIALS INCIDENTS. AMBIPAR SUPPLEMENTED THE RESPONSE WITH VACUUM TRUCKS, PERSONNEL, AND TRAILERS EQUIPPED WITH SCBAS, TYVEK SUITS, AND ADDITIONAL CONTAINMENT MEASURES. ALTHOUGH NO VAPORS OF H2S WERE AT RISK, ESTABLISHED RESPONSE PROTOCOLS EFFECTIVELY MITIGATED THE HAZARD. ENVIRONMENTAL CONTRACTORS IMMEDIATELY BEGAN SITE CONTAINMENT AND REMEDIATION ACTIVITIES.    NO INJURIES OR SAFETY-RELATED INCIDENTS WERE REPORTED DURING THE INITIAL RESPONSE OR THROUGHOUT THE REPAIR AND REPLACEMENT ACTIVITIES. EMERGENCY RESPONSE ACTIVATION REMAINED IN PLACE FROM NOVEMBER 19 TO DECEMBER 3 (14 DAYS).    FAILURE OCCURRED AT MP 62 IN A BURIED PIPELINE SEGMENT. METALLURGICAL TESTING CONFIRMED THE PRESENCE OF EXTERNAL CORROSION ON THE SITE OF A PINHOLE LEAK. SOIL ANALYSIS REVEALED ELEVATED LEVELS OF CHLORINE AND MAGNESIUM, WHICH LIKELY CONTRIBUTED TO THE CORROSION. COATING EVALUATIONS POST REVIEW SHOWED INCONSISTENT THICKNESSES ACROSS FOUR CROSS-SECTIONS. ACCORDING TO THE MANUFACTURER SPECIFICATIONS FOR DENSO-PROTAL 7200, THE RECOMMENDED COATING THICKNESS FOR FBE REPAIRS IS 25–30 MILS, WITH A MINIMUM AND MAXIMUM THICKNESSES BETWEEN 20 AND 70 MILS. THE 12 AND 6 O’CLOCK POSITIONS HAD THE THINNEST AVERAGE COATING THICKNESS IN THE PIPE SECTIONS, WITH A MINIMUM COATING THICKNESS FOUND ON PIPE SECTION 3 AT THE 12 O’CLOCK POSITION READING 7.6 MILS. WHILE THE MAXIMUM COATING ON THAT SECTION WAS FOUND TO BE 40.2.    THIS SEGMENT WAS COATED ON-SITE DURING A 2023 REPLACEMENT PROJECT, WHERE EXPEDITED SCHEDULING AND THE USE OF BARE PIPE RESULTED IN LIMITED QA/QC OVERSIGHT. THE LACK OF OVERSIGHT, ALONG WITH DEVIATIONS FROM COATING SPECIFICATIONS AND PROCEDURES, CONTRIBUTED TO THE RELEASE. IN ADDITION, THE CATHODIC PROTECTION SYSTEM SHOWED SIGNS OF INTERFERENCE, LIKELY FROM DC INTERACTION WITH OTHER PIPELINES IN THE SHARED CORRIDOR AND POSSIBLY COMPOUNDED BY NEARBY AC POWER SOURCES.    LEAK DETECTION SYSTEMS DID NOT TRIGGER DURING THE EVENT, LIKELY DUE TO THE SMALL RELEASE VOLUME COMBINED WITH METERING INACCURACIES. SEVERAL IMPROVEMENT OPPORTUNITIES WERE IDENTIFIED, INCLUDING STRENGTHENING COATING QUALITY ASSURANCE PROCESSES, ENHANCING CATHODIC PROTECTION MONITORING, AND UPGRADING LEAK DETECTION SYSTEMS.

ON NOVEMBER 18, 2024, AT 9:17 AM CST, A TECHNICIAN WAS DOING MAINTENANCE NEAR THE LINE 4 UNIT 2 VALVE (DN-4-UDV-21) AT DONALDSON STATION.  DURING A WALK AROUND THEY DISCOVERED CRUDE OIL ON THE VALVE AND THE SURROUNDING GROUND. THE EDMONTON CONTROL CENTER WAS IMMEDIATELY NOTIFIED, AND THE UNIT WAS ISOLATED.  THE SOURCE OF THE RELEASE WAS A LEAKING VALVE STEM SEAL THAT RELEASED APPROXIMATELY 1.25 GALLONS OF CRUDE OIL.  THE NRC WAS NOTIFIED ON NOVEMBER 18, 2024, AT 10:16 AM CST (NRC #1416706).  THE MINNESOTA DUTY OFFICER WAS ALSO NOTIFIED (#224022). OPERATIONS AND CONTRACTED LABOR RESPONDED TO THE SITE TO CLEAN UP ANY CONTAMINATED SOIL. OPERATIONS PERFORMED A STEM SEAL PACKING OPERATION AFTER THE VALVE WAS CLOSED WHICH STOPPED THE LEAKAGE. A 48-HOUR UPDATE TO THE NRC WAS MADE ON NOVEMBER 20, 2024, AT 10:01 AM CST (NRC #1416880). ALL CONTAMINATED SOIL HAS BEEN REMOVED FROM THE RELEASE SITE.    THE REPAIR ASSEMBLY WAS INSTALLED ON DECEMBER 18, 2024.  ENBRIDGE PERSONNEL COMPLETED THE STEM SEAL INVESTIGATION AND REPAIR WITH THE MANUFACTURER PRESENT. IT WAS DETERMINED THAT TWO CONTRIBUTING FACTORS CAUSED THE STEM SEAL FAILURE. THE FIRST OBSERVATION WAS DEBRIS BUILD-UP WITHIN THE STEM SEAL ASSEMBLY. THE OBSERVED DEBRIS COULD HAVE CONTRIBUTED TO THE DAMAGED STEM. THIS DEBRIS COULD HAVE BEEN LEFT IN THE ASSEMBLY DURING MANUFACTURING. THE SECOND OBSERVATION WAS THAT THE STEM WAS DAMAGED/GOUGED WHICH COULD HAVE ALSO OCCURRED DURING THE MANUFACTURING PROCESS. THE DAMAGED STEM CREATED A LEAK PATH FOR THE SEAL TO FAIL.     THE ACTUAL VOLUME RELEASED AT DONALDSON STATION WAS 0.02 BARRELS (1.25 GALLONS) OF CRUDE OIL. THE PHMSA PORTAL DOES NOT RECOGNIZE VOLUMES LESS THAN 0.1 BARRELS THEREFORE THAT IS THE VOLUME ENTERED.

LINE 59 WAS IMMEDIATELY SHUT DOWN AND A TECHNICIAN WAS DISPATCHED TO INVESTIGATE THE ALARM. THE UNIT WAS ISOLATED, AND CLEANUP OF THE RELEASE WAS COMPLETED BY COMPANY PERSONNEL. UPON FURTHER INVESTIGATION THE CAUSE OF THE RELEASE WAS DUE TO AN INTERLOCK TAB BREAKING OFF WHICH ALLOWED THE THRUST NUT TO COME UNTHREADED CAUSING THE SHAFT TO WORK LOOSE RESULTING IN DAMAGE TO BOTH SEALS.

ON OCTOBER 17, 2024, AT 18:35 CDT, SECURITY PERSONNEL AT GRIFFITH TERMINAL NOTIFIED OPERATIONS OF A STRONG PETROLEUM ODOR AT THE FRONT GATE OF THE FACILITY. OPERATIONS ARRIVED ONSITE TO INVESTIGATE THE ODOR AND AT 19:13 CDT DISCOVERED A RELEASE FROM THE 202 MANIFOLD. THE EDMONTON CONTROL CENTER WAS IMMEDIATELY CONTACTED, AND LINES 6A, 62, 64, AND BP DELIVERIES WERE SHUT DOWN AND THE AREA WAS ISOLATED. THE RELEASE WAS ESTIMATED AT 350 BARRELS OF CRUDE OIL AND WAS FULLY CONTAINED WITHIN THE MANIFOLD'S VICINITY WITH NO RISK OF MIGRATION OFF SITE. REGIONAL AND CONTRACTOR RESOURCES WERE MOBILIZED TO BEGIN RESPONSE. NRC CRITERIA WAS DETERMINED TO BE MET AT 20:13 CDT, AND NRC WAS NOTIFIED AT 20:56 CDT (NRC# 1414013). A 48-HOUR UPDATE TO THE NRC WAS MADE ON OCTOBER 19, 2024, AT 20:40 CDT (NRC# 1414196). UPON EXCAVATION OF THE RELEASE AREA, THE SOURCE OF THE RELEASE WAS A PINHOLE AT THE 6 O'CLOCK POSITION ON 20" INTERCONNECT MANIFOLD PIPING. THE SECTION OF PIPE WAS CUT OUT AND THE LINE WAS ISOLATED. APPROXIMATELY 270 BARRELS OF CRUDE OIL WAS RETURNED TO THE SYSTEM, AND CONTAMINATED SOIL HAS BEEN REMOVED FROM THE RELEASE SITE. AN INTERNAL INVESTIGATION DETERMINED THE RELEASE WAS CAUSED BY INTERNAL CORROSION PITTING ON THE INTERCONNECT PIPING. THE RESULTS OF THE ANALYSIS INDICATE THAT THE INTERNAL CORROSION OBSERVED ON THE PIPE OCCURRED DUE TO SIGNIFICANT MICROBIAL ACTIVITY. THE FAILED PIPING WAS REMOVED AND BLINDED ON BOTH END CONNECTIONS AS A PERMANENT REPAIR. ADDITIONAL STEPS ARE BEING TAKEN TO PREVENT RECURRENCE, INCLUDING VERIFYING THE ACCURACY OF THE RISK/THREAT EVALUATION AND REVIEWING DEAD LEG PIPING FOR SIMILAR THREATS.

text: AT 17:30 OPERATIONS DISCOVERED A LEAK ON THE EAST HOUSTON TO HEARNE PIPELINE FAST LOOP SAMPLE PUMP.   EAST HOUSTON TO HEARNE WAS PUMPING OUTBOUND AND THE FAST LOOP SAMPLE PUMP WAS RUNNING UNDER NORMAL OPERATING CONDITIONS. AT 11:06, THE CONTROL ROOM RECEIVED A SALEM BOOSTER PUMP LOCKOUT FIRST. THIS CAUSED THE CLAY CITY PIPELINE TO SHUT DOWN IMMEDIATELY UPON THE ALARM COMING IN ALONG WITH A LIST OF OTHER ALARMS REGARDING THE SHUTDOWN. THE CONTROL ROOM ALSO RECEIVED A CLAY CITY TO JOHNSONVILLE DELIVERY TRIP. THE CONTROL ROOM RESET ALL THE PUMPS AND LOOKED AT THE ALARMS IN THE HISTORICAL. THERE WERE NO ACTIVE ALARMS HOLDING OUT PERMISSIVE TO RESTART. THE REASONING OF THE SHUTDOWN WAS NOT APPARENT AND BELIEVED TO BE AN ISSUE IN THE PROGRAMING SINCE 2 AUTOMATION TECHS (CONTRACT) WERE IN THE SOFTWARE FIXING ISSUES UNRELATED TO THIS INCIDENT. THE CONTROL ROOM TRIED TO RESTART THE CLAY CITY TO JOHNSONVILLE PIPELINE. THE CONTROL ROOM RECEIVED SALEM BOOSTER PUMP LOCKOUT, SALEM TO CLAY CITY DELIVERY TRIP, CLAY CITY DELIVERY TRIP AND A LIST OF OTHER ALARMS REGARDING THE SHUTDOWN. THE CONTROL ROOM DISCUSSED WITH THE AUTOMATION CONTRACTOR, BUT THEY WERE UNABLE TO TELL US WHAT WAS CAUSING THE DELIVERY TRIPS. AT 11:50 THE CONTROL ROOM DECIDED TO ATTEMPT TO START JUST THE CLAY CITY LINE. THE BOOSTER PUMP AT CLAY CITY WAS STARTED, BUT SHUTDOWN ON DELIVERY TRIP.   THE CONTROL ROOM CALLED THE I&E SUPV. TO GET AN I&E TECH TO GO TO CLAY CITY TO LOOK AT A PRESSURE TRANSMITTER. WHEN HE WAS INFORMED WE HAD A PRESSURE TRANSMITTER READING ZERO, HE TOLD THE CONTROL ROOM THEY HAD TAKEN ALL OF THOSE LINES APART DURING A PIPING PROJECT AND WE MAY WANT TO GET A GAUGER OVER THERE TO CHECK IT OUT FIRST. AT 11:58 THE CONTROL ROOM CONTACTED THE GAUGER TO CHECK THE TRANSMITTER. AT 12:15 THE GAUGER INFORMED THE CONTROL ROOM THERE WAS A LEAK ON A PRESSURE TRANSMITTER AND THAT HE WAS GOING TO SHUT THE VALVE TO ISOLATE THE LEAK. THE CONTROL ROOM IMMEDIATELY CALLED THE QUALIFIED INDIVIDUAL TO INITIATE EMERGENCY RESPONSE ACTIVITIES. ADDITIONAL RESOURCES ARRIVED ON SITE AT 12:45 TO BEGIN RESPONSE ACTIVITIES. THE TUBING TO THE TRANSMITTER WAS REPAIRED AT 15:46. OPERATIONS RESTARTED THE CLAY CITY PUMPS AT 4:20 UNDER OBSERVATION OF THE MAINTENANCE PERSONNEL. THE RESPONSE CREWS COMPLETED REMEDIATION ACTIVITIES OF THE SITE ON OCTOBER 11TH. A THIRD PARTY MATERIALS LAB COMPLETED A FAILURE ANALYSIS ON THE TUBING. THE FAILURE ANALYSIS CONCLUDED THAT "VIBRATION IN SERVICE FROM PRESSURE VARIATION WAS A LIKELY CAUSE OF THE CRACKING"

DURING A PLANNED PROJECT, TANK LINE 250 IN PELHAM JUNCTION WAS BEING EXCAVATED FOR AN INSPECTION. PRODUCT HAD BEEN DRAINED FROM THE TANK LINE APPROXIMATELY THREE WEEKS PRIOR TO THE EXCAVATION. DURING THE EXCAVATION, CONTAMINATED SOIL WAS DISCOVERED. ADDITIONAL EXCAVATION AND EXAMINATION IDENTIFIED A PINHOLE AS THE SOURCE OF THE LEAK ON TANK LINE 250. ON AUGUST 19, 2024, AT APPROXIMATELY 03:50 HOURS, A LOCAL OPERATOR STARTED A DELIVERY FROM TANK 1211 TO A MARINE BARGE UTILIZING THE TANK PUMP.  THE LOCAL OPERATOR STARTED THE TANK PUMP USING THE PHYSICAL ON/OFF SWITCH. AFTER STARTING THE PUMP, THE LOCAL OPERATOR OBSERVED FLAMES EMITTING FROM THE PUMP.     THE OPERATOR IMMEDIATELY CALLED 911 TO DISPATCH EMERGENCY RESPONDERS. THE SOURCE WAS ISOLATED AND ALL INTERNAL AND EXTERNAL NOTIFICATIONS WERE MADE. THE FIRE DEPARTMENT ARRIVED AND EXTINGUISHED THE FIRE. APPROXIMATELY 30 GALLONS OF ULSD WAS RELEASED INTO SECONDARY CONTAINMENT AND COMPLETELY CONTAINED ON OPERATOR PROPERTY.      ADDITIONALLY, APPROXIMATELY 30 GALLONS OF FIRE FOAM WAS RELEASED BY THE FIRE DEPARTMENT TO ENSURE THERE WERE NO REMAINING HAZARDS. ALL RELEASED PRODUCT WAS RECOVERED.  ALL RELEASED FIRE FOAM WAS RECOVERED. ALL AFFECTED SOIL HAS BEEN REMOVED AND PROPERLY DISPOSED OF.    FURTHER INVESTIGATION REVEALED A MINOR PUMP SEAL FAILURE WAS THE CAUSE OF THE INCIDENT.  THE FAILED TANK PUMP WAS REMOVED AND SENT TO 3RD PARTY FOR FAILURE ANALYSIS. A REPLACEMENT PUMP WAS INSTALLED, AND NORMAL OPERATIONS RESUMED.    1/10/2025   THIRD PARTY FAILURE ANALYSIS DETERMINED THE CAUSE OF THE FAILURE WAS LINE FEEDER WIRES FEEDING THE MOTOR HAS A CATASTROPHIC FAILURE OR SHORT.  THIS CAUSED TEMPERATURES TO RISE WHICH THEN CAUSED WIRE INSULATION TO FAIL RESULTING IN A FLASH FIRE. THE HEAT AND EXCESSIVE VIBRATION BY THE PUMP DAMAGED THE O RING FORMING A LEAK PATH. THE SEAL ITSELF WAS FOUND TO BE PROPERLY BOLTED AND TIGHTENED.

PHILLIPS 66 BARTLESVILLE CONTROL CENTER NOTIFIED LOCAL OPERATIONS OF A LEAK DETECTION ALARM ON PH50 PIPELINE. LOCAL OPERATIONS INVESTIGATED THE NOTIFICATION AND DISCOVERED THE LEAKING BODY BLEED ON THE BLOCK VALVE. THIS TUBING IS PART OF THE BODY RELIEF SYSTEM OF THE WKM POW R SEAL VALVE, WHICH DISCHARGES INTO THE UPSTREAM SIDE OF THE PIPE.    THE LABORATORY ANALYSIS CONFIRMED THE TUBING FAILED DUE TO HIGH CYCLE FATIGUE FROM LOW STRESS CYCLIC STRESS.    CORRECTIVE ACTIONS:     1. REPLACE THE BODY HEAVY (MASS) CARBON STEEL FITTINGS WITH LIGHTWEIGHT STAINLESS-STEEL INSTRUMENTATION FITTINGS.    2. INSTALL TUBING SUPPORT TO MINIMIZE VIBRATION.    SUPPLEMENTAL:     CORRECTED LOCAL TIME OF CONFIRMED DISCOVERY.     CORRECTED TYPE OF MATERIAL INVOLVED.     CORRECTED DOWNSTREAM VALVE TYPE USED TO INITIALLY ISOLATE RELEASE SOURCE.

THE OPERATOR ON 7/30/24 AT APPROX. 1:50AM WENT TO CLOSE A MANUAL VALVE FOR THE MOVEMENT.  WHILE HEADING OUT THERE, HE NOTICED OIL BY TANK 7 WHERE THE 12-INCH FILL LINES COMES THROUGH THE BERM/DIKE WALL. UPON FURTHER INSPECTION, HE ALSO NOTICED OIL ON THE GROUND BY TANK 6 COMING OUT OF THE CULVERT PIPE.      THE PIPE FAILURE WAS INSIDE A GALVANIZED CULVERT PIPE THAT PENETRATED THROUGH THE BERM/DIKE WALL BETWEEN TANK 6 AND TANK 7, ALL WITHIN CONTAINMENT.  THE CULVERT PIPE CORRODED AND COLLAPSED ONTO THE CARRIER PIPE INSULATION/COATING CAUSING EXTERNAL CORROSION AND PIPE FAILURE.      THIS PARTICULAR SECTION OF THE 12-INCH LINE FILL WAS BLINDED ON BOTH SIDES AND WILL NOT BE USED IN THE FUTURE.  THE SUCTION LINE WILL NOW BE BI-DIRECTIONAL.

COMPANY OPERATORS WERE NOTIFIED OF A POSSIBLE RELEASE BY A 3RD PARTY OPERATOR IN A SHARED RIGHT OF WAY. AT 18:00 ON JULY 18, 2024, COMPANY PERSONNEL WERE ABLE TO CONFIRM OWNERSHIP OF THE LEAK AND BEGAN ACTIVATION OF THE COMPANY RESPONSE PLAN. THE PIPELINE WAS ISOLATED, AND ALL NOTIFICATIONS WERE MADE AT THIS TIME TO LOCAL, STATE AND FEDERAL AGENCIES. SIMULTANEOUSLY, THE LOCAL TEAM BEGAN EXCAVATION AND BLOWDOWN OPERATIONS TO ALLOW FOR INVESTIGATION AND REPAIR OF THE RELEASE. A TEMPORARY LEAK CLAMP WAS INSTALLED, AND THE LINE WAS RETURNED TO SERVICE ON JULY 21, 2024, AT 14:15.    THE LINE WAS CUT OUT AND REPLACED ON JANUARY 25, 2025.    AFTER RECEIVING THE FINAL METALLURGICAL REPORT, ON APRIL 7, 2025, IT WAS DETERMINED THE RELEASE WAS DUE TO EXTERNAL CORROSION CAUSED BY LOCAL ENVIRONMENTAL CONDITIONS.     EXTENSIVE FIELD TESTING WAS DONE AT THE LEAK SITE THAT INDICATES 3RD PARTY INFLUENCE DUE TO RECENTLY INSTALLED CATHODIC PROTECTION SYSTEMS IN CLOSE PROXIMITY TO THE PIPELINE.

NGL TECH ARRIVED AT THE SANDHILLS PINTO CREEK TRAP RECEIVER ON 7/18/24 @ 8:42 AM FOR SCHEDULED ROUTINE MAINTENANCE. THE NGL TECH IMMEDIATELY NOTICED THE CLOSURE DOOR ON THE PIG RECEIVER TRAP HAD AN ICE BALL ON IT. THE TECH BACKED OFF AND MADE NOTIFICATIONS TO FIELD SUPERVISION THEN ISOLATED THE RECEIVER TRAP TO STOP THE LEAK @ 8:51 AM. THE LEAK AMOUNT WAS CALCULATED BY ENGINEERING AND DETERMINED TO BE REPORTABLE TO THE TRRC. THE LEAK WAS REPORTED TO THE TRRC 24 HOUR EMERGENCY LINE @ 9:20 AM. BETWEEN THE HOURS OF 8:30PM ON 7/10/24 AND 8:46AM ON 7/11/24 APPROXIMATELY 2,800 BARRELS OF CRUDE OIL RELEASED FROM THE PIPING MANIFOLD INTO THE PRIMARY CONTAINMENT SURROUNDING TANK 202. THE RELEASE WAS DISCOVERED AT 8:45 AM ON 7/11/24 BY THE MAINTENANCE MANAGER (MM) WHO SMELLED THE CRUDE OIL WHILE DRIVING BY THE TANK FARM. THE MM IMMEDIATELY INVESTIGATED THE SPILL AND DISCOVERED THAT THE 2" DIXON ANDREWS CAM FITTING HAD FAILED, AND THE MANIFOLD VALVE WAS OPEN ON THE LOW POINT OF TANK 202. THE MM SHUT THE MANIFOLD VALVE AND OPERATIONS LEADERSHIP WAS NOTIFIED. WHILE THE VALVE WAS REQUIRED TO BE OPEN DURING THE MAINTENANCE ACTIVITY, IT WAS NOT CLOSED AT THE COMPLETION OF THE DAY'S ACTIVITY AS A SECONDARY LAYER OF PROTECTION.  BUT FOR THE CRACK AND SUBSEQUENT FAILURE OF THE BODY OF THE 2" DIXON ANDREWS CAM FITTING, THERE WOULD NOT HAVE BEEN A RELEASE.    RECOVERY AND REMEDIATION EFFORTS BEGAN THE SAME DAY. SPILL CLEAN UP CONTRACTORS ARRIVED AT THE SITE WITHIN 30 MINUTES OF THE SPILL BEING DISCOVERED.    THE INVESTIGATION DETERMINED THAT THE BODY OF THE 2" DIXON ANDREWS CAM FITTING CONNECTED TO THE VALVE FAILED, AND THE VALVE TO THE MANIFOLD WAS OPEN ALLOWING PRODUCT TO FLOW FREELY FROM TANK 201 AND 205, UNTIL THE VALVE WAS CLOSED. THE PROCEDURES WERE DETERMINED TO BE INADEQUATE. THIS WAS A ONE-OFF MAINTENANCE ACTIVITY THAT HAS NOW BEEN ADEQUATELY DOCUMENTED IN THE REVISED PROCEDURES. ALSO, TRAINING HAS COMMENCED WITH OPERATIONS PERSONNEL.     PLEASE NOTE IN PART E (2, 2.A, 2.B, 2.C, 3 & 8) THESE ARE ANSWERED REGARDING THE 2" DIXON ANDREWS CAM FITTING MOP/MAOP. THE DATE FOR E2.B WAS LISTED AS 7/11/24 AS THE ESTABLISHED MOP DATE FOR THE 2" DIXON ANDREWS CAM FITTING BY THE MANUFACTURER IS UNKNOWN AS OF NOW.     THE 2" DIXON ANDREWS CAM FITTING WAS PROPERLY INSTALLED APPROXIMATELY ONE WEEK BEFORE THE ACCIDENT AND WAS INTERMITTENTLY IN SERVICE DURING THAT TIME FRAME AND THERE WERE NO LEAKS THAT OCCURRED PRIOR TO THE 7/11/2024 DATE.    *NOTE FROM SECTION G6: THE FAILED SECTION OF THE SUBMITTED ENGINE CAM SAMPLE SHOWED PRIMARY BRITTLE INTERGRANULAR FRACTURE MODE DUE TO MECHANICAL OVERSTRESS OF THE PART WITH MATERIAL DEGRADATION DUE TO CORROSIVE CHLORIDE ATTACK.    MAINTENANCE ACTIVITY: REPLACE MIXER MOTOR ON TANK 202.     INADEQUACY OF PROCEDURES: THE PROCEDURE DID NOT EMPHASIZE THE INSPECTION OF THE EXTERNAL VALVE FITTING.     PROCEDURE REVISIONS: THEY HAVE BEEN UPDATED TO INCLUDE THE INSPECTION OF THE EXTERNAL VALVE FITTING. WE HAVE ALSO ADOPTED AN INSPECTION PROCESS THAT HAS IN-SERVICE DATES, END DATES, AND TIME SCHEDULED INSPECTIONS FOR CRITICAL COMPONENTS. WE ARE IN THE PROCESS OF CHANGING OUR CAM FITTINGS TO STAINLESS STEEL.

ON 6/22/24 AT APPROXIMATELY 20:46, A FIRE AT THE TANK 2536 MIXER AT THE CUSHING NORTH TERMINAL WAS DISCOVERED. LOCAL OPERATING PERSONNEL CONTACTED THE TERMINAL MANAGER, THEN CALLED 911 AND REQUESTED FIRE SERVICES TO ASSIST IN EXTINGUISHING THE FIRE.  THE TERMINAL MANAGER CONTACTED THE CONTROL CENTER AND REQUESTED THAT THE TERMINAL BE SHUT DOWN.    ONCE THE FIRE WAS EXTINGUISHED IT WAS DETERMINED THAT APPROXIMATELY 2 BARRELS OF CRUDE OIL WAS RELEASED. A CONTRACTOR CREW CLEANED UP PRODUCT AND REMOVED CONTAMINATED SOIL.    OPERATIONS PUMPED THE TANK DOWN, REPLACED THE MIXER, INSPECTED THE TANK AND RETURNED TO NORMAL SERVICE THE FOLLOWING DAY.     THE CAUSE OF THE ACCIDENT IS STILL UNDER INVESTIGATION. THE REMOVED MIXER WAS EXAMINED BY THE MANUFACTURER AND A BEARING FAILURE IS SUSPECTED TO BE THE CAUSE.  THE OTHER MIXER BEARING ON TANK 2536 WAS REMOVED AND IT ALONG WITH THE FAILED BEARING WERE SENT TO AN INDEPENDENT 3RD PARTY LAB FOR ADDITIONAL ANALYSIS.      A SUPPLEMENTAL AND FINAL REPORT WILL BE SUBMITTED ONCE THE INVESTIGATION IS COMPLETE.    SUPPLEMENTAL & FINAL:  THE INVESTIGATION DETERMINED THE ACCIDENT WAS CAUSED BY EQUIPMENT FAILURE. TANK MIXER SEAL FAILURE WAS CAUSED BY MIXER BEARING FAILURE WHICH WAS LIKELY DUE TO A BEARING LUBRICATION FAILURE OR PIECE OF DEBRIS ENTERING THE BEARING ASSEMBLY.  SOMETIME AFTER THE SEAL LEAK BEGAN THE POWER WIRING TO THE MIXER SHORTED TO GROUND THROUGH A WORN CONDUIT AND THE RESULTANT SPARKS CAUSED IGNITION TO THE CRUDE OIL RELEASED FROM THE SEAL FAILURE.     THE INVESTIGATION IDENTIFIED THAT THE POWER WIRING TO THE MIXER WAS ROUTED IN A MANNER THAT ALLOWED RUBBING AGAINST THE MIXER MOUNTING PLATE. TO PREVENT REOCCURRENCE, OPERATIONS IS REROUTING CONDUITS THAT ARE CURRENTLY IN CONTACT WITH THE MIXER MOUNTING PLATE.

DURING PIGGING OPERATIONS AT THE DEER RIVER STATION ON APRIL 22, 2024, AT APPROXIMATELY 11:17 PM CDT, THE EDMONTON CONTROL CENTER RECEIVED A GAS ALARM IN THE LINE 4 PUMP HOUSE.  SIMULTANEOUSLY, OPERATIONS TECHNICIANS ON SITE HEARD LINE 4 PUMPING EQUIPMENT SHUT DOWN AND WENT TO INVESTIGATE. WARNING BEACONS WERE FOUND TO BE ACTIVE OUTSIDE OF THE PUMP HOUSE AND CRUDE OIL WAS DISCOVERED ON THE CONCRETE FLOOR.  OPERATIONS CONFIRMED WITH THE CONTROL CENTER THAT THERE WAS AN ACTIVE RELEASE, AND THE STATION WAS ISOLATED.  THE SOURCE OF THE RELEASE WAS IDENTIFIED AS AN INBOARD AND OUTBOARD SEAL FAILURE ON UNIT 3.  ADDITIONAL RESOURCES ARRIVED ON SITE FOR CLEANUP AND REPAIRS. AN ATMOSPHERIC MONITOR WAS ALSO PLACED INTO THE PIPE AND CONFIRMED ZERO LEL. DURING TORCH CUTTING OF THE PIPE, THE TORCH CAME INTO CONTACT WITH A SMALL AMOUNT OF DIESEL IN THE PIPELINE AT THE 6 O'CLOCK POSITION AND A FLAME IGNITED. THE FLAME WAS EXTINGUISHED WITH A FIRE EXTINGUISHER. A SUPPLEMENTAL REPORT WILL BE FILED UPON COMPLETION OF THE ACCIDENT INVESTIGATION.     SUPPLEMENTAL UPDATE:   THE ACCIDENT INVESTIGATION REVEALED A SMALL AMOUNT OF PRODUCT WAS LIKELY DAMMED BEHIND SOME SEDIMENT UPSTREAM OF THE CUTTING LOCATION. THE NITROGEN PURGING PROCESS AS WELL AS THE ENERGY ISOLATION PROCESS PROCEDURES WERE UPDATED TO INCLUDE VISUAL INSPECTION AND OR SWABBING OF THE PIPE IN THE PROXIMITY OF WHERE TORCH CUTTING WILL TAKE PLACE. MPL BELIEVES THESE STEPS WILL HELP MITIGATE THE RISK OF RE-OCCURRENCE.

ON JANUARY 23, 2024, AT 13:00 FLINT HILLS RESOURCES (FHR) RECEIVED A CALL FROM THE RECEIVING FACILITY'S PERSONNEL INDICATING A RELEASE OF PRODUCT FROM A DRAIN LINE VALVE AT OUR SOUTHLAKE DELIVERY STATION. AT 13:03 AN FHR OPERATOR NOTIFIED THE PIPELINE CONTROL CENTER (PCC) OF THE REPORTED RELEASE. THE PCC SHUTDOWN THE PUMPS AND BEGAN CLOSING UPSTREAM AND DOWNSTREAM VALVES. AT 13:05 AN FHR QUALIFIED INDIVIDUAL WAS NOTIFIED AND AN OSRO WAS CONTACTED AT 13:10. AN FHR OPERATOR ARRIVED ON-SITE AT 13:20 AND CONFIRMED A RELEASE FROM 1/2 INCH TUBING ON A 2-INCH TWIN SEAL VALVE LOCATED ON A DRAIN LINE ON THE PROVER. PRODUCT WAS OBSERVED ON RAINWATER AND THAT PRODUCT HAD MIGRATED OFF SITE TO AN UNNAMED DRAINAGE DITCH DUE TO LEAK IN CONTAINMENT DRAIN/WALL. THE ONSITE FHR OPERATOR BEGAN EFFORTS TO CONTAIN THE PRODUCT BY DEPLOYING ABSORBENT BOOMS AND PADS IN THE SECONDARY CONTAINMENT AND THE DRAINAGE DITCH LEAVING THE STATION. THE DRAIN LINE VALVE WAS REPAIRED ON JANUARY 23, 2024. THE CONTAINMENT VALVE AND DIKE WALL WERE ALSO REPAIRED, AND THE LINE WAS RESTARTED ON JANUARY 25, 2024. CLEANUP OF SOIL AND SURFACE WATER IMPACTS CONTINUED AND WERE COMPLETED ON JANUARY 31, 2024. LEAK DETECTION DATA INDICATED THAT THE RELEASE OCCURRED DURING TWO DELIVERIES; ONE BEGINNING ON JANUARY 22, 2024, AT 00:58 AND THE SECOND ON JANUARY 23, 2024, BEGINNING AT 09:20.     AN NRC REPORT WAS MADE 14:34 (# 1389726). AN UPDATE TO THE NRC REPORT WAS MADE AT 18:53 (# 1389749) TO REFLECT PRODUCT WAS A MIX OF GASOLINE AND DIESEL.    FHR'S INVESTIGATION DETERMINED THAT THE ROOT CAUSE OF THE RELEASE WAS DETERMINED TO BE MANUFACTURING DEFECT DUE TO INCORRECT ASSEMBLY OF THE VALVE TUBING. IT WAS IDENTIFIED THAT THE TUBING WAS NOT FULLY INSERTED INTO THE FITTING DURING INITIAL MAKEUP, NOT ALLOWING THE FERRULE TO SECURE THE TUBING IN THE FITTING.  THE VALVE AND TUBING WERE PRESSURE TESTED BY THE MANUFACTURER PRIOR TO INSTALLATION AT THE SITE ON FEBRUARY 15, 2023.

ON JANUARY 8, 2024, AT 12:17 LOCAL TIME, A COLONIAL EMPLOYEE WAS PERFORMING A ROUTINE STATION CHECK AT THE ST. IVES BOOSTER STATION IN ALPINE, ALABAMA. THE EMPLOYEE OBSERVED PRODUCT STAINING ON THE GROUND AROUND THE LINE 2 UNIT 3 PUMP INSIDE THE FACILITY. UPON FURTHER INVESTIGATION, THE EMPLOYEE IDENTIFIED AN ACTIVE LEAK FROM A PINHOLE IN TUBING ASSOCIATED WITH THE UNIT.     AN INCIDENT ANALYSIS DETERMINED THAT THE CAUSE OF THE LEAK WAS EQUIPMENT FAILURE. THE 1/2-INCH DIAMETER STAINLESS STEEL TUBING REMAINED IN CONTACT WITH A STEEL SUPPORT FOR AN INDETERMINATE PERIOD OF TIME CAUSING A WEAR GROOVE IN THE SUPPORT RESULTING IN A PINHOLE LEAK IN THE TUBING.

SUPPLEMENTAL INCLUDES PART G TO INCLUDE A NEW SUB-CASE FROM ROOT CAUSE INVESTIGATION, AND PART H UPDATED TO INCLUDE THE INVESTIGATION FINDINGS.    ON JANUARY 6, 2024, FLINT HILLS RESOURCES OPERATIONS PERSONNEL NOTICED AN ODOR WHILE PERFORMING NIGHTLY ROUNDS AND SHORTLY THEREAFTER, HEARD FLOWING LIQUID. AT THAT TIME, THEY NOTIFIED THE PIPELINE CONTROL CENTER TO SHUT DOWN ALL INBOUND AND OUTBOUND PIPELINES. AT 21:23, PERSONNEL VISUALLY CONFIRMED PRODUCT BEING RELEASED FROM THE ROOF DRAIN ON TANK 28075. FLINT HILLS RESOURCES MADE NOTIFICATION TO TEXAS RAILROAD COMMISSION OFFICE OF PIPELINE SAFETY AT 22:15. REFINERY TERMINAL FIRE COMPANY WAS NOTIFIED AND ARRIVED ONSITE AT 22:00. FOAM WAS APPLIED TO THE AREA TO SUPPRESS VAPORS. ONCE AIR MONITORING READINGS INDICATED IT WAS SAFE FOR PERSONNEL TO ENTER THE AREA, THE MANUAL ROOF DRAIN VALVE WAS CLOSED AT 23:48. AFTER THE ROOF DRAIN WAS ISOLATED, FLINT HILLS RESOURCES BEGAN CLEAN-UP OF FREE LIQUID, FOLLOWED BY SOIL RECOVERY. FREE PRODUCT RECOVERY FROM THE TANK CONTAINMENT AREA WAS COMPLETE JANUARY 12. TANK DEGASSING FOR TANK INSPECTION WAS COMPLETE JANUARY 19.     FHR'S INVESTIGATION REVEALED THAT THE ROOT CAUSE WAS THAT THE ROLLING LADDER TRACK WAS NOT DESIGNED TO ACCOMMODATE THE TANK'S LOW LEG SETTINGS, WHICH AT THE TIME OF THE INCIDENT WAS AT THE TANK'S LOWEST LEG SETTING SINCE THE TANK WAS LAST OUT OF SERVICE (2016/2017). THE TANK INSPECTION REPORT STATED THAT AN EXTENSION TO THE ROLLING LADDER TRACK WAS ADDED TO THE END OF THE TRACK AND A NEW STOP ANGLE IRON STOP WAS INSTALLED. HOWEVER, BASED ON THE EVENTS THAT OCCURRED ON JANUARY 6TH AND FIELD OBSERVATIONS MADE BY THE INVESTIGATION TEAM, THAT MODIFICATION TO EXTEND THE TRACK WAS NOT INSTALLED. AT LOW LEVEL, THE LADDER HAD DISENGAGED FROM THE LADDER RUNWAY. WHEN A PIPELINE RECEIPT WAS INITIATED INTO THE TANK, THE ROOF STARTED RISING AND THE LADDER DID NOT REENGAGE PROPERLY WITH THE RUNWAY. UPON FILLING THE TANK, THE BUOYANT FORCES OF THE CRUDE OIL UNDERNEATH, PUT THE LADDER UNDER STRESS AND THEN ALLOWED THE WHEELS TO SHEER FROM THE AXLE CAUSING THE LADDER TO "JOLT" FORWARD AND PUNCTURE THE ROOF. AS THE PRODUCT LEVEL CONTINUED TO RISE, PRODUCT FLOWED UP THROUGH THE PUNCTURE AND TO THE ROOF DRAIN. THE DRAIN HAD BEEN OPENED PRIOR TO THE TANK RECEIPT TO ACCOMMODATE RAINFALL DURING THE DAYS LEADING UP TO THE EVENT. THIS ALLOWED PRODUCT TO FLOW INTO THE TANK'S SECONDARY CONTAINMENT DIKE WHERE IT WAS FULLY CONTAINED.

ON JANUARY 3, 2024, AT 11:09 CST, THE EDMONTON CONTROL CENTER RECEIVED A GAS ALARM IN THE LINE 59 SAMPLE BUILDING AT FLANAGAN TERMINAL.  AT APPROXIMATELY 11:12 CST FIELD PERSONNEL CONFIRMED A RELEASE CONTAINED WITHIN THE SAMPLE BUILDING AND LINE 59 WAS SHUT DOWN.  THE SOURCE OF THE RELEASE WAS IDENTIFIED AS A CRACK IN THE CELL SAMPLER THAT SPRAYED APPROXIMATELY 20 GALLONS OF CRUDE OIL ONTO THE INTERIOR WALLS.  CLEAN-UP ACTIVITIES WERE STARTED AND PERMISSION TO RESTART LINE 59 WITHOUT THE SAMPLE BUILDING WAS GIVEN TO THE CONTROL CENTER.  THE SAMPLER WAS REPLACED, CLEAN-UP WAS COMPLETED, AND CLEAN-UP MATERIAL WAS PROPERLY DISPOSED. THE CAUSE OF THE RELEASE WAS IDENTIFIED AS FRACTURED HOUSING ON THE SAMPLER DUE TO FATIGUE. THE FATIGUE CRACKING HAD INITIATED AND PROPAGATED FROM SURFACE CRACKS IN THE COATING AS A RESULT OF SERVICE-RELATED STRESSES, PROGRESSIVELY REDUCING THE EFFECTIVE CROSS-SECTION OF THE HOUSING UNTIL THE LOADING EXCEEDED THE LOAD CAPACITY OF THE CRACKED HOUSING, RESULTING IN OVERLOAD FAILURE OF THE HOUSING.

ON 12/27/2023 AT 09:30, AN OPERATOR EMPLOYEE FOUND A SMALL STREAM OF OIL COMING OUT OF ROOF DRAIN WHILE DOING MORNING WALK AROUNDS. THE EMPLOYEE IMMEDIATELY CLOSED THE ROOF DRAIN.     APPROXIMATELY 38 GALLONS OF CRUDE OIL WAS RELEASED ON THE GROUND. CONTAMINATED SOIL WAS REMOVED FOR ONSITE REMEDIATION.    SAFE GUARDS IN PLACE ON THE ROOF DRAIN SYSTEM, WHICH ALLOW THE TANK TO REMAIN IN SERVICE AND OPERATE SAFELY.     THE CAUSE OF THE ACCIDENT IS PENDING INVESTIGATION.     SUPPLEMENTAL & FINAL:  THE TANK WAS TAKEN OUT OF SERVICE, CLEANED AND AN API 653 OOS INSPECTION COMPLETED. A PINHOLE WAS FOUND IN THE ROOF DRAIN HOSE WHILE THE TANK INSPECTION CREW WAS FLUSHING DRAIN HOSE.    THE ROOF DRAIN LINE IS CONSTRUCTED WITH A FLEXIBLE EXTERNAL STAINLESS STEEL JACKET OVER A POLYMER INTERNAL SHEATH.  THE CAUSE OF THE ACCIDENT WAS POTENTIALLY DUE TO MECHANICAL DAMAGE OF THE ROOF DRAIN LINE.    TANK 2523 REMAINS OUT OF SERVICE WITH NO PLANS TO BE REPAIRED AND PLACED BACK IN SERVICE.  SHOULD THE TANK BE SCHEDULED FOR REPAIRS AND A RETURN TO SERVICE THE FAILED ROOF DRAIN HOSE WILL BE REPLACED.

ON 12/18/23 AT APPROXIMATELY 11:00, LANDOWNER REPORTED A LEAK IN HIS PASTURE. THE CONTROL CENTER SHUTDOWN THE LINE AND OPERATIONS CONFIRMED LEAK ON THE 10-INCH CRAWFORD LINE.     APPROXIMATELY 2 BARRELS OF CRUDE OIL WAS RELEASED. ALL PRODUCT WAS CLEANED UP AND CONTAMINATED SOIL REMOVED.    AT APPROXIMATELY 18:00, THE LINE WAS REPAIRED WITH 10-INCH PLIDCO CLAMP AND THE LINE WAS RESTARTED AT 18:30.     THE CAUSE OF THE ACCIDENT WAS DETERMINED TO BE INTERNAL CORROSION AT THE 6 O'CLOCK POSITION ON THE PIPE.    TO PREVENT REOCCURRENCE, OPERATIONS IS WORKING ON A CHEMICAL INJECTION. ALSO, AN ILI TOOL RUN IS PLANNED FOR THIS MONTH AND AN ADDITIONAL COUPON WAS ADDED AT THE CRAWFORD RECEIVER.     SUPPLEMENTAL REPORT:  FURTHER INVESTIGATION INTO THE CAUSE OF THE FAILURE AND METALLURGICAL ANALYSIS DETERMINED THE ROOT CAUSE OF THE INTERNAL CORROSION WAS MICROBIAL INDUCED.

ON 12/15/23 AT APPROXIMATELY 05:15, LOCAL FIELD PIPELINE OPERATIONS PERSONNEL NOTIFIED THE CONTROL CENTER AND OPERATIONS MANAGEMENT OF A POTENTIAL RELEASE INSIDE THE COLORADO CITY STATION. THE PE2 LINE WAS IMMEDIATELY SHUT DOWN, BLOCKED IN AND ISOLATED. THE LEAK WAS DETERMINED TO BE COMING FROM 20-INCH STATION PIPING.     APPROXIMATELY 181 BARRELS OF CRUDE OIL WAS RELEASED. THE CRUDE OIL MIGRATED OFFSITE AND IMPACTED NEARBY SULPHUR CREEK AND A PRIVATE LIVESTOCK POND. OSROS REMOVED FREE PRODUCT AND CONTAMINATED SOIL.    THE PIPE WAS DETERMINED TO BE DEAD LEG SUCTION LINE PIPING ASSOCIATED WITH MAINLINE PUMPS THAT HAD BEEN REMOVED PREVIOUSLY.  THE FAILED PIPING WAS REMOVED AND THE MAINLINE RESTARTED ON 12/16/2023.     THE FAILED PIPING WAS SENT TO 3RD PARTY LABORATORY FOR ANALYSIS. A SUPPLEMENTAL REPORT WILL BE SUBMITTED ONCE THE INVESTIGATION IS COMPLETE.    SUPPLEMENTAL REPORT:  RESULTS FROM THE THIRD PARTY ANALYSIS DETERMINED THE FAILURE WAS AT THE 6:00 O'CLOCK POSITION AND WAS CAUSED BY INTERNAL CORROSION WITH PIT IN PIT MORPHOLOGY CHARACTERISTIC OF MICROBIAL INDUCED INTERNAL CORROSION.  CORROSION DEPOSIT ANALYSIS ALSO SUPPORTED A MICROBIAL INDUCED INTERNAL CORROSION CAUSE.    TO PREVENT REOCCURRENCE, OPERATIONS IS INCREMENTALLY REMOVING DEAD-LEG FACILITY PIPING, INTERMITTENTLY FLUSHING LOW FLOW FACILITY PIPING LINES TO PREVENT CORROSION PITTING AND ENHANCING THE CHEMICAL TREATMENT PROGRAM.

ON 12/01/2023 AT 15:00, A LOCAL OPERATOR WAS PERFORMING A ROUTINE MONTHLY TANK INSPECTION ON TANK 2725 AT THE CORSICANA TANK FARM AND OBSERVED A SMALL OIL RESIDUE AROUND THE ROOF DRAIN DISCHARGE VALVE AND PRODUCT ON THE GROUND WHERE THE DRAIN VALVE DISCHARGES FROM THE TANK.     APPROXIMATELY, 30 GALLONS OF CRUDE OIL WAS RELEASED ON THE GROUND. FREE PRODUCT WAS RECOVERED WITH A VACUUM TRUCK. CONTAMINATED SOIL WAS REMOVED FOR ONSITE REMEDIATION.    SUPPLEMENTAL:  THE FAILURE WAS DETERMINED TO HAVE BEEN CAUSED BY A FAILURE OF THE EXTERNAL FLOATING ROOF TANK DRAIN HOSE WHICH IS UTILIZED TO DRAIN WATER FROM THE ROOF. THE HOSE IS COMPRISED OF AN EXTERNAL THERMOPLASTIC SHEATH EXTRUDED OVER A SPIRAL WOUND STAINLESS STEEL INTERNAL CARCASS. THE RELEASE OF NGL VAPORS OCCURRED ON THE MORNING OF SEPTEMBER 21, 2023, AS A RESULT OF A PACKING FAILURE ON THE VALVE STEM OF A 24" GATE VALVE ON SCM OPERATIONS, LLC'S (SCM) NGL TRANSMISSION SYSTEM IN REEVES COUNTY, TEXAS.    THE EVENT OCCURRED AFTER SCM'S DOWNSTREAM CUSTOMER (ENTERPRISE) EXPERIENCED A LIGHTNING STRIKE THAT CAUSED THEIR VALVE AT THE RECEIPT SITE TO FAIL CLOSED, WHICH CAUSED SCM'S 24" DELIVERY VALVE TO CLOSE ON HIGH DIFFERENTIAL.  SCM'S LINE PRESSURE REACHED 1,327 PSIG, WHICH IS BELOW THE MAOP OF THE SYSTEM OF 1,480 PSIG.  WHEN ENTERPRISE WAS ABLE TO RESET THEIR SYSTEM, SCM'S DELIVERY VALVE (MOV 0312) WAS THEN OPENED BY SCM'S CONTROL ROOM.  THE VALVE OPENING REQUIRED 4 ITERATIONS OF THE OPEN/CLOSE ACTION OVER THE COURSE OF A 17-MINUTE TIME PERIOD.    WHILE THE VALVE WAS BEING OPENED, ENTERPRISE'S ON-SITE TECHNICIAN HEARD A LOUD POP, OBSERVED A LEAK, AND CONTACTED SCM.  SCM PERSONNEL MOBILIZED TO SITE AND INSTRUCTED THE CONTROL ROOM TO ISOLATE THE LINE SEGMENT BY CLOSING AN ISOLATION VALVE AT THE UPSTREAM VALVE SETTING.  UPON ARRIVAL ON SITE SCM PERSONNEL CONFIRMED DISCOVERY OF A LEAK ON VALVE MOV 0312, AND DETERMINED A BLOWDOWN OF THE LINE WAS NECESSARY TO EFFECTUATE REPAIRS.      THE BLOWDOWN WAS INITIATED,  AND THE PRESSURE WAS DRAWN DOWN BY THE FOLLOWING MORNING. A VALVE REPAIR TEAM INSPECTED THE FAILED VALVE AND DETERMINED A REPLACEMENT WAS NECESSARY.  A REPLACEMENT VALVE WAS INSTALLED, AND THE LINE SEGMENT WAS PLACED BACK INTO SERVICE ON SEPTEMBER 24, 2023.    FOLLOWING THE REMOVAL AND DISASSEMBLY OF THE FAILED VALVE AN INSPECTION REVEALED THE SEAL BETWEEN THE GRAPHITE PACKING AND THE VALVE STEM WAS COMPROMISED DUE TO WEAR ON THE PACKING AND ROUGHNESS OF THE VALVE STEM.  THE LEAK OCCURRED WHEN THE COMPROMISED SEAL WAS BREACHED AFTER THE MULTIPLE CYCLING ATTEMPTS TO OPEN THE VALVE.      DURING THE CYCLE ATTEMPTS THE EXPANDING NGL WOULD HAVE COOLED AN ESTIMATED 0.1 DEG F WITH A DIFFERENTIAL PRESSURE OF 50 PSID.  BASED ON THE ROUGHNESS OF THE STEM, THE REDUCED FRICTION BETWEEN THE STEM AND THE PACKING, RAPID PRESSURIZATION OF THE BODY CAVITY, AND INSUFFICIENT TIME FOR TEMPERATURE TO EQUALIZE, NGL LIKELY MIGRATED INTO THE PACKING GLAND UNTIL THE PIPELINE PRESSURE OF APPROXIMATELY 1,327 PSIG OVERCAME THE ABILITY OF THE PACKING TO MAINTAIN A SEAL.      VALVE STEM ROUGHNESS MAY HAVE BEEN A CONTRIBUTING FACTOR TO THE WEAR ON THE PACKING, SO THE VALVE STEM MATERIAL WAS EVALUATED.  IT WAS IDENTIFIED TO BE AISI 4140, WHICH IS A LOW ALLOY STEEL AND OFTEN SELECTED FOR ITS TOUGHNESS AND HIGH FATIGUE STRENGTH, HOWEVER, IT HAS A HIGHER CARBON CONTENT THAN A182 F6A OR 17-4.  ALTHOUGH AISI 4140 IS WITHIN INDUSTRY STANDARDS, AN UPGRADE ON THE VALVE STEM MATERIAL TO AISI 4140 WITH 3 MILS OF ELECTROLESS NICKEL PLATING (ENP), A182 F6A, OR 17-4 IS A POSSIBLE DESIGN IMPROVEMENT THAT COULD LOWER THE RISK OF A SIMILAR FAILURE.    PLAN TO PREVENT RECURRENCE  REVIEW OF THE ISOLATION VALVES ON SCM'S SYSTEM IDENTIFIED ONE OTHER VALVE WITH A STEM THAT WAS OF SIMILAR MATERIAL.  THE STEM CANNOT BE VISUALLY EXAMINED DURING NORMAL VALVE MAINTENANCE AND INSPECTION, THEREFORE, SCM WILL REPLACE THAT VALVE WITH ONE THAT HAS A STEM WITH IMPROVED METALLURGICAL PROPERTIES.

THE EMPLOYEE IMMEDIATELY BEGAN NOTIFYING SUPERVISORY AND REGULATORY PERSONNEL, WHILE ALSO INITIATING EMERGENCY RESPONSE ACTIVITIES. THE RELIEF LINE WAS ISOLATED AND ROUTED TO A DIFFERENT TANK, AS THE LINE WAS NOT ACTIVE AT THE TIME OF THE RELEASE. THE PRODUCT RELEASE MIGRATED OFF SITE TO A NEARBY DRAINAGE DITCH VIA CULVERT AND WAS CONTAINED BY OPERATOR PERSONNEL BY USE OF AN EARTHEN DAM IN THE DITCH. ALL PRODUCT AND AFFECTED SOIL WERE REMEDIATED/REMOVED VIA VACUUM TRUCK AND/OR ROLL OFF BOX. THE RELEASE WAS DUE TO A HOLE ON THE UNDERGROUND PORTION OF THE PIPING DOWNSTREAM OF THE AIR TO SOIL TRANSITION.     AFTER LABORATORY ANALYSIS, REPORT RECEIVED 11/15/2023, IT WAS DETERMINED THAT THE RELEASE WAS DUE TO INTERNAL CORROSION FROM SLUDGE AND WATER DROP OUT IN THE PRODUCT. THE REMAINDER OF THE LINE WAS INSPECTED, AND NO FURTHER ISSUES WERE FOUND.

ON 7/11/23 AT 04:18 THE CONTROL CENTER RECEIVED AN LEL, SEAL FAILURE AND FIRE SUPPRESSION SYSTEM ALARM FOR PUMP UNIT 2120 AT LONGVIEW STATION.  THE CONTROLLER SHUT THE PUMP DOWN AND NOTIFIED LOCAL OPERATIONS PERSONNEL.  UPON ARRIVAL AT THE STATION, FIELD PERSONNEL OBSERVED A RELEASE OF APPROXIMATELY, 2 GALLONS OF CRUDE OIL INTO SECONDARY CONTAINMENT AND NOTED THAT THE FIRE SUPPRESSION SYSTEM HAD ACTIVATED.  A MIST OF CRUDE OIL HAD IGNITED DUE TO CONTACT WITH ANCILLARY PUMP COMPONENTS THAT WERE HOT.  THE FACILITY DRY CHEMICAL FIRE SUPPRESSION SYSTEM ACTIVATED AND EXTINGUISHED THE FIRE WITH MINIMAL DAMAGE.     AN INVESTIGATION DETERMINED THE RELEASE WAS DUE TO A PUMP SEAL FAILURE.  THE SEAL FAILURE OCCURRED BECAUSE OF COUPLING MISALIGNMENT BETWEEN THE PUMP AND THE PUMP MOTOR WHICH CAUSED VIBRATION.  FURTHER, THE MULTILIN RELAY PROTECTIVE UNIT DID NOT ACTIVATE AND SHUT THE PUMP DOWN DUE TO VIBRATION AUTOMATICALLY AS IS INTENDED.     TO PREVENT REOCCURRENCE, OPERATIONS IS ADDING LOGIC TO SHUT THE PUMP UNITS DOWN WHEN THE MULTILIN LOSES COMMUNICATION AND/OR THE MULTILIN HEALTH CHECK BIT IS FAULTED. AN ENGINEERING ANALYSIS WILL BE CONDUCTED TO DETERMINE THE BEST PIPING MODIFICATIONS TO PREVENT COUPLING MISALIGNMENT ISSUES.  THE PUMP AND MOTOR ARE BEING REPAIRED AND WILL BE REINSTALLED ALONG WITH A NEW MULTILIN RELAY PROTECTIVE UNIT.

ON JUNE 29, 2023, AT APPROXIMATELY 07:47 AM CST, A CENTURION PIPELINE, L.P. (CPL) EMPLOYEE DISCOVERED A LEAK IN CPL'S MIDLAND STATION NEAR MIDLAND, TEXAS. CPL DETERMINED THE SOURCE OF THE LEAK TO BE STATION PIPING AND PROMPTLY ISOLATED THE LEAK. THE PIPELINE SEGMENT HAD BEEN EXCAVATED AND EXPOSED PRIOR TO THE LEAK AND WAS PENDING PIPE REPLACEMENT. ACTUAL PIPE REPLACEMENT HAD NOT COMMENCED. THIRTY-SEVEN (37) BARRELS OF CRUDE OIL WAS RELEASED AND WAS CONTAINED COMPLETELY ON-SITE. THE CONTAMINATED SOIL WILL BE REMEDIATED ON SITE. NO INJURIES, FATALITIES OR FIRES WERE ASSOCIATED WITH THIS INCIDENT.    CPL REPORTED THE LEAK TO THE TEXAS RAILROAD COMMISSION, OFFICE OF PIPELINE SAFETY AT 08:44 AM CST ON JUNE 29, 2023. THE "AFTER-HOURS" OPERATOR NOTED THE INCIDENT AND DID NOT PROVIDE AN INCIDENT NUMBER.    AT THE TIME OF THIS WRITING, THE REPAIR OF THE STATION PIPING IS PENDING AND THE ROOT CAUSE FAILURE ANALYSIS WILL BE CONDUCTED PENDING THE REMOVAL OF THE DAMAGED PIPING SEGMENT. THE RESULTING INFORMATION RELATED TO THE CAUSE OF THE LEAK, PREVENTATIVE AND MITIGATIVE MEASURES (P&M) AND COSTS ASSOCIATED WITH THE REPAIRING THE STATION PIPING WILL BE SUBMITTED VIA SUPPLEMENTAL REPORT(S).    SUPPLEMENTAL REPORT REPORTED ON AUGUST 28, 2023:  DURING THE ROOT CAUSE ANALYSIS, CPL DETERMINES THAT UNDER-DEPOSIT MICROBIOLOGICALLY INFLUENCED CORROSION (MIC) RESULTED IN A THROUGH-WALL INTERNAL CORROSION PIT IN THE 6 O'CLOCK POSITION OF THE MTF ROW 5 DEAD LEG #2 STATION PIPING. THIS STATION PIPING WAS A PREVIOUSLY IDENTIFIED DEAD LEG THAT WAS SCHEDULED TO BE REPLACED. ONCE REPLACED, NO FURTHER ACTIONS WILL BE REQUIRED.

ON JUNE 12, 2023, A COLONIAL EMPLOYEE WAS CONDUCTING NORMAL STATION MAINTENANCE ACTIVITIES AT THE BOLIGEE DELIVERY FACILITY IN BOLIGEE, ALABAMA. THE EMPLOYEE OBSERVED AN AREA OF STAINED GRAVEL. UPON FURTHER INVESTIGATION, THE EMPLOYEE IDENTIFIED A CAP MISSING FROM A TUBING CONNECTION ON THE PRESSURE SWITCH DOWNSTREAM OF THE LINE 449-2 METER RUN CONTROL VALVE, WHICH WAS DETERMINED TO BE THE SOURCE OF THE RELEASE. AN INVESTIGATION IS ON-GOING.    UPDATE: AN ACCIDENT INVESTIGATION DETERMINED THAT THE CAUSE OF THE RELEASE WAS EQUIPMENT FAILURE. THE FAILURE OCCURRED DUE TO EXCESSIVE VIBRATION EXPERIENCED ON THE LINE DURING DELIVERIES. THESE VIBRATIONS CAUSED THE CAP TO LOOSEN OVER TIME, AND ULTIMATELY SEPARATING COMPLETELY. AN ACTION PLAN HAS BEEN DEVELOPED TO ADDRESS THE EXCESSIVE VIBRATIONS EXPERIENCED ON THE LINE AT BOLIGEE DELIVERY DURING NORMAL OPERATIONS.

ON 6/7/23 AT APPROXIMATELY 07:25, AN OPERATOR DISCOVERED A RELEASE OF APPROXIMATELY 8 BARRELS OF CRUDE OIL FROM THE PIG TRAP TUBING ONTO THE GROUND SURROUNDING THE ST. MARTINVILLE PUMP STATION SCRAPER TRAP. THE TRAP WAS ISOLATED AND CLEANUP CONTRACTORS WERE DISPATCHED TO REMOVE FREE PRODUCT AND CONTAMINATED SOIL AND ROCKS.     ON 6/12/23, IT WAS DETERMINED THAT TOTAL COSTS WOULD EXCEED $50K DUE TO ENVIRONMENTAL REMEDIATION COSTS EXCEEDING THOSE WHICH WERE INITIALLY ANTICIPATED FOR A RELEASE OF THIS SIZE.  IMMEDIATELY FOLLOWING DETERMINATION THAT TOTAL COSTS WOULD EXCEED $50K THE NRC AND PHMSA AID WERE NOTIFIED.    OPERATIONS ASSESSED THE SCRAPER TRAP AND THE INVESTIGATION DETERMINED THE RELEASE WAS CAUSED BY A TUBING FAILURE DUE TO IMPROPER TIGHTENING OF A SWAGELOK FITTING WHEN INSTALLED DURING CONSTRUCTION.  DUE TO THE FITTING NOT BEING PROPERLY TIGHTENED ACCORDING TO THE MANUFACTURERS PROCEDURE IT PREVENTED THE FERRULE FROM PROPERLY CRIMPING THE STAINLESS STEEL TUBING RESULTING IN THE TUBING COMING OUT OF THE FITTING AND CAUSING THE RELEASE.    REPAIRED THE FAILURE BY REINSTALLING THE TUBING TO MANUFACTURERS SPECIFICATION.     TO PREVENT REOCCURRENCE, OPERATIONS ASSESSED ALL OTHER TUBING FITTINGS ON THE SYSTEM USING SWAGELOK PROCEDURE AND GAUGE TO CHECK FITTINGS FOR PROPER TIGHTNESS.

ON 4/25 @ 10:06, AIR PATROL REPORTED A SHEEN ON THE WATER. MULTIPLE TECHNICIANS FROM VARIOUS PIPELINE COMPANIES WERE DISPATCHED TO INVESTIGATE THE SHEEN. AT THAT POINT, ABSORBENT BOOM WAS DEPLOYED AND RECOVERY EFFORTS WERE UNDERWAY. WHEN THE PIPE WAS EXPOSED, ROCKS WERE FOUND OVER AND AROUND THE RELEASE SITE. A ROOT CAUSE ANALYSIS WILL BE CONDUCTED AND THIS REPORT WILL BE UPDATED WITH ANY FINDINGS.    ** A ROOT CAUSE AND THOROUGH INVESTIGATION PROVED INCONCLUSIVE AS TO HOW THE RIP RAP MIGRATED TO THE AREA OF THE PIPELINE DAMAGE.     *** THIS SERVES AS THE CORRECTED UPDATE TO THE FINAL REPORT. IT SHOULD'VE BEEN 7/18/2023 AND I PUT 7/18/2024. THIS IS TO CORRECT THE TYPO.

CRIMSON DISPATCHED FILED PERSONAL TO THE LOCATION.  UPON ARRIVAL KINDER MORGAN AND MARATHON AND THEIR EMERGENCY PERSONAL WERE ON SITE RESPONDING.  CRIMSON CONFIRMED THE RELEASE WAS FROM AN OOS CRIMSON PIPELINE OSFM #0414.  CRIMSON CONFIRMED ISOLATION AND SECURED THE RELEASE LOCATION.  THE RELEASE WAS CONTAINED AND CRIMSON COORDINATED CLEANUP AND REPAIR.    SUPLEMENTAL   MEETING WITH CRIMSON PIPELINE CATHODIC PROTECTION PERSONNEL AND INTEGRITY MANAGEMENT PERSONNEL THE INVESTIGATION FOUND THE PIN HOLE LEAK WAS CAUSED BY EXTERNAL CORROSION AROUND THE TRANSITION AREA AT THE SOIL TO AIR INTERFACE. NUSTAR OPERATIONS PERSONNEL DISCOVERED A LEAK INSIDE NUSTAR'S WICHITA FALLS TERMINAL FACILITY.  THE LEAK ORIGINATED FROM A 6-INCH RELIEF LINE PIPE SEGMENT BETWEEN THE PIPELINE RECEIVER TRAP AND THE TANK MANIFOLD INSIDE THE TERMINAL.  THE LEAK WAS ISOLATED USING VALVES INSIDE THE TERMINAL FACILITY, AND A SEGMENT OF PIPE CONTAINING THE FAILURE HAS BEEN REMOVED FOR ANALYSIS TO DETERMINE THE CAUSE OF THE RELEASE.  UPDATE - THE FAILURE WAS THE RESULT OF UNDER DEPOSIT CORROSION CAUSED BY A SEQUENTIAL PROCESS OF EVENTS THAT CAUSED CONTINUAL LOCALIZED CORROSION AND WALL-LOSS OVER TIME, LEADING TO EVENTUAL FAILURE.  THE PROCESSES WERE INTERNAL AND STRONGLY DRIVEN BY THE PRESENCE OF SULFIDES AND CHLORIDES IN THE CRUDE, WHICH LED TO THE CORROSION OF THE IRON FROM THE WALL SECTION.  THE ATTACK WAS ALSO DRIVEN BY EROSION CORROSION FROM INTERMITTENT FLOW THROUGH THE LINE WHICH REMOVED LOOSELY ADHERENT CORROSION PRODUCTS FROM THE WALL INTERIOR SURFACE TO ALLOW FOR CONTINUED CORROSION ATTACK AND LOSS OF WALL THICKNESS.

5/12/2023 ORIGINAL NARRATIVE    ON APRIL 13, 2023, OPERATOR PERSONNEL WERE OPENING VAULTS CONTAINING VALVES AHEAD OF BI-ANNUAL VALVE MAINTENANCE. WHEN THE VAULT FOR MOV-613 AT THE GUERNSEY NORTH TERMINAL WAS OPENED, CRUDE OIL WAS OBSERVED. THE FACILITY WAS IN A PAUSE BETWEEN BATCHES AND MOV-613 WAS ISOLATED TO CONTAIN THE LEAK.     AFTER THE VAULT WAS CLEANED AND CLEARED FOR ENTRY, THE ANSI 150 FLANGE WAS FOUND TO HAVE FAILED AT THE AT THE 8:00 O'CLOCK POSITION ON DOWNSTREAM SIDE OF THE VALVE IN RELATION TO FLOW. NO DAMAGE WAS FOUND ON THE ISOLATION GASKET THAT WOULD INDICATE A FAILURE. AN INVESTIGATION IS STILL UNDERWAY TO DETERMINE APPARENT CAUSE AND A SUPPLEMENTAL REPORT WILL BE SUBMITTED ONCE THE INVESTIGATION IS COMPLETE. UNTIL TALLGRASS CONCLUDES ITS INVESTIGATION, IT HAS IMPLEMENTED CERTAIN INTERIM MEASURES INCLUDING OPENING THE VAULTS AT THE TERMINAL AND VISUALLY INSPECTING THEM WITH INCREASED FREQUENCY.    THE CRUDE OIL RELEASE WAS CONFINED COMPLETELY TO THE VAULT CONTAINING MOV-613. THERE IS NO IMPACT TO THE TERMINAL OUTSIDE OF THE CONCRETE VAULT.    ANOTHER VALVE IN THE TERMINAL, INSTALLED IN A SIMILAR FASHION AS MOV-613, WAS INSPECTED AS A PREVENTATIVE MEASURE. TALLGRASS WILL ALSO IMPLEMENT THE INTERIM MEASURES DISCUSSED ABOVE AT THE OTHER VALVE VAULT ON THE TERMINAL.    5/16/2024 UPDATE  PART G APPARENT CAUSE UPDATED TO G7 INCORRECT OPERATION    THE INVESTIGATION DETERMINED THAT THE FLANGE WAS NOT PROPERLY TORQUED WHICH RESULTED IN AN IMPROPER GASKET SEAL CAUSING PRODUCT TO BE RELEASED INTO THE FULLY CONTAINED CONCRETE VAULT. THE UNEVEN TORQUE PLACED UPON THE FLANGE CAUSED AN UNEVEN LOADING OF THE FLANGE FACE. ONCE THE FLANGE BOLTS WERE TIGHTENED TO 600 FT/LBS UTILISING A PROPER TORQUE SEQUENCE THE RELEASE TERMINATED. THE GASKET WAS REPLACED AT THE TIME OF THE EVENT. TALLGRASS HAS DEVELOPED SITE-SPECIFIC PROCEDURE TO INCLUDE PERIODIC INSPECTIONS OF THE VALVES IN VAULTS ON A WEEKLY BASIS.

ON MARCH 28, 2023 AT APPROXIMATELY 08:52, DURING A STATION CHECK THE OPERATOR DISCOVERED A RELEASE COMING FROM THE TANK 2598 MIXER AREA. APPROXIMATELY 1094 BARRELS OF CRUDE OIL WAS RELEASED TO CONTAINMENT AND APPROXIMATELY 25 BARRELS OF THE TOTAL VOLUME MIGRATED OFF OPERATOR PROPERTY AND REACHED MESQUITE BRANCH CREEK. THE TANK IMPOUNDMENT DIKE DRAIN VALVE WAS IN THE CLOSED POSITION. HOWEVER, DUE TO DEBRIS IN THE VALVE BODY THE VALVE WAS NOT FULLY SEATED WHICH ALLOWED PRODUCT TO LEAK BY.      BOOM WAS PLACED IN THE CREEK TO PREVENT FURTHER MIGRATION AND OSROS WERE DISPATCHED TO COLLECT FREE PRODUCT. CONTAMINATED SOIL FROM THE IMPOUNDMENT DIKE WAS REMOVED AND CLEAN FILL WAS BROUGHT IN.    AN INVESTIGATION DETERMINED THE MIXER SEAL FAILED DUE TO A MIXER BEARING FAILURE.    THE FAILED SEAL AND TANK MIXER WILL BE REPLACED AND THE ORIGINAL MIXER WILL BE SENT TO THE MANUFACTURER (PHILADELPHIA) FOR FAILURE ANALYSIS AND REBUILD. ADDITIONAL PREVENTATIVE MEASURES ARE EXPECTED TO BE DETERMINED FOR THIS MODEL OF MIXER POST ANALYSIS.      SUPPLEMENTAL REPORT WILL BE FILED AFTER ANALYSIS IS COMPLETE.    SUPPLEMENTAL & FINAL REPORT:  UPDATED TOTAL COSTS AND CHANGED FUNCTION OF PIPELINE SYSTEM TO >20% SMYS REGULATED TRANSMISSION.  A REPLACEMENT TANK MIXER WAS INSTALLED AND THE FAILED UNIT IS BEING RECONDITIONED. A REPRESENTATIVE FROM THE MIXER MANUFACTURER MADE A SITE VISIT TO EXAMINE THE FAILED MIXER AND CONFIRMED THE CAUSE OF THE FAILURE WAS A MIXER SEAL FAILURE DUE TO A BEARING FAILURE ON THE MIXER WHICH ALLOWED THE SHAFT TO DROP  LEADING TO THE SEAL FAILURE.
